## Agent claims and parallel branches

Read [repository rules](../AGENTS.md), [project context](../PROJECT.md), this task's
source rows and [module ownership](module-boundaries.md). For source discovery use
CodeGraph first when indexed. The active coordinator owns task selection and
integration; one implementer owns each task at a time. Agents do not silently
reassign others' tasks or treat a branch name as proof of ownership.

### Claim and state protocol

1. Re-read current `main`, task and shared-interface decisions. Confirm required
   inputs are linked and adequate, not just checked boxes. If a PR already owns the
   change, attach/continue it through the supported session workflow rather than
   create a duplicate. Preserve unrelated work.
2. Atomically agree the claim through the active coordinator/tracker before
   editing. The coordinator records one compact row below (or a linked issue/PR
   as the single live owner). A stale copy of this document is not a lock.
3. Claim includes task, agent/session, base SHA, owned paths, branch, shared
   interface assumptions, acceptance/evidence owner and current next action.
   Record exact source paths only after inspection. No overlapping mutations
   without the interface/integration owner explicitly coordinating the split.
4. Create one task branch in the session namespace from the accepted base; use
   its registered isolated worktree where needed. A stack uses its real parent
   branch and verified head, with a stated merge order. Do not keep all work on
   one long-lived feature branch or add another worktree without ownership notes.
5. Keep the PR limited to the task and any inseparable contract/selector/docs.
   Update progress and blocker/review/CI state. Push fixes for the same task to
   the same PR, resolve addressed review threads and revalidate current source.
6. Integrator rechecks required current-head CI and reviews, then squash-merges
   under [merge policy](../specifications/git_standards.md). Rebase/merge dependent
   work deliberately; no force-push without authorization. Capture delivered
   acceptance or named limits, release the claim and clean only task-owned
   branches/worktrees under repository preservation rules.

States: `Unclaimed -> Claimed -> Investigating -> Ready for design/implementation
-> Implementing -> In review -> Validated -> Merged`. Use `Needs decision` or
`Needs evidence` with owner/next action when blocked, and `Deferred`/`Retained`
with reason/revisit conditions for no-go results. A merged research PR completes
its evidence task, not a downstream implementation or a release guarantee.

| Task     | Claimant / session | Branch / base | Owned paths / shared interfaces | State / next action                             | Issue / PR / evidence |
| -------- | ------------------ | ------------- | ------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------- | --------------------- |
| None yet | Unassigned         | Not created   | Not assigned                    | Planning document only; no product task claimed | No product PR         |

Suggested lanes, subject to actual path/resource review:

| Lane                      | Initial eligible work                                | Conflict boundary                                                                                                                                |
| ------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Coordinator / domain      | T001, then T002/T008/T009                            | One owner coordinates glossary, authority and shared-interface decisions; do not funnel every tiny fix through an all-app redesign.              |
| Runtime performance       | T003/T004, then independent measured P1 slices       | Coordinate shared stores, session lifecycle and native measurement resources; reserve production-like profiling to avoid concurrent build noise. |
| Validation engineering    | T005/T006, then T010/T038                            | One owner for selection, runner and required-check policy; reuse tests and maintain current protections.                                         |
| Privacy and user controls | T007, then T030/T031/T032                            | Identity/crypto/wire decisions require the core contract owner; separate endorsement research.                                                   |
| Independent UI features   | T039 after T001; later review/voice/PWA ready slices | Do not concurrently edit shared chat/store/IPC contracts without a designated integration owner.                                                 |
| Platform research         | T034/T047 when inputs ready; T035/T069 later         | Research output alone does not claim core files or authorize branch extraction/migration.                                                        |

Start with a small number of nonconflicting tasks; expand only when review and
runner/native capacity permit. Do not invent a universal agent count or start
parallel workers merely because a roadmap row exists. Workers register meaningful
progress, evidence and blockers with the active project coordinator. This roadmap
supports parallel delivery; it does not automatically dispatch agents.

## Requirements-to-release document flow

Use the existing documentation owners. Requirements explain desired outcomes;
architecture explains contracts; implementation plans explain the next bounded
change; tests/evals provide evidence; ADRs preserve important trade-offs. A giant
permanent implementation diary is not the source of truth.

| Step                            | Deliverable / owner                                     | Entry and exit                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| ------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 1. Requirement                  | This roadmap, stable REQ/WORK/T links and product owner | Observable user scenario, constraints, explicit unknowns and non-goals; preserve the original confirmed scope.                                                                                                  |
| 2. Evidence / triage            | Existing owning guide plus linked PR/CI evidence        | Inspect implementation/callers and actual conditions; quantify when relevant, label uncertainty; select retain/fix/feature/experiment rather than assume a defect.                                              |
| 3. Feature contract / design    | Owning feature/network/storage/privacy guide            | Define authority, state/lifetimes, errors, permission, failure/recovery and budget; compare alternatives. Use a short design for a small feature, a substantial design for protocol/migration/platform changes. |
| 4. Important choice             | Existing topic rationale or linked ADR                  | Record why, alternatives, consequences/status and reconsideration triggers. Do not require an RFC/ADR for every small edit.                                                                                     |
| 5. Implementation slice         | Task PR plus ignored local plan under tmp               | Claim exact paths/interfaces, test selectors and concrete steps. Do not commit scratch plans or duplicate the existing contract. Read performance/reliability rules before edits.                               |
| 6. Change and boundary feedback | Owning tests, validation.json and relevant guide        | Requirement-derived assertions, applicable failure paths, affected static/tests and browser/native evidence; update rule/selector/consumers together when boundaries change.                                    |
| 7. Candidate acceptance         | Current committed PR, reviews and protected checks      | Report tested SHA, command results, gaps and rollback/recovery; required current-head gates before merge. Optional full local preparation is not an automatic per-edit burden.                                  |
| 8. Integration / release        | Existing update and release lifecycle                   | Integrate compatible slices, update backlog/status/help only as warranted, rehearse affected install/restore/upgrade/native behavior; publish only through existing authorized release flow.                    |

### Document owners and entry paths

| Information                                                             | Existing owner / intended destination                                                                                                                         |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Future work, priority, source mapping and claim entry                   | This roadmap; linked from docs/README.md, already reachable through PROJECT.md.                                                                               |
| Implemented capabilities / deliberate limits                            | [Implementation status](../specifications/TODO.md); do not turn it into a competing chronological backlog.                                                    |
| Domain terms and modeling                                               | [CONTEXT.md](../CONTEXT.md), [domain-design.md](domain-design.md).                                                                                            |
| Module authority and parallel interface ownership                       | [module-boundaries.md](module-boundaries.md).                                                                                                                 |
| Protocol, network, storage and crypto                                   | [ARCHITECTURE.md](ARCHITECTURE.md), [network-design-reference.md](network-design-reference.md) and relevant topic guides.                                     |
| Performance and AI reliability                                          | [performance-requirements.md](performance-requirements.md), [ai-coding-reliability.md](ai-coding-reliability.md); extend existing rules with proven patterns. |
| Validation/eval coverage and cost                                       | [testing-feedback-loop.md](testing-feedback-loop.md), [ci-maintenance.md](ci-maintenance.md), owning validation.json, [evaluation inputs](evals/README.md).   |
| Durable significant trade-offs                                          | Existing topic guide; linked ADR only when needed under [DDD conventions](domain-design.md).                                                                  |
| User help and product claims                                            | [Help](help/README.md), relevant feature guide, documentation hub; do not claim roadmap features are shipped.                                                 |
| Temporary plans, raw profiles, research snapshots and generated reports | Ignored task-owned tmp/target or PR/CI artifacts; reusable suites in docs/evals, not run histories.                                                           |

### Validation and definition of done

Use the [existing stages](testing-feedback-loop.md#validation-stages-and-agent-responsibilities)
and current required-check policy. For future code work preview `make test-plan`
or `make verify-plan`; run affected tests while changing and `make verify-changed`
with the necessary browser/native escalation. Run `make standards-check` when
adding/moving source or changing contracts. Run repository hygiene before commit.
Create PRs through `./scripts/create-pr.sh -- <gh pr create options>`; it requires
a clean committed candidate. Do not fabricate receipt/coverage evidence or change
thresholds simply to pass. Exact commands and filters come from the selected
owner and actual diff, not a generic all-suite instruction in this roadmap.

A delivery is done only when the accepted user outcome and failure/recovery paths
are evidenced, resource behavior is compared for the affected startup/idle/active
and return-to-idle phases, relevant compatibility/migration/reversal limits are
explicit, selectors and maintained docs match behavior, and the current head
meets required reviews/checks. Full workspace/native/release gates remain in their
owners; a subset or model score is not universal correctness evidence. All methods
in REQ-030 receive a later applicability decision, not silent removal or blanket
mandatory execution. Optional extensive checks must not recreate REQ-003's delays.

### Reusable task handoff fields

Before a ready task is assigned, put these fields in its issue/PR or task record:

- Stable T/WORK/REQ IDs and concrete outcome/non-goals.
- Owner/agent, base/source SHA, branch, exact paths and shared-interface owner.
- Completed hard inputs and conditional/product decisions with links.
- Authoritative rule, real consumers, lifecycle/authority and resource invariants.
- Selected tests/evals, platform/native scenarios and performance baseline identity.
- Expected completion evidence, review/integration owner and rollback/recovery limits.
- Current state, blocker/decision/evidence owner, next action and claim release path.

An AI starting here should choose only a ready task of the authorized kind, confirm its claim, inspect
owners/callers, resolve missing decisions, implement the bounded slice, validate
and report evidence, then request integration under existing gates. It must not
silently select Raft, replace SQLite/Tauri, rewrite crypto in JS, expose a service,
change retention or publish packages because such an option appears in a row.

### Mature-process references and adaptation

These are narrowly reviewed process sources, not a completed competitor, CI or
framework survey. Accessed during roadmap preparation; current versions can change.
Our adaptation below is a project recommendation, not a claim every mature project
uses identical gates or a reason to copy their schedule/telemetry policies.

- [VS Code development process](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/Development-Process)
  separates high-level roadmap, iteration plans and done criteria, with a testing
  and stabilization period. Apply the separation and evidence-based milestone
  exits, not a mandatory monthly release cadence.
- [VS Code contribution guide](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute)
  emphasizes small issue-linked PRs and discussion of architectural impact. Use
  independently reviewable slices with an explicit owner and tests.
- [VS Code test-plan items](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/Writing-Test-Plan-Items)
  specify tester context/setup, platform and bounded scope. Use reproducible
  native acceptance cases and split oversized test plans.
- [Rust RFC process](https://rust-lang.github.io/rfcs/)
  distinguishes substantial design decisions from ordinary PR changes and records
  alternatives, rationale and postponed work. Use proportional design review and
  significant ADRs; do not impose an RFC ceremony on a small correction.
- [Zed contribution guide](https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
  asks contributors to discuss features first and limits simultaneous open PRs to
  protect review capacity. Use capacity-aware parallel claims and finishable
  slices; do not copy its numeric PR limit as a Mesh Talk policy.

## Open decision register

These decisions are deliberately represented as work, not missing plan content.
The responsible task gathers its listed evidence, presents alternatives and then
records the chosen behavior. A decision blocks its own affected implementation,
not every independent task in the program.

| Decision                                                      | Resolving task(s)   | Owner / closure evidence                                                                                           |
| ------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| First actual bottlenecks and first delivery slice             | T003-T009           | Product/integration owner plus runtime/validation evidence; no assumed root cause.                                 |
| Monitoring defaults/history and user alerts                   | T026/T027           | Product owner chooses after source/overhead options; no always-on costly collection assumed.                       |
| Startup, memory, retention/sync/deletion boundaries           | T014-T019           | Product owner and core/storage owner; define visibility versus durable deletion, safe recovery and reclamation.    |
| Announcement/member offline conflict and confirmation         | T022/T023           | Group/core authority owner and product owner; pending/effective distinction preserved, Raft open.                  |
| Database/stack/UI retain versus replace                       | T034-T036           | Measured workload, parity/cost/license and reviewed migration/rollback; retained current stack is valid.           |

- **Discussion state:** Clarifying; exploratory idea, not a fixed feature specification.
- **Captured / updated:** 2026-11-17 (Asia/Singapore).
- **Original user input:** “第二个需求，应该是功能想法，不一定完全按照以下描述，大概是可以头脑风暴，看看有什么好的局域网工具可以在机遇这个app上开发”。
- **User-supplied inspiration, not independently verified:** “baoyu-design 增加了局域网内的团队共享功能，现在你的设计稿做好了，或者slides写好了，可以在局域网内分享，生成一个内部 IP 地址加端口的 URL（注意防火墙设置），让你的同事、老板也能对你的内容进行编辑、评论，并且实时同步。安全性也不用担心，所有数据都在你本机，你可以控制分享的权限级别：只读、评论、编辑，并且可以随时修改权限设置。deepseek harness 的插件也同步更新了，一样支持这个功能。” These product claims and the security assurance are supplied inspiration only, not verified facts or adopted guarantees.
- **Scenario and affected users:** Colleagues on the LAN open shared content in a browser to view it and leave comments without installing Mesh Talk. Designs and slides remain examples; supported formats are not selected.
- **Pain point or question:** Which LAN collaboration tools would meaningfully complement Mesh Talk? The primary scenario is now confirmed as browser-based viewing and commenting; detailed workflow friction remains to be clarified.
- **Desired outcome:** Let a Mesh Talk user share content with colleagues who can view and comment through a browser without installing the app. Continue clarifying this review workflow while retaining other LAN collaboration ideas for discussion.
- **Confirmed conclusions:**
  - Primary scenario: colleagues need no Mesh Talk installation and use a browser to view and comment on shared content.
  - Multi-user editing remains a direction for later discussion, outside the currently confirmed primary scenario. Native workspaces and external-tool integrations have not been selected.
  - The sharer can configure either link-only access or link plus an access code. Per-person approval is not a primary scenario. No default mode has been chosen.
  - Commenter identity and whether viewing/commenting permissions are separate remain open; do not add an account or per-person approval requirement to the confirmed browser entry flow.
  - Keep this session in requirements collection and clarification; do not begin development.
  - Content formats, detailed permission behavior, transport and update semantics remain undecided. The inspiration need not be implemented literally.
- **Additional original user clarification:** “先以‘同事无需安装 Mesh Talk，通过浏览器查看和评论我分享的内容’为主要场景，多人编辑保留为待讨论方向。请据此更新 REQ-002，继续澄清关键边界，暂不进入开发。”

- **Assistant suggestions / alternatives — unconfirmed, not ranked for global planning:**
  1. **Share and review existing work:** Publish selected designs, slides, HTML or other supported artifacts into a scoped sharing session; distribute an entry in a conversation and potentially a LAN browser URL. Viewing and comments could address review workflows without requiring an in-app authoring suite. Browser-based viewing and commenting is the confirmed primary direction. Content formats, revisions and entry distribution still require clarification; the detailed solution is not approved.
  2. **Native collaborative workspace:** Shared notes, whiteboard or lightweight team task board associated with a conversation. Allows direct joint work, but introduces editing semantics, concurrent changes, persistence and recovery responsibilities. These are candidate tools, not promised capabilities.
  3. **Integration with existing local tools:** Let authorized external tools publish sharing entries or previews through Mesh Talk, keeping authoring in the original tool. Requires deliberate integration, lifecycle and permission boundaries; do not assume an existing API supports this or that Mesh Talk should expose arbitrary local services.
- **Additional candidate use cases — unconfirmed:** Temporary transfer/download space and team review/decision sessions. Avoid committing to a broad toolbox until real scenarios are clear.
- **Design considerations to resolve, not fixed requirements:**
  - Browser participation without installation and sharer-configurable link-only/link-plus-code entry are confirmed. A reachable IP/port alone is not the scoped sharing link; exact link scope and access-code behavior remain to be designed.
  - In link-only mode forwarding the sharing link can pass access onward; in access-code mode the link and code can both be forwarded. Per-person approval is outside the primary scenario. Expiry, code changes, revocation and view/comment permissions still need decisions; no default mode selected.
  - Comment identity may be a self-entered nickname or verified identity; do not imply a nickname proves who submitted a comment. Comment persistence, replies, deletion/moderation and attachment to a page/region/version remain open.
  - Decide which content is shared and how safely it can be presented. An immutable published snapshot and a live local-file view have different update and comment-anchoring behavior. Do not assume arbitrary HTML can run with host/app privileges or that sharing one item exposes a directory.
  - Local storage alone does not establish confidentiality or safe access. Distinguish host storage, recipient/browser copies, authentication, transport protection and enforced read/comment/edit permissions.
  - Specify permission changes and revocation for already-open sessions; stopping future access cannot recall copies already downloaded. Avoid inheriting the quoted unconditional security assurance.
  - Distinguish viewing the latest published revision, live propagation of host edits, live comments and true simultaneous editing. They have different acceptance boundaries; “real time” alone does not specify which is wanted.
  - Clarify host sleep/exit, network changes, firewall reachability, reconnection and persistence. Host availability and copies on other devices need explicit behavior rather than an assumed always-available service.
  - Prefer reuse of existing identity, conversation, discovery, transport and file capabilities where suitable, subject to later owner/code inspection. This is an architectural proposal, not a verified reuse claim.
  - Keep optional sharing work demand-driven and consider resource budgets, consistent with the user's low-resource product goal. Do not introduce a permanent background service merely from this brainstorming discussion.
- **Content and comment options for clarification — not selected:**
  - Content families: static images/design exports; PDF documents or slide exports; Markdown/text; HTML pages or slide bundles with referenced assets. Original editable office/design files could instead be download attachments; inline preview/conversion is not assumed.
  - Distinguish one file from a multi-file page/bundle and a single artifact from a multi-item sharing session. No arbitrary directory exposure is implied.

# AI coding reliability guide

Use this guide before implementing or reviewing a change, especially a bug fix,
refactor, merge resolution or optimization. Its purpose is to turn recurring
failure modes into concrete design questions and executable checks. Compiling,
adding a timeout or passing a happy-path test does not establish reliability.

This guide owns the cross-cutting review method and reusable failure patterns.
[Module ownership](module-boundaries.md) owns implementation boundaries;
[architecture](ARCHITECTURE.md), [network contracts](network-design-reference.md)
and feature guides own behavior and resource limits. The
[testing workflow](testing-feedback-loop.md) owns commands, selection and gates.
Link to those owners instead of copying their changing contracts here. When code
and a contract disagree, resolve the intended behavior rather than documenting
the regression as the new rule.

## Use on every change

1. **Locate the owner and consumers.** Read the owning implementation, callers,
   existing tests and relevant guide before adding another helper or state owner.
   Include callbacks, IPC handlers, retries, startup, shutdown and recovery paths;
   an import graph alone cannot reveal all consumers.
2. **State the invariant and select risks.** Describe what must remain true on
   success, failure, cancellation and replacement. Use the table below to select
   applicable rules. A small diff can change lock order or lifetime semantics.
3. **Trace the failure path before editing.** For concurrency work, sketch who
   owns each lock, permit, task and mutable state; what it waits for; and who
   releases it. For a reproducible bug, construct a focused failing regression.
   Record unresolved hypotheses as hypotheses, not confirmed defects.
4. **Implement at the existing boundary.** Preserve authority, durable acceptance,
   compatibility and resource budgets. Recheck invariants after moving work
   outside a guard. Evaluate the proposed fix for new races and deadlocks too.
5. **Verify the changed boundary and report evidence.** Run affected checks and
   required boundary scenarios under the testing workflow. Explain results,
   exclusions and unresolved evidence. Update this guide when the defect exposes
   a reusable failure pattern; follow the maintenance procedure below.

Accessible message summaries are consumer contracts. When photo, expression or
file naming changes, update browser selectors and the owning `prScenarios`
selection together; retain payload, privacy and receipt assertions instead of
restoring implementation-specific names for tests. The inline-media owner uses
`screenshot-portable.spec.ts` and `automatic-delivery.spec.ts` to cover screenshot
sending and group custody alongside the presentation scenarios.

Keep the risk explanation proportional to the change. A documentation edit does
not require a new concurrency test. A changed async callback does require a
lifetime review even when the diff is one line. Put task-specific reasoning and
results in the PR or ignored local evidence, not a new permanent report.

Cross-cutting idle budgets, demand-driven work and accumulation rules belong to
[performance requirements](performance-requirements.md). Apply them alongside the
correctness rules below; a smaller resource chart does not prove preserved recovery.

## Select rules by the changed boundary

| Change or symptom                                                        | Read at least                                                                                                                                         |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Locks, callbacks, synchronous dispatch, UI freezes                       | [R01](#r01-lock-order-and-reentrant-calls), [R02](#r02-thread-and-scheduler-progress), [R10](#r10-evidence-that-exercises-the-failure)                |
| Background work, native providers, logout, shutdown or cancellation      | [R02](#r02-thread-and-scheduler-progress), [R03](#r03-actual-work-owns-its-lifetime), [R06](#r06-exact-authority-and-stale-completions)               |
| Network requests, retries, polling, queues or batches                    | [R03](#r03-actual-work-owns-its-lifetime), [R04](#r04-deadlines-cover-the-whole-operation), [R05](#r05-bounded-work-must-also-make-progress)          |
| React effects, IPC reads, dialogs, optimistic updates or mutation status | [R06](#r06-exact-authority-and-stale-completions), [R07](#r07-observation-is-not-mutation-ownership), [R10](#r10-evidence-that-exercises-the-failure) |
| Storage, settings, imports, deletion or recovery                         | [R06](#r06-exact-authority-and-stale-completions), [R08](#r08-durable-state-and-failure-semantics), [R09](#r09-bound-input-and-resource-use)          |
| IPC/API inputs, files, media or protocol changes                         | [R06](#r06-exact-authority-and-stale-completions), [R08](#r08-durable-state-and-failure-semantics), [R09](#r09-bound-input-and-resource-use)          |
| Merge resolution, shared helper or dependency changes                    | Revisit the affected callers and all applicable rules; a clean textual merge does not establish compatible ownership or semantics.                    |

These are starting points, not permission to ignore another reachable boundary.
Do not add a global lock, retry loop, timeout or shared abstraction solely to make
the local symptom disappear.

A frozen UI may result from a lock cycle, blocked event thread, starvation, lost
wakeup, unbounded work or stale loading state. Identify the mechanism and the
missing progress condition before selecting a fix; these need different evidence.

## R01: Lock order and reentrant calls

**Failure pattern:** one path takes A then B while another takes B then A; or a
helper/callback reacquires a nonrecursive lock its caller already holds. The
second case can deadlock on a single thread. Nested reads also need review when
a queued writer can prevent a new read from completing.

Trace actual acquisition order through callees, authorization callbacks,
destructors and error cleanup. Include main-thread dispatch and task joins as
wait dependencies, not just mutexes. A typical UI cycle is:

```text
background task: holds session guard -> waits for main-thread callback
main thread:     handles UI event    -> waits for session guard
```

Use the owning module's order; do not invent one universal order for unrelated
subsystems. Make whether a helper acquires a guard or requires one explicit.
Account archive snapshots, history projections and delivery recovery share the
plaintext-sidecar order: sent, received, then received files. Recovery must not
hold received while waiting for sent: an archive has no delivery guard and can
otherwise hold sent while waiting for received. The real recovery regression
`recovery_does_not_hold_received_while_waiting_for_sent` in the
[recovery owner](../crates/mesh-talk-core/src/node/delivery_runtime.rs) holds sent,
probes received at the actual acquisition boundary, then releases contention and
joins the worker before asserting replay and progress.
Archive revision snapshots must read and release device-sync policy before
acquiring plaintext sidecars. Attachment commit holds delivery and policy while
checking the live received-file card; an archive holding received files while
waiting for policy creates a cycle and can also block erasure behind delivery.
Keep archive-key revalidation after indexing and page selection so a changed
policy still invalidates the export. The regression belongs to the
[account archive owner](../crates/mesh-talk-core/src/node/account_sync/archive.rs)
and must qualify progress while the competing policy/sidecar boundary is held,
then release and join both owners before asserting the outcome.
The same boundary applies to file-proof revisions: identity import holds the
proof store while validating received-file rows. Archive snapshots must read and
release proof metadata before taking sidecars, and retain proof revision in the
final archive-key validation. Its separate held-proof regression qualifies the
actual archive path; policy-only coverage does not establish this lock order.
Do not build a revision array from chained mutex temporaries: guards can survive
until the entire array statement ends. Snapshot each value in a completed
statement before acquiring the next metadata lock. The archive's held-identity
control must also prove suppression is free, preserving the identity-then-
suppression order used by file-row visibility checks.
Avoid invoking arbitrary callbacks while guarded. Where a commit callback must
run inside an authority guard, keep that contract narrow and inspect its complete
call chain. Queue presentation without retaining a guard needed by the UI;
validate captured authority when the queued callback executes.

Rust [temporary scopes](https://doc.rust-lang.org/reference/destructors.html#temporary-scopes)
can keep guards alive through the complete statement, including struct literals
and tuples. Read repeated owner scalars under one explicit short guard,
then release it before constructing a value that could acquire the owner again.
Check the actual temporary scope before declaring a cycle: each operand of a lazy
Boolean expression has its own temporary scope. An explicit short block can make
an observation boundary clearer without changing an already-released guard.

**Evidence:** exercise both competing paths and the real authorization variant.
An ordinary admission fixture does not cover a sensitive proof that itself locks
app state. Assert that the other operation progresses, not just that the first
eventually returns. See `checked_at_lock_revision` in
[runtime admission](../src-tauri/src/runtime_admission.rs), the verified-login
regression in [shared login tests](../src-tauri/src/shared_account_login/tests.rs),
and queued notification tests in [runtime state](../src-tauri/src/chat_commands/state.rs).

## R02: Thread and scheduler progress

**Failure pattern:** an `async` function performs blocking disk, crypto, OS-provider
or process work; a blocking worker retains a globally needed guard; or the parent
scheduler awaits optional work before polling unrelated ready operations.

Identify the executing thread and scheduling owner, not just the function's
signature. Move blocking work through the existing admitted worker boundary.
Inspect React render/effect/subscriber feedback loops and large synchronous data
transforms too; moving I/O off the UI thread does not bound those CPU costs.
Subscribe to status-only observations at the smallest presentation owner. A
parent chat subscription can rerender its virtualized message viewport for every
peer-check timestamp even when the rows are unchanged. The mounted
[conversation idle regression](../frontend/src/features/chat/ConversationViewIdle.test.ts)
requires live status updates without viewport renders, while new messages and
conversation replacement remain live.
Apply the same semantic boundary to native effects: the mounted
[chat shell regression](../frontend/src/features/chat/ChatAppIdle.test.ts) requires
unchanged notification context through peer freshness and ordering changes,
while real conversation/device-set changes, session replacement and unmount
retain publication and cleanup. Native revision admission still fences stale calls.

# Verification Before Completion

## Overview

Claiming work is complete without verification is dishonesty, not efficiency.

**Core principle:** Evidence before claims, always.

**Violating the letter of this rule is violating the spirit of this rule.**

## The Iron Law

```
NO COMPLETION CLAIMS WITHOUT FRESH VERIFICATION EVIDENCE
```

If you haven't run the verification command in this message, you cannot claim it passes.

## The Gate Function

```
BEFORE claiming any status or expressing satisfaction:

1. IDENTIFY: What command proves this claim?
2. RUN: Execute the FULL command (fresh, complete)
3. READ: Full output, check exit code, count failures
4. VERIFY: Does output confirm the claim?
   - If NO: State actual status with evidence
   - If YES: State claim WITH evidence
5. ONLY THEN: Make the claim

Skip any step = lying, not verifying
```

## Common Failures

| Claim | Requires | Not Sufficient |
|-------|----------|----------------|
| Tests pass | Test command output: 0 failures | Previous run, "should pass" |
| Linter clean | Linter output: 0 errors | Partial check, extrapolation |
| Build succeeds | Build command: exit 0 | Linter passing, logs look good |
| Bug fixed | Test original symptom: passes | Code changed, assumed fixed |
| Regression test works | Red-green cycle verified | Test passes once |
| Agent completed | VCS diff shows changes | Agent reports "success" |
| Requirements met | Line-by-line checklist | Tests passing |

## Red Flags - STOP

- Using "should", "probably", "seems to"
- Expressing satisfaction before verification ("Great!", "Perfect!", "Done!", etc.)
- About to commit/push/PR without verification
- Trusting agent success reports
- Relying on partial verification
- Thinking "just this once"
- Tired and wanting work over
- **ANY wording implying success without having run verification**

## Rationalization Prevention

| Excuse | Reality |
|--------|---------|
| "Should work now" | RUN the verification |
| "I'm confident" | Confidence ≠ evidence |
| "Just this once" | No exceptions |
| "Linter passed" | Linter ≠ compiler |
| "Agent said success" | Verify independently |
| "I'm tired" | Exhaustion ≠ excuse |
| "Partial check is enough" | Partial proves nothing |
| "Different words so rule doesn't apply" | Spirit over letter |

## Key Patterns

**Tests:**
```
✅ [Run test command] [See: 34/34 pass] "All tests pass"
❌ "Should pass now" / "Looks correct"
```

**Regression tests (TDD Red-Green):**
```
✅ Write → Run (pass) → Revert fix → Run (MUST FAIL) → Restore → Run (pass)
❌ "I've written a regression test" (without red-green verification)
```

**Build:**
```
✅ [Run build] [See: exit 0] "Build passes"
❌ "Linter passed" (linter doesn't check compilation)
```

**Requirements:**
```
✅ Re-read plan → Create checklist → Verify each → Report gaps or completion
❌ "Tests pass, phase complete"
```

**Agent delegation:**
```
✅ Agent reports success → Check VCS diff → Verify changes → Report actual state
❌ Trust agent report
```

## Why This Matters

From 24 failure memories:
- your human partner said "I don't believe you" - trust broken
- Undefined functions shipped - would crash
- Missing requirements shipped - incomplete features
- Time wasted on false completion → redirect → rework
- Violates: "Honesty is a core value. If you lie, you'll be replaced."

## When To Apply

**ALWAYS before:**
- ANY variation of success/completion claims
- ANY expression of satisfaction
- ANY positive statement about work state
- Committing, PR creation, task completion
- Moving to next task
- Delegating to agents

**Rule applies to:**
- Exact phrases
- Paraphrases and synonyms
- Implications of success
- ANY communication suggesting completion/correctness

## The Bottom Line

**No shortcuts for verification.**

Run the command. Read the output. THEN claim the result.

This is non-negotiable.

## Agent claims and parallel branches

Read [repository rules](../AGENTS.md), [project context](../PROJECT.md), this task's
source rows and [module ownership](module-boundaries.md). For source discovery use
CodeGraph first when indexed. The active coordinator owns task selection and
integration; one implementer owns each task at a time. Agents do not silently
reassign others' tasks or treat a branch name as proof of ownership.

### Claim and state protocol

1. Re-read current `main`, task and shared-interface decisions. Confirm required
   inputs are linked and adequate, not just checked boxes. If a PR already owns the
   change, attach/continue it through the supported session workflow rather than
   create a duplicate. Preserve unrelated work.
2. Atomically agree the claim through the active coordinator/tracker before
   editing. The coordinator records one compact row below (or a linked issue/PR
   as the single live owner). A stale copy of this document is not a lock.
3. Claim includes task, agent/session, base SHA, owned paths, branch, shared
   interface assumptions, acceptance/evidence owner and current next action.
   Record exact source paths only after inspection. No overlapping mutations
   without the interface/integration owner explicitly coordinating the split.
4. Create one task branch in the session namespace from the accepted base; use
   its registered isolated worktree where needed. A stack uses its real parent
   branch and verified head, with a stated merge order. Do not keep all work on
   one long-lived feature branch or add another worktree without ownership notes.
5. Keep the PR limited to the task and any inseparable contract/selector/docs.
   Update progress and blocker/review/CI state. Push fixes for the same task to
   the same PR, resolve addressed review threads and revalidate current source.
6. Integrator rechecks required current-head CI and reviews, then squash-merges
   under [merge policy](../specifications/git_standards.md). Rebase/merge dependent
   work deliberately; no force-push without authorization. Capture delivered
   acceptance or named limits, release the claim and clean only task-owned
   branches/worktrees under repository preservation rules.

States: `Unclaimed -> Claimed -> Investigating -> Ready for design/implementation
-> Implementing -> In review -> Validated -> Merged`. Use `Needs decision` or
`Needs evidence` with owner/next action when blocked, and `Deferred`/`Retained`
with reason/revisit conditions for no-go results. A merged research PR completes
its evidence task, not a downstream implementation or a release guarantee.

| Task     | Claimant / session | Branch / base | Owned paths / shared interfaces | State / next action                             | Issue / PR / evidence |
| -------- | ------------------ | ------------- | ------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------- | --------------------- |
| None yet | Unassigned         | Not created   | Not assigned                    | Planning document only; no product task claimed | No product PR         |

Suggested lanes, subject to actual path/resource review:

| Lane                      | Initial eligible work                                | Conflict boundary                                                                                                                                |
| ------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Coordinator / domain      | T001, then T002/T008/T009                            | One owner coordinates glossary, authority and shared-interface decisions; do not funnel every tiny fix through an all-app redesign.              |
| Runtime performance       | T003/T004, then independent measured P1 slices       | Coordinate shared stores, session lifecycle and native measurement resources; reserve production-like profiling to avoid concurrent build noise. |
| Validation engineering    | T005/T006, then T010/T038                            | One owner for selection, runner and required-check policy; reuse tests and maintain current protections.                                         |
| Privacy and user controls | T007, then T030/T031/T032                            | Identity/crypto/wire decisions require the core contract owner; separate endorsement research.                                                   |
| Independent UI features   | T039 after T001; later review/voice/PWA ready slices | Do not concurrently edit shared chat/store/IPC contracts without a designated integration owner.                                                 |
| Platform research         | T034/T047 when inputs ready; T035/T069 later         | Research output alone does not claim core files or authorize branch extraction/migration.                                                        |

Start with a small number of nonconflicting tasks; expand only when review and
runner/native capacity permit. Do not invent a universal agent count or start
parallel workers merely because a roadmap row exists. Workers register meaningful
progress, evidence and blockers with the active project coordinator. This roadmap
supports parallel delivery; it does not automatically dispatch agents.

## Requirements-to-release document flow

Use the existing documentation owners. Requirements explain desired outcomes;
architecture explains contracts; implementation plans explain the next bounded
change; tests/evals provide evidence; ADRs preserve important trade-offs. A giant
permanent implementation diary is not the source of truth.

| Step                            | Deliverable / owner                                     | Entry and exit                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| ------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 1. Requirement                  | This roadmap, stable REQ/WORK/T links and product owner | Observable user scenario, constraints, explicit unknowns and non-goals; preserve the original confirmed scope.                                                                                                  |
| 2. Evidence / triage            | Existing owning guide plus linked PR/CI evidence        | Inspect implementation/callers and actual conditions; quantify when relevant, label uncertainty; select retain/fix/feature/experiment rather than assume a defect.                                              |
| 3. Feature contract / design    | Owning feature/network/storage/privacy guide            | Define authority, state/lifetimes, errors, permission, failure/recovery and budget; compare alternatives. Use a short design for a small feature, a substantial design for protocol/migration/platform changes. |
| 4. Important choice             | Existing topic rationale or linked ADR                  | Record why, alternatives, consequences/status and reconsideration triggers. Do not require an RFC/ADR for every small edit.                                                                                     |
| 5. Implementation slice         | Task PR plus ignored local plan under tmp               | Claim exact paths/interfaces, test selectors and concrete steps. Do not commit scratch plans or duplicate the existing contract. Read performance/reliability rules before edits.                               |
| 6. Change and boundary feedback | Owning tests, validation.json and relevant guide        | Requirement-derived assertions, applicable failure paths, affected static/tests and browser/native evidence; update rule/selector/consumers together when boundaries change.                                    |
| 7. Candidate acceptance         | Current committed PR, reviews and protected checks      | Report tested SHA, command results, gaps and rollback/recovery; required current-head gates before merge. Optional full local preparation is not an automatic per-edit burden.                                  |
| 8. Integration / release        | Existing update and release lifecycle                   | Integrate compatible slices, update backlog/status/help only as warranted, rehearse affected install/restore/upgrade/native behavior; publish only through existing authorized release flow.                    |

### Document owners and entry paths

| Information                                                             | Existing owner / intended destination                                                                                                                         |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Future work, priority, source mapping and claim entry                   | This roadmap; linked from docs/README.md, already reachable through PROJECT.md.                                                                               |
| Implemented capabilities / deliberate limits                            | [Implementation status](../specifications/TODO.md); do not turn it into a competing chronological backlog.                                                    |
| Domain terms and modeling                                               | [CONTEXT.md](../CONTEXT.md), [domain-design.md](domain-design.md).                                                                                            |
| Module authority and parallel interface ownership                       | [module-boundaries.md](module-boundaries.md).                                                                                                                 |
| Protocol, network, storage and crypto                                   | [ARCHITECTURE.md](ARCHITECTURE.md), [network-design-reference.md](network-design-reference.md) and relevant topic guides.                                     |
| Performance and AI reliability                                          | [performance-requirements.md](performance-requirements.md), [ai-coding-reliability.md](ai-coding-reliability.md); extend existing rules with proven patterns. |
| Validation/eval coverage and cost                                       | [testing-feedback-loop.md](testing-feedback-loop.md), [ci-maintenance.md](ci-maintenance.md), owning validation.json, [evaluation inputs](evals/README.md).   |
| Durable significant trade-offs                                          | Existing topic guide; linked ADR only when needed under [DDD conventions](domain-design.md).                                                                  |
| User help and product claims                                            | [Help](help/README.md), relevant feature guide, documentation hub; do not claim roadmap features are shipped.                                                 |
| Temporary plans, raw profiles, research snapshots and generated reports | Ignored task-owned tmp/target or PR/CI artifacts; reusable suites in docs/evals, not run histories.                                                           |

### Validation and definition of done

Use the [existing stages](testing-feedback-loop.md#validation-stages-and-agent-responsibilities)
and current required-check policy. For future code work preview `make test-plan`
or `make verify-plan`; run affected tests while changing and `make verify-changed`
with the necessary browser/native escalation. Run `make standards-check` when
adding/moving source or changing contracts. Run repository hygiene before commit.
Create PRs through `./scripts/create-pr.sh -- <gh pr create options>`; it requires
a clean committed candidate. Do not fabricate receipt/coverage evidence or change
thresholds simply to pass. Exact commands and filters come from the selected
owner and actual diff, not a generic all-suite instruction in this roadmap.

A delivery is done only when the accepted user outcome and failure/recovery paths
are evidenced, resource behavior is compared for the affected startup/idle/active
and return-to-idle phases, relevant compatibility/migration/reversal limits are
explicit, selectors and maintained docs match behavior, and the current head
meets required reviews/checks. Full workspace/native/release gates remain in their
owners; a subset or model score is not universal correctness evidence. All methods
in REQ-030 receive a later applicability decision, not silent removal or blanket
mandatory execution. Optional extensive checks must not recreate REQ-003's delays.

### Reusable task handoff fields

Before a ready task is assigned, put these fields in its issue/PR or task record:

- Stable T/WORK/REQ IDs and concrete outcome/non-goals.

Use this guide before implementing or reviewing a change, especially a bug fix,
refactor, merge resolution or optimization. Its purpose is to turn recurring
failure modes into concrete design questions and executable checks. Compiling,
adding a timeout or passing a happy-path test does not establish reliability.

This guide owns the cross-cutting review method and reusable failure patterns.
[Module ownership](module-boundaries.md) owns implementation boundaries;
[architecture](ARCHITECTURE.md), [network contracts](network-design-reference.md)
and feature guides own behavior and resource limits. The
[testing workflow](testing-feedback-loop.md) owns commands, selection and gates.
Link to those owners instead of copying their changing contracts here. When code
and a contract disagree, resolve the intended behavior rather than documenting
the regression as the new rule.

## Use on every change

1. **Locate the owner and consumers.** Read the owning implementation, callers,
   existing tests and relevant guide before adding another helper or state owner.
   Include callbacks, IPC handlers, retries, startup, shutdown and recovery paths;
   an import graph alone cannot reveal all consumers.
2. **State the invariant and select risks.** Describe what must remain true on
   success, failure, cancellation and replacement. Use the table below to select
   applicable rules. A small diff can change lock order or lifetime semantics.
3. **Trace the failure path before editing.** For concurrency work, sketch who
   owns each lock, permit, task and mutable state; what it waits for; and who
   releases it. For a reproducible bug, construct a focused failing regression.
   Record unresolved hypotheses as hypotheses, not confirmed defects.
4. **Implement at the existing boundary.** Preserve authority, durable acceptance,
   compatibility and resource budgets. Recheck invariants after moving work
   outside a guard. Evaluate the proposed fix for new races and deadlocks too.
5. **Verify the changed boundary and report evidence.** Run affected checks and
   required boundary scenarios under the testing workflow. Explain results,
   exclusions and unresolved evidence. Update this guide when the defect exposes
   a reusable failure pattern; follow the maintenance procedure below.

Accessible message summaries are consumer contracts. When photo, expression or
file naming changes, update browser selectors and the owning `prScenarios`
selection together; retain payload, privacy and receipt assertions instead of
restoring implementation-specific names for tests. The inline-media owner uses
`screenshot-portable.spec.ts` and `automatic-delivery.spec.ts` to cover screenshot
sending and group custody alongside the presentation scenarios.

Keep the risk explanation proportional to the change. A documentation edit does
not require a new concurrency test. A changed async callback does require a
lifetime review even when the diff is one line. Put task-specific reasoning and
results in the PR or ignored local evidence, not a new permanent report.

Cross-cutting idle budgets, demand-driven work and accumulation rules belong to
[performance requirements](performance-requirements.md). Apply them alongside the
correctness rules below; a smaller resource chart does not prove preserved recovery.

## Select rules by the changed boundary

| Change or symptom                                                        | Read at least                                                                                                                                         |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Locks, callbacks, synchronous dispatch, UI freezes                       | [R01](#r01-lock-order-and-reentrant-calls), [R02](#r02-thread-and-scheduler-progress), [R10](#r10-evidence-that-exercises-the-failure)                |
| Background work, native providers, logout, shutdown or cancellation      | [R02](#r02-thread-and-scheduler-progress), [R03](#r03-actual-work-owns-its-lifetime), [R06](#r06-exact-authority-and-stale-completions)               |
| Network requests, retries, polling, queues or batches                    | [R03](#r03-actual-work-owns-its-lifetime), [R04](#r04-deadlines-cover-the-whole-operation), [R05](#r05-bounded-work-must-also-make-progress)          |
| React effects, IPC reads, dialogs, optimistic updates or mutation status | [R06](#r06-exact-authority-and-stale-completions), [R07](#r07-observation-is-not-mutation-ownership), [R10](#r10-evidence-that-exercises-the-failure) |
| Storage, settings, imports, deletion or recovery                         | [R06](#r06-exact-authority-and-stale-completions), [R08](#r08-durable-state-and-failure-semantics), [R09](#r09-bound-input-and-resource-use)          |
| IPC/API inputs, files, media or protocol changes                         | [R06](#r06-exact-authority-and-stale-completions), [R08](#r08-durable-state-and-failure-semantics), [R09](#r09-bound-input-and-resource-use)          |
| Merge resolution, shared helper or dependency changes                    | Revisit the affected callers and all applicable rules; a clean textual merge does not establish compatible ownership or semantics.                    |

These are starting points, not permission to ignore another reachable boundary.
Do not add a global lock, retry loop, timeout or shared abstraction solely to make
the local symptom disappear.

A frozen UI may result from a lock cycle, blocked event thread, starvation, lost
wakeup, unbounded work or stale loading state. Identify the mechanism and the
missing progress condition before selecting a fix; these need different evidence.

## R01: Lock order and reentrant calls

**Failure pattern:** one path takes A then B while another takes B then A; or a
helper/callback reacquires a nonrecursive lock its caller already holds. The
second case can deadlock on a single thread. Nested reads also need review when
a queued writer can prevent a new read from completing.

Trace actual acquisition order through callees, authorization callbacks,
destructors and error cleanup. Include main-thread dispatch and task joins as
wait dependencies, not just mutexes. A typical UI cycle is:

```text
background task: holds session guard -> waits for main-thread callback
main thread:     handles UI event    -> waits for session guard
```

Use the owning module's order; do not invent one universal order for unrelated
subsystems. Make whether a helper acquires a guard or requires one explicit.
Account archive snapshots, history projections and delivery recovery share the
plaintext-sidecar order: sent, received, then received files. Recovery must not
hold received while waiting for sent: an archive has no delivery guard and can
otherwise hold sent while waiting for received. The real recovery regression
`recovery_does_not_hold_received_while_waiting_for_sent` in the
[recovery owner](../crates/mesh-talk-core/src/node/delivery_runtime.rs) holds sent,
probes received at the actual acquisition boundary, then releases contention and
joins the worker before asserting replay and progress.
Archive revision snapshots must read and release device-sync policy before
acquiring plaintext sidecars. Attachment commit holds delivery and policy while
checking the live received-file card; an archive holding received files while
waiting for policy creates a cycle and can also block erasure behind delivery.
Keep archive-key revalidation after indexing and page selection so a changed
policy still invalidates the export. The regression belongs to the
[account archive owner](../crates/mesh-talk-core/src/node/account_sync/archive.rs)
and must qualify progress while the competing policy/sidecar boundary is held,
then release and join both owners before asserting the outcome.
The same boundary applies to file-proof revisions: identity import holds the
proof store while validating received-file rows. Archive snapshots must read and
release proof metadata before taking sidecars, and retain proof revision in the
final archive-key validation. Its separate held-proof regression qualifies the
actual archive path; policy-only coverage does not establish this lock order.
Do not build a revision array from chained mutex temporaries: guards can survive
until the entire array statement ends. Snapshot each value in a completed
statement before acquiring the next metadata lock. The archive's held-identity
control must also prove suppression is free, preserving the identity-then-
suppression order used by file-row visibility checks.
Avoid invoking arbitrary callbacks while guarded. Where a commit callback must
run inside an authority guard, keep that contract narrow and inspect its complete
call chain. Queue presentation without retaining a guard needed by the UI;
validate captured authority when the queued callback executes.

Rust [temporary scopes](https://doc.rust-lang.org/reference/destructors.html#temporary-scopes)
can keep guards alive through the complete statement, including struct literals
and tuples. Read repeated owner scalars under one explicit short guard,
then release it before constructing a value that could acquire the owner again.
Check the actual temporary scope before declaring a cycle: each operand of a lazy
Boolean expression has its own temporary scope. An explicit short block can make
an observation boundary clearer without changing an already-released guard.

**Evidence:** exercise both competing paths and the real authorization variant.
An ordinary admission fixture does not cover a sensitive proof that itself locks
app state. Assert that the other operation progresses, not just that the first
eventually returns. See `checked_at_lock_revision` in
[runtime admission](../src-tauri/src/runtime_admission.rs), the verified-login
regression in [shared login tests](../src-tauri/src/shared_account_login/tests.rs),
and queued notification tests in [runtime state](../src-tauri/src/chat_commands/state.rs).

## R02: Thread and scheduler progress

**Failure pattern:** an `async` function performs blocking disk, crypto, OS-provider
or process work; a blocking worker retains a globally needed guard; or the parent
scheduler awaits optional work before polling unrelated ready operations.

Identify the executing thread and scheduling owner, not just the function's
signature. Move blocking work through the existing admitted worker boundary.
Inspect React render/effect/subscriber feedback loops and large synchronous data
transforms too; moving I/O off the UI thread does not bound those CPU costs.
Subscribe to status-only observations at the smallest presentation owner. A
parent chat subscription can rerender its virtualized message viewport for every
peer-check timestamp even when the rows are unchanged. The mounted
[conversation idle regression](../frontend/src/features/chat/ConversationViewIdle.test.ts)
requires live status updates without viewport renders, while new messages and
conversation replacement remain live.
Apply the same semantic boundary to native effects: the mounted
[chat shell regression](../frontend/src/features/chat/ChatAppIdle.test.ts) requires
unchanged notification context through peer freshness and ordering changes,
while real conversation/device-set changes, session replacement and unmount
retain publication and cleanup. Native revision admission still fences stale calls.

# Verification Before Completion

## Overview

Claiming work is complete without verification is dishonesty, not efficiency.

**Core principle:** Evidence before claims, always.

**Violating the letter of this rule is violating the spirit of this rule.**

## The Iron Law

```
NO COMPLETION CLAIMS WITHOUT FRESH VERIFICATION EVIDENCE
```

If you haven't run the verification command in this message, you cannot claim it passes.

## The Gate Function

```
BEFORE claiming any status or expressing satisfaction:

1. IDENTIFY: What command proves this claim?
2. RUN: Execute the FULL command (fresh, complete)
3. READ: Full output, check exit code, count failures
4. VERIFY: Does output confirm the claim?
   - If NO: State actual status with evidence
   - If YES: State claim WITH evidence
5. ONLY THEN: Make the claim

Skip any step = lying, not verifying
```

## Common Failures

| Claim | Requires | Not Sufficient |
|-------|----------|----------------|
| Tests pass | Test command output: 0 failures | Previous run, "should pass" |
| Linter clean | Linter output: 0 errors | Partial check, extrapolation |
| Build succeeds | Build command: exit 0 | Linter passing, logs look good |
| Bug fixed | Test original symptom: passes | Code changed, assumed fixed |
| Regression test works | Red-green cycle verified | Test passes once |
| Agent completed | VCS diff shows changes | Agent reports "success" |
| Requirements met | Line-by-line checklist | Tests passing |

## Red Flags - STOP

- Using "should", "probably", "seems to"
- Expressing satisfaction before verification ("Great!", "Perfect!", "Done!", etc.)
- About to commit/push/PR without verification
- Trusting agent success reports
- Relying on partial verification
- Thinking "just this once"
- Tired and wanting work over
- **ANY wording implying success without having run verification**

## Rationalization Prevention

| Excuse | Reality |
|--------|---------|
| "Should work now" | RUN the verification |
| "I'm confident" | Confidence ≠ evidence |
| "Just this once" | No exceptions |
| "Linter passed" | Linter ≠ compiler |
| "Agent said success" | Verify independently |
| "I'm tired" | Exhaustion ≠ excuse |
| "Partial check is enough" | Partial proves nothing |
| "Different words so rule doesn't apply" | Spirit over letter |

## Key Patterns

**Tests:**
```
✅ [Run test command] [See: 34/34 pass] "All tests pass"
❌ "Should pass now" / "Looks correct"
```

**Regression tests (TDD Red-Green):**
```
✅ Write → Run (pass) → Revert fix → Run (MUST FAIL) → Restore → Run (pass)
❌ "I've written a regression test" (without red-green verification)
```

**Build:**
```
✅ [Run build] [See: exit 0] "Build passes"
❌ "Linter passed" (linter doesn't check compilation)
```

**Requirements:**
```
✅ Re-read plan → Create checklist → Verify each → Report gaps or completion
❌ "Tests pass, phase complete"
```

**Agent delegation:**
```
✅ Agent reports success → Check VCS diff → Verify changes → Report actual state
❌ Trust agent report
```

## Why This Matters

From 24 failure memories:
- your human partner said "I don't believe you" - trust broken
- Undefined functions shipped - would crash
- Missing requirements shipped - incomplete features
- Time wasted on false completion → redirect → rework
- Violates: "Honesty is a core value. If you lie, you'll be replaced."

## When To Apply

**ALWAYS before:**
- ANY variation of success/completion claims
- ANY expression of satisfaction
- ANY positive statement about work state
- Committing, PR creation, task completion
- Moving to next task
- Delegating to agents

**Rule applies to:**
- Exact phrases
- Paraphrases and synonyms
- Implications of success
- ANY communication suggesting completion/correctness

## The Bottom Line

**No shortcuts for verification.**

Run the command. Read the output. THEN claim the result.

This is non-negotiable.

# Mesh Talk project context

Mesh Talk is a local-first, end-to-end encrypted desktop messenger with a UI-free
Rust core, a Tauri host and a React frontend. Direct LAN/routed communication is
independent of optional peer-operated post offices. Equal trusted relays add
bounded encrypted custody and opt-in cross-site introductions; no global hub or
vendor-operated account service is required.

## Deliberate design boundaries

- **Pairing authorization:** a one-time 128-bit code binds the linker and joiner
  device keys. Durable enrollment invalidates old sessions; interrupted adoption
  has a restricted code-authenticated retry. There is no separate SAS ceremony.
- **Relay metadata:** production relays store opaque outer events, not readable
  original authors, conversation IDs or channel controls. Connection identities,
  pseudonymous mailboxes, size buckets and timing remain observable. See
  [the exact privacy boundary](../docs/post-office-metadata-privacy.md).
- **Bounded custody:** relay copies have capacity limits and a 30-day maximum age;
  this is not guaranteed minimum retention or permanent storage.
- **Connections:** the client Node has bounded sequential session reuse, not one
  multiplexed socket per relay or an eight-socket ceiling for the whole machine.
- **Reachability and trust:** Tailscale does not merge LANs; explicit relay trust
  and client directory consent are independent of routing.
- **Membership presentation:** removed group members' past reactions no longer
  render under the current-membership visibility rule.
- **Linux dependency constraint:** the maintained
  [GLib compatibility workflow](../.github/workflows/glib-0.20-watch.yml) tracks the
  GTK/Tauri dependency gate. Consult the lockfile and security configuration before
  changing versions; do not treat this note as a vulnerability waiver.

## Evidence and future decisions

The [implementation/evidence tracker](../docs/network-design-reference.md#implementation-and-evidence-tracker)
records named logical and physical checks. Three independent physical LANs, a
separate ordinary client host on the mini's LAN, native macOS WebView media and
physical camera/microphone quality remain distinct acceptance cases.

New protocol capabilities such as true multiplexing, automatic federation trust,
mailbox-backed calling, TURN or stronger replicated-storage guarantees require
an explicit design and new evidence. They are not implied by the implemented
capabilities above.

## Agreed workflow

1. The user introduces items one at a time, in any order, without needing to categorize them.
2. The assistant records and clarifies each item, updating this same document after each discussion. Preserve original intent and distinguish user-confirmed conclusions from suggestions, assumptions and unanswered questions.
3. Collection continues until the user explicitly says “收集完了” (collection complete), or gives an equivalent explicit instruction. Silence, topic changes and requests to continue do not close collection.
4. Only after collection closes, review the complete set together: deduplicate, consolidate, split oversized items and resolve conflicts. Preserve original IDs and traceability.
5. Classify the work together: defect fixes, experience/performance improvements, new features, technical maintenance and future roadmap. Categories may overlap. Some questions may close with explanations instead of development tasks.
6. Prioritize globally using value, urgency, effort, risk and prerequisites. Distinguish confirmed from suspected dependencies. Define acceptance criteria, phases, order and parallel opportunities.
7. Confirm the complete actionable TODO document, then prepare its maintained repository placement and PR. Merge into main through repository review and current-head check requirements before starting planned implementation.
8. Use the confirmed global plan to decide branch boundaries, shared-interface ownership, integration order and incremental execution.

# Mesh Talk project context

Mesh Talk is a local-first, end-to-end encrypted desktop messenger with a UI-free
Rust core, a Tauri host and a React frontend. Direct LAN/routed communication is
independent of optional peer-operated post offices. Equal trusted relays add
bounded encrypted custody and opt-in cross-site introductions; no global hub or
vendor-operated account service is required.

versions and implementation history belong to their references and Git history.
# Implementation status and acceptance boundaries

This stable path is the current status index, not a chronological TODO list or a
claim that every topology/platform combination has been verified. Feature and
protocol details belong to the linked owning guides; Git history records completed
work.

## Current capability areas

| Area                       | Implemented behavior                                                                                                                             | Reference / boundary                                                                                                                                                                    |
| -------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Direct conversations       | Signed discovery, identity-pinned Noise/TCP, encrypted account-addressed DMs, replies, reactions, mentions, search and retained history.         | [Architecture](../docs/ARCHITECTURE.md); discovery and TCP reachability remain separate.                                                                                                |
| Groups                     | Signed membership controls, sender-key encryption, bounded fanout and authorized member recovery with per-member sharing.                        | [Group flows and scenarios](../docs/network-design-reference.md#d-group-creation-distribution-and-member-recovery); a removed/nonmember device cannot acquire authority from discovery. |
| Relay networking           | Equal trusted post offices, shared public enrollment, opaque custody/federation, direct-first attempts, soft preference and alternatives.        | [Network baseline](../docs/network-design-reference.md); an alternate needs a surviving onward route.                                                                                   |
| Network controls           | Per-device master/send/receive/directory preferences, physical-LAN-only discovery and direct LAN/Tailscale relay selection.                      | [Privacy controls](../docs/privacy-controls.md); visibility does not grant conversation authority or create a firewall.                                                                 |
| Files and folders          | Encrypted chunks, exact-offer consent, durable decisions, restart recovery, integrity checks and recipient completion.                           | [File flow](../docs/network-design-reference.md#e-files-folders-consent-and-completion); card arrival is not byte completion.                                                           |
| Linked devices             | Code-authorized enrollment, certified sibling synchronization and device-local category preferences.                                             | [Pairing and replay](../docs/network-design-reference.md#g-linking-and-ongoing-account-synchronization); full replay needs its own live authenticated route.                            |
| Calls                      | Optional device-addressed live Noise signaling and separate WebRTC media.                                                                        | No post-office signaling fallback or TURN service; native WebView and physical capture acceptance remain separate.                                                                      |
| Desktop presentation       | Shared person/relay classification, account/device profile details, themes, avatars, stickers, virtualized navigation and optional pack installation. | [Visual system](../frontend/DESIGN.md) · [Customization packs](../docs/CUSTOMIZATION_PACKS.md).                                                                                         |
| Local privacy and recovery | Privacy presets, lock controls, hidden contacts, local retention, recall and encrypted manual backup/restore.                                    | [Privacy](../docs/privacy-controls.md) · [Backup/recovery](../docs/backup-recovery.md); restore creates a new device and cannot revoke an old one.                                      |

## Deliberate design boundaries

- **Pairing authorization:** a one-time 128-bit code binds the linker and joiner
  device keys. Durable enrollment invalidates old sessions; interrupted adoption
  has a restricted code-authenticated retry. There is no separate SAS ceremony.
- **Relay metadata:** production relays store opaque outer events, not readable
  original authors, conversation IDs or channel controls. Connection identities,
  pseudonymous mailboxes, size buckets and timing remain observable. See
  [the exact privacy boundary](../docs/post-office-metadata-privacy.md).
- **Bounded custody:** relay copies have capacity limits and a 30-day maximum age;
  this is not guaranteed minimum retention or permanent storage.
- **Connections:** the client Node has bounded sequential session reuse, not one
  multiplexed socket per relay or an eight-socket ceiling for the whole machine.
- **Reachability and trust:** Tailscale does not merge LANs; explicit relay trust
  and client directory consent are independent of routing.
- **Membership presentation:** removed group members' past reactions no longer
  render under the current-membership visibility rule.
- **Linux dependency constraint:** the maintained
  [GLib compatibility workflow](../.github/workflows/glib-0.20-watch.yml) tracks the
  GTK/Tauri dependency gate. Consult the lockfile and security configuration before
  changing versions; do not treat this note as a vulnerability waiver.

## Evidence and future decisions

The [implementation/evidence tracker](../docs/network-design-reference.md#implementation-and-evidence-tracker)
records named logical and physical checks. Three independent physical LANs, a
separate ordinary client host on the mini's LAN, native macOS WebView media and
physical camera/microphone quality remain distinct acceptance cases.

New protocol capabilities such as true multiplexing, automatic federation trust,
mailbox-backed calling, TURN or stronger replicated-storage guarantees require
an explicit design and new evidence. They are not implied by the implemented
capabilities above.
