## Priority and classification

| Priority | Meaning                                               | Selection rule                                                                                                                                                   |
| -------- | ----------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| P0       | Establish trustworthy evidence and critical contracts | First bounded inventory, runtime/validation baselines, privacy and sync authority models; urgent verified security/data-loss defects take immediate precedence.  |
| P1       | Improve and protect the current messenger             | Evidence-backed performance/reliability fixes, practical protection, reusable contracts, monitoring, documentation and validation effectiveness.                 |
| P2       | Bounded capability expansion or decision research     | QR, browser review, group voice, mobile PWA and client adapters after their own readiness gates; UI/peer research is not a commitment to migrate/add features.   |
| P3       | Conditional longer-term roadmap                       | Forum/feed, incentives/endorsements, external SDK, marketplace, video and any justified UI migration; each requires a concrete product/technical decision first. |

Categories are orthogonal to priority: **Optimization** changes cost/latency at a
preserved contract; **Feature** adds observable capability; **Quality/Security**
protects named invariants; **Architecture/Governance** clarifies ownership and
interfaces; **Research/Decision** produces evidence or an explicit choice. No
suspected issue is labeled a confirmed bug. An investigation may close with
retain/no-change and recorded evidence. That is a valid outcome, not permission to
manufacture a refactor to satisfy a checkbox.

Every task has a priority and hard input dependencies. Within one priority, task
ID is a default discussion/dispatch tie-break, never an excuse to block independent
ready work. Lower-priority work can run concurrently only when it does not consume
the constrained owner/review/native-test capacity needed for higher-priority work.
An actual urgent security, data-loss or hard-freeze finding overrides this queue.

Start with a small number of nonconflicting tasks; expand only when review and

progress, evidence and blockers with the active project coordinator. This roadmap

## Capability and responsibility evidence map

Use this map with the [roadmap](../docs/development-roadmap.md), not as a second
backlog. Inspection baseline: `e5133000ec8ea2375de81fdcf55c2561c8cee0b2`,
remote `main` independently checked on 2026-11-18 (Asia/Singapore).
Source links below pin that baseline; recheck symbols, callers and selectors when
claiming work on a newer source. No `.codegraph/` index exists in this checkout;
source discovery used direct file inspection and text search.

**Evidence levels:** source/test presence is static evidence, not a passing test.
The network guide's [evidence tracker](../docs/network-design-reference.md#implementation-and-evidence-tracker)
is historical evidence with named limits, not a fresh run. This inventory did not
launch the application, read user chat data, profile processes, execute product
tests/E2E, or evaluate another project's technology. Documentation validation is
reported separately. No current runtime, platform or performance acceptance is
inferred from source presence or the earlier documentation-only PR's green CI.

**Status describes the current foundation relative to the requested topic:**
Implemented means the named foundation has concrete owners and consumers; it does
not complete every roadmap refinement. Partial means existing functionality
covers part of the desired scope. Missing is bounded to a requested entry absent
from the inspected entry points, not proof that no experimental branch implements
it. Unknown means the desired capability or decision has insufficient inspected
evidence. None of these labels closes a delivery task.

### Topic coverage

Every WORK topic appears once. Evidence IDs below provide source symbols,
representative caller paths, authoritative guides and existing test selectors.

Full process-family CPU/memory/physical disk/network/connection and peer-latency collection, tray display, reuse costs and off-state acceptance remain T004/T026/T027. Do not relabel last-seen age as latency.                                                      |

### Evidence and representative caller paths

E01–E13 are navigational evidence, not a competing protocol contract. `core` below
means `crates/mesh-talk-core`; frontend test paths are relative to `frontend/`.
Rust filters and validation contract IDs are examples of existing selections;
read the complete owning `validation.json` and its escalation notes before use.

**E01 — Diagnostics, logging and work attribution.**
[useDiagnosticsController](https://github.com/OctopusGarage/mesh-talk/blob/e5133000ec8ea2375de81fdcf55c2561c8cee0b2/frontend/src/features/chat/diagnostics/useDiagnosticsController.ts#L49) → `frontend/src/lib/api/diagnostics.ts` → [diag_get_peers](https://github.com/OctopusGarage/mesh-talk/blob/e5133000ec8ea2375de81fdcf55c2561c8cee0b2/src-tauri/src/chat_commands/diagnostics.rs#L37) reads the existing
roster. Environment facts live in `src-tauri/src/diagnostics.rs`; log rotation,
retention and opt-in IPC command counts live in [ipc_work_enabled](https://github.com/OctopusGarage/mesh-talk/blob/e5133000ec8ea2375de81fdcf55c2561c8cee0b2/src-tauri/src/logger/mod.rs#L24). The startup
[application_startup timer](https://github.com/OctopusGarage/mesh-talk/blob/e5133000ec8ea2375de81fdcf55c2561c8cee0b2/src-tauri/src/lib.rs#L130) uses `perf.rs` elapsed-time tracing; it is not a full-family resource
sampler. Core [OrderWorkObserver::from_env](https://github.com/OctopusGarage/mesh-talk/blob/e5133000ec8ea2375de81fdcf55c2561c8cee0b2/crates/mesh-talk-core/src/node/work_observation.rs#L164) and [database observation::from_env](https://github.com/OctopusGarage/mesh-talk/blob/e5133000ec8ea2375de81fdcf55c2561c8cee0b2/crates/mesh-talk-core/src/storage/database/observation.rs#L149) expose opt-in work/write attribution.
These observations are not OS physical-write or energy measurements. Reuse must
preserve bounded collection, sensitive metadata policy and disabled-mode cost.
Guide: [diagnostics](../docs/help/topics/diagnostics.md) and
[performance requirements](../docs/performance-requirements.md).
Present selectors: `desktop-diagnostics` (Rust `diagnostics::`, `perf::`),
`frontend-updates` includes
`src/features/chat/diagnostics/useDiagnosticsController.test.ts`.

**E02 — Trigger, scheduling and retirement ownership.**
[spawn_node_runtime](https://github.com/OctopusGarage/mesh-talk/blob/e5133000ec8ea2375de81fdcf55c2561c8cee0b2/src-tauri/src/runtime_bootstrap.rs#L31) installs the bounded participant runtime; [RuntimeWork::local_repair_capacity](https://github.com/OctopusGarage/mesh-talk/blob/e5133000ec8ea2375de81fdcf55c2561c8cee0b2/crates/mesh-talk-core/src/node/runtime_work.rs#L74) serializes local
repair capacity while actual tracked work owns retirement. Account [send_account_wake](https://github.com/OctopusGarage/mesh-talk/blob/e5133000ec8ea2375de81fdcf55c2561c8cee0b2/crates/mesh-talk-core/src/node/account_sync/wake.rs#L275) and
[LocalMaintenance](https://github.com/OctopusGarage/mesh-talk/blob/e5133000ec8ea2375de81fdcf55c2561c8cee0b2/crates/mesh-talk-core/src/node/account_sync/local_maintenance.rs#L6) retain semantic input/retry state. Frontend event consumers share
[subscribeDocumentInvalidation](https://github.com/OctopusGarage/mesh-talk/blob/e5133000ec8ea2375de81fdcf55c2561c8cee0b2/frontend/src/lib/syncInvalidation.ts#L29) and [useSerialPoll](https://github.com/OctopusGarage/mesh-talk/blob/e5133000ec8ea2375de81fdcf55c2561c8cee0b2/frontend/src/features/chat/useSerialPoll.ts#L10) rather than interpreting every wake as a full reload.
The diagnostics caller passes `open` with a 1,500 ms interval and no `wakeOn`;
`useSerialPoll` suppresses hidden reads and drains the actual request after a UI
timeout. This bounded example is not an exhaustive timer audit or measured
performance finding. Guides: [module map](../docs/module-boundaries.md),
[reliability](../docs/ai-coding-reliability.md),
[network budgets](../docs/network-design-reference.md#8-resource-budgets-compatibility-and-performance).
Present selections: `node::runtime_work::`,
`node::account_sync::local_maintenance::` and `frontend-sync-reconciliation`
(`src/features/chat/useSerialPoll.test.ts`, `src/lib/readDeadline.test.ts`).

**E03 — Storage and startup.**
Desktop [spawn_node_runtime](https://github.com/OctopusGarage/mesh-talk/blob/e5133000ec8ea2375de81fdcf55c2561c8cee0b2/src-tauri/src/runtime_bootstrap.rs#L31) → `RuntimeStartup::bounded` → participant startup/Node →
[Node::open_with_profile_lease](https://github.com/OctopusGarage/mesh-talk/blob/e5133000ec8ea2375de81fdcf55c2561c8cee0b2/crates/mesh-talk-core/src/node/node.rs#L683) / bounded variant → [ProfileStorage::open_participant](https://github.com/OctopusGarage/mesh-talk/blob/e5133000ec8ea2375de81fdcf55c2561c8cee0b2/crates/mesh-talk-core/src/storage/profile/context.rs#L42) → participant database bootstrap.
[EncryptedDatabase SQLCipher configuration](https://github.com/OctopusGarage/mesh-talk/blob/e5133000ec8ea2375de81fdcf55c2561c8cee0b2/crates/mesh-talk-core/src/storage/database.rs#L253) configures encrypted connections, provenance, FULL synchronous and WAL.
[PersistentEventLog::open_profile](https://github.com/OctopusGarage/mesh-talk/blob/e5133000ec8ea2375de81fdcf55c2561c8cee0b2/crates/mesh-talk-core/src/eventlog/persist.rs#L41) selects the indexed event repository; the explicit standalone `open`
retains a legacy backend using [EncryptedRecordLog](https://github.com/OctopusGarage/mesh-talk/blob/e5133000ec8ea2375de81fdcf55c2561c8cee0b2/crates/mesh-talk-core/src/storage/record_log.rs#L37). Do not generalize the legacy record
log's full visitor traversal to all desktop history. Conversely, do not claim
all stores have migrated merely because one indexed database exists.
Guides: [architecture](../docs/ARCHITECTURE.md) and
[backup/recovery](../docs/backup-recovery.md). The core crate README's broad
all-sidecar record-log description needs store-by-store reconciliation against
these current paths (T034/T037), not a storage rewrite in T001.
Present selection: `core-storage` (Rust `storage::`, `node::received_log::tests::`,
`node::sentlog::tests::`); process suite `persistent_history`.

**E04 — History, search, retention and erasure.**
[historyFor](https://github.com/OctopusGarage/mesh-talk/blob/e5133000ec8ea2375de81fdcf55c2561c8cee0b2/frontend/src/store/conversationHistory.ts#L124) requests account owner history or channel history with a default
200-entry page; host messaging/owner adapters delegate to [Node::account_history](https://github.com/OctopusGarage/mesh-talk/blob/e5133000ec8ea2375de81fdcf55c2561c8cee0b2/crates/mesh-talk-core/src/node/queries.rs#L88) and core
projections. [SearchDialog search request](https://github.com/OctopusGarage/mesh-talk/blob/e5133000ec8ea2375de81fdcf55c2561c8cee0b2/frontend/src/features/chat/SearchDialog.tsx#L103) → `chat.searchRecent` → [owner_search_recent](https://github.com/OctopusGarage/mesh-talk/blob/e5133000ec8ea2375de81fdcf55c2561c8cee0b2/src-tauri/src/owner_commands/search.rs#L123) → [Node::search_recent_limited](https://github.com/OctopusGarage/mesh-talk/blob/e5133000ec8ea2375de81fdcf55c2561c8cee0b2/crates/mesh-talk-core/src/node/search.rs#L101).
Recent search matches case-insensitive substrings in recent per-conversation
windows; host count/serialized-byte caps exist. The source explicitly says
retained metadata scanning can remain proportional to history: this is an
investigation input, not measured cost or a chosen index replacement.
[Node::delete_message](https://github.com/OctopusGarage/mesh-talk/blob/e5133000ec8ea2375de81fdcf55c2561c8cee0b2/crates/mesh-talk-core/src/node/lifecycle.rs#L42) and [ConversationPersonalState](https://github.com/OctopusGarage/mesh-talk/blob/e5133000ec8ea2375de81fdcf55c2561c8cee0b2/crates/mesh-talk-core/src/node/account_documents/personal.rs#L9) distinguish local erasure and account-scoped
personal state/floors; recall, favorites and synchronized ciphertext have separate
owners. Retention pruning is adapted by `src-tauri/src/settings.rs`.
Guides: [recent-search references](../docs/ARCHITECTURE.md#recent-search-references),
[history](../docs/help/topics/history.md), [favorites](../docs/favorites.md).
Present selectors: `core-search-references` (`node::search::tests::`),
`desktop-search` (`owner_commands::tests::registered_search_recent_and_exact_context_shapes`),
`frontend-search`, `frontend-history` (`src/store/conversationHistory.test.ts`).
T008 must inspect anti-resurrection, marker growth and recovery in depth; these
entry points do not establish their universal correctness.

**E05 — Account/group sync and authority.**
Frontend [chat account-group adapter](https://github.com/OctopusGarage/mesh-talk/blob/e5133000ec8ea2375de81fdcf55c2561c8cee0b2/frontend/src/lib/api/chat.ts#L295) and `store/outgoingIntent/groupOperations.ts` submit through
[AccountGroupControlRequest](https://github.com/OctopusGarage/mesh-talk/blob/e5133000ec8ea2375de81fdcf55c2561c8cee0b2/src-tauri/src/owner_commands/group_operations.rs#L22) to core account-group operations. [AccountGroupOperationPhase](https://github.com/OctopusGarage/mesh-talk/blob/e5133000ec8ea2375de81fdcf55c2561c8cee0b2/crates/mesh-talk-core/src/node/account_group/operations.rs#L376) distinguishes waiting,
acceptance, reconciliation and committed outcomes; it is not simply a sent flag.
[OwnerControlInput](https://github.com/OctopusGarage/mesh-talk/blob/e5133000ec8ea2375de81fdcf55c2561c8cee0b2/crates/mesh-talk-core/src/node/channels/owner_control.rs#L17) prepares owner effects; `channel_account_controls.rs` delegates
membership mutations to that owner. [AccountDocumentDomain](https://github.com/OctopusGarage/mesh-talk/blob/e5133000ec8ea2375de81fdcf55c2561c8cee0b2/crates/mesh-talk-core/src/node/account_documents/mod.rs#L27), `account_documents/store.rs`,
`account_documents/sync.rs` and `account_sync.rs` own typed documents, persistence
and sibling exchange; eventlog sync, privacy admission and relay transport remain
separate. No inspected rename/history-policy/member control is proof of a
complete announcement feature. Guides:
[network flows](../docs/network-design-reference.md#5-concrete-data-flows),
[groups](../docs/help/topics/channels.md), [linked devices](../docs/help/topics/link-devices.md).
Present contracts: `core-account-group-operations`, `core-account-documents`,
`core-channel-account-membership`, `desktop-account-group-inventory`;
representative Rust selectors `node::account_group::`,
`node::account_documents::`, `node::account_sync::`; process suites
`channel_peer_recovery`, `channel_mixed_version`, `post_office_offline`.
These have not been run for this inventory. T008 owns deep causal/confirmation,
partition/restart/deletion and old-binary assessment.

**E06 — Privacy, identity and trust.**
Frontend `store/privacy.ts` → [privacy IPC adapter](https://github.com/OctopusGarage/mesh-talk/blob/e5133000ec8ea2375de81fdcf55c2561c8cee0b2/frontend/src/lib/api/privacy.ts#L10) → [set_privacy_allowed](https://github.com/OctopusGarage/mesh-talk/blob/e5133000ec8ea2375de81fdcf55c2561c8cee0b2/src-tauri/src/privacy_commands.rs#L106) → [PrivacyPolicy](https://github.com/OctopusGarage/mesh-talk/blob/e5133000ec8ea2375de81fdcf55c2561c8cee0b2/crates/mesh-talk-core/src/node/privacy.rs#L75) and runtime
admission. Private [TrustRecord](https://github.com/OctopusGarage/mesh-talk/blob/e5133000ec8ea2375de81fdcf55c2561c8cee0b2/src-tauri/src/trust.rs#L17) records manual verification separately from first
observation; signed [TrustCard](https://github.com/OctopusGarage/mesh-talk/blob/e5133000ec8ea2375de81fdcf55c2561c8cee0b2/crates/mesh-talk-core/src/node/trust_card.rs#L54) authenticates profile fields, not real-world trust
or a public endorsement score. Core identity/ratchet/channel/transport owners
protect content independently of UI hiding. Guides:
[privacy controls](../docs/privacy-controls.md), [peer trust](../docs/peer-trust.md),
[relay metadata privacy](../docs/post-office-metadata-privacy.md).
The latter explicitly retains connecting IP/device, pseudonymous mailbox,
size/timing visibility. That documented boundary is not a fresh cryptographic
audit. Present selectors: `desktop-privacy` (`privacy_commands::` plus queued
owner rejection controls), `node::privacy_sync::`,
`node::trust_card::indexed::tests::`; frontend
`src/features/chat/VerifyContactDialog.test.ts`. T007 must bind assets/adversaries
to exact wire/storage/log observations and distinguish trusted peer/relay behavior
from a LAN observer; no anonymity or anti-spam completeness claim is made.

**E07 — Core and application adapters.**
[core public module exports](https://github.com/OctopusGarage/mesh-talk/blob/e5133000ec8ea2375de81fdcf55c2561c8cee0b2/crates/mesh-talk-core/src/lib.rs#L32) exports UI-free protocol modules. `mesh-talk-node` and the desktop
participant runtime consume core behavior; [IntegrationHost](https://github.com/OctopusGarage/mesh-talk/blob/e5133000ec8ea2375de81fdcf55c2561c8cee0b2/crates/mesh-talk-integrations/src/service.rs#L23) supplies admitted operations
to `IntegrationService`. Desktop `src-tauri/src/integrations.rs` binds session
leases. [MessagingServer](https://github.com/OctopusGarage/mesh-talk/blob/e5133000ec8ea2375de81fdcf55c2561c8cee0b2/crates/mesh-talk-mcp/src/lib.rs#L52) wraps `LocalClient` calls for context, conversations, sending and
send-result; IPC/HTTP delegate grants and durable acceptance to the same service.
[HTTP dispatch](https://github.com/OctopusGarage/mesh-talk/blob/e5133000ec8ea2375de81fdcf55c2561c8cee0b2/crates/mesh-talk-integrations/src/http.rs#L224) explicitly rejects browser-origin/fetch requests, matches fixed routes
and authenticates scoped credentials; it is not a browser-share server or a
mobile relay gateway. Guides: [core embedding](../crates/mesh-talk-core/README.md),
[bot integrations](../docs/bot-integrations.md), [module map](../docs/module-boundaries.md).
Present selectors: integration `service::`, `http::tests::`, `ipc::`, `host::`;
MCP `tests::`; desktop `integrations::`; core `two_node_cli` process target.

## Deliberate design boundaries

- **Pairing authorization:** a one-time 128-bit code binds the linker and joiner
  device keys. Durable enrollment invalidates old sessions; interrupted adoption
  has a restricted code-authenticated retry. There is no separate SAS ceremony.
- **Relay metadata:** production relays store opaque outer events, not readable
  original authors, conversation IDs or channel controls. Connection identities,
  pseudonymous mailboxes, size buckets and timing remain observable. See
  [the exact privacy boundary](../docs/post-office-metadata-privacy.md).
- **Bounded custody:** relay copies have capacity limits and a 30-day maximum age;
  this is not guaranteed minimum retention or permanent storage.
- **Connections:** the client Node has bounded sequential session reuse, not one
  multiplexed socket per relay or an eight-socket ceiling for the whole machine.
- **Reachability and trust:** Tailscale does not merge LANs; explicit relay trust
  and client directory consent are independent of routing.
- **Membership presentation:** removed group members' past reactions no longer
  render under the current-membership visibility rule.
- **Linux dependency constraint:** the maintained
  [GLib compatibility workflow](../.github/workflows/glib-0.20-watch.yml) tracks the
  GTK/Tauri dependency gate. Consult the lockfile and security configuration before
  changing versions; do not treat this note as a vulnerability waiver.

The [implementation/evidence tracker](../docs/network-design-reference.md#implementation-and-evidence-tracker)
records named logical and physical checks. Three independent physical LANs, a
separate ordinary client host on the mini's LAN, native macOS WebView media and
physical camera/microphone quality remain distinct acceptance cases.

New protocol capabilities such as true multiplexing, automatic federation trust,
mailbox-backed calling, TURN or stronger replicated-storage guarantees require
an explicit design and new evidence. They are not implied by the implemented
capabilities above.

projections. Recent search matches case-insensitive substrings in recent per-conversation
windows; host count/serialized-byte caps exist. The source explicitly says
retained metadata scanning can remain proportional to history: this is an
investigation input, not measured cost or a chosen index replacement.
[Node::delete_message](https://github.com/OctopusGarage/mesh-talk/blob/e5133000ec8ea2375de81fdcf55c2561c8cee0b2/crates/mesh-talk-core/src/node/lifecycle.rs#L42) and [ConversationPersonalState](https://github.com/OctopusGarage/mesh-talk/blob/e5133000ec8ea2375de81fdcf55c2561c8cee0b2/crates/mesh-talk-core/src/node/account_documents/personal.rs#L9) distinguish local erasure and account-scoped
personal state/floors; recall, favorites and synchronized ciphertext have separate
owners. Retention pruning is adapted by `src-tauri/src/settings.rs`.

[history](../docs/help/topics/history.md), [favorites](../docs/favorites.md).

`account_documents/sync.rs` and `account_sync.rs` own typed documents, persistence
and sibling exchange; eventlog sync, privacy admission and relay transport remain

complete announcement feature. Guides:

**E06 — Privacy, identity and trust.**
Frontend `store/privacy.ts` → [privacy IPC adapter](https://github.com/OctopusGarage/mesh-talk/blob/e5133000ec8ea2375de81fdcf55c2561c8cee0b2/frontend/src/lib/api/privacy.ts#L10) → [set_privacy_allowed](https://github.com/OctopusGarage/mesh-talk/blob/e5133000ec8ea2375de81fdcf55c2561c8cee0b2/src-tauri/src/privacy_commands.rs#L106) → [PrivacyPolicy](https://github.com/OctopusGarage/mesh-talk/blob/e5133000ec8ea2375de81fdcf55c2561c8cee0b2/crates/mesh-talk-core/src/node/privacy.rs#L75) and runtime
admission. Private [TrustRecord](https://github.com/OctopusGarage/mesh-talk/blob/e5133000ec8ea2375de81fdcf55c2561c8cee0b2/src-tauri/src/trust.rs#L17) records manual verification separately from first

or a public endorsement score. Core identity/ratchet/channel/transport owners
protect content independently of UI hiding. Guides:
[privacy controls](../docs/privacy-controls.md), [peer trust](../docs/peer-trust.md),
[relay metadata privacy](../docs/post-office-metadata-privacy.md).
The latter explicitly retains connecting IP/device, pseudonymous mailbox,
size/timing visibility. That documented boundary is not a fresh cryptographic
audit. Present selectors: `desktop-privacy` (`privacy_commands::` plus queued

`src/features/chat/VerifyContactDialog.test.ts`. T007 must bind assets/adversaries
to exact wire/storage/log observations and distinguish trusted peer/relay behavior

participant runtime consume core behavior; [IntegrationHost](https://github.com/OctopusGarage/mesh-talk/blob/e5133000ec8ea2375de81fdcf55c2561c8cee0b2/crates/mesh-talk-integrations/src/service.rs#L23) supplies admitted operations

send-result; IPC/HTTP delegate grants and durable acceptance to the same service.
[HTTP dispatch](https://github.com/OctopusGarage/mesh-talk/blob/e5133000ec8ea2375de81fdcf55c2561c8cee0b2/crates/mesh-talk-integrations/src/http.rs#L224) explicitly rejects browser-origin/fetch requests, matches fixed routes

mobile relay gateway. Guides: [core embedding](../crates/mesh-talk-core/README.md),
[bot integrations](../docs/bot-integrations.md), [module map](../docs/module-boundaries.md).

MCP `tests::`; desktop `integrations::`; core `two_node_cli` process target.
Independent SDK clients, arbitrary GUI/TUI parity and concurrent-client authority

**E08 — Calls.**
[useCalls](https://github.com/OctopusGarage/mesh-talk/blob/e5133000ec8ea2375de81fdcf55c2561c8cee0b2/frontend/src/store/calls.ts#L192) → `frontend/src/lib/api/calls.ts` → [send_call_signal command](https://github.com/OctopusGarage/mesh-talk/blob/e5133000ec8ea2375de81fdcf55c2561c8cee0b2/src-tauri/src/chat_commands/messaging.rs#L38) → [Node::send_call_signal_if](https://github.com/OctopusGarage/mesh-talk/blob/e5133000ec8ea2375de81fdcf55c2561c8cee0b2/crates/mesh-talk-core/src/node/call.rs#L70),

and policy work. The convenience `send_call_signal` wrapper is not this desktop
call path. Authenticated inbound signals return through runtime events. The call store owns

Guide: [image handling](../docs/help/topics/send-files.md) and
[privacy](../docs/privacy-controls.md). Present baseline selectors:
`frontend-inline-media`, `frontend-image-live-text`

**E10 — Profiles, saved/forwarded records and external copies.**
`AccountProfilePanel` consumes `store/accountProfiles.ts` and
`lib/api/accountProfile.ts`; signed account profile documents use E05/E06.

**E11 — Verification and feedback ownership.**
The six maintained `validation.json` files contain 175 contracts at this source:

owns cost/reliability decisions. Existing owners include
[CodeQL](../.github/workflows/codeql.yml), [fuzz](../.github/workflows/fuzz.yml),
[sanitizers](../.github/workflows/sanitizers.yml),
[mutation](../.github/workflows/mutants.yml), [fuzz inputs](../fuzz/README.md),

`scripts/diagnostics/ci-timing-report.test.mjs`.

`src-tauri/src/lib.rs` registers native commands, events and OS integration;
`scripts/release/package-app.sh` and [updates](../docs/updates.md) own packaging.
No comparative asset-size or alternative-UI benchmark was run. Existing release
regressions include `scripts/diagnostics/release-assets.test.mjs` and
`scripts/diagnostics/release-sevenzip.test.mjs`; these are packaging regressions,

[PROJECT.md](../PROJECT.md) → [documentation map](../docs/README.md) →
[roadmap](../docs/development-roadmap.md) routes work. [CONTEXT.md](../CONTEXT.md)
owns terms, [domain design](../docs/domain-design.md) owns model/naming translation,
[module boundaries](../docs/module-boundaries.md) owns implementation paths and
[documentation guidelines](../docs/DOCUMENTATION_GUIDELINES.md) owns placement.
E05's operation phases and E07's host/core separation give concrete consumers of
those distinctions. Existing [settled network decisions](../docs/network-design-reference.md#9-settled-decisions-and-acceptance-evidence)
and the deliberate boundaries below contain rationale/limits; roadmap decisions
retain unanswered questions. Structural standards/links can check navigation,
not semantic completeness. The [decision lookup](../docs/development-roadmap.md#decision-lookup-and-reassessment)
connects supported rationale, Unknown history, current decision state and proposed
revisit conditions to these existing owners. It does not introduce a second
protocol contract or make an unrecorded historical choice. The roadmap claim
table is the single local integration record; T037 owns any confirmed
component-document mismatch.

### Known limits and refresh responsibilities

- T001 is a bounded static map, **independently reviewed and locally accepted as input**, not a

  T007/T008 own deep privacy/sync investigations; T004/T005 own runtime/validation
  measurements. Revalidate pinned evidence against each new accepted base.
- At this snapshot [PR #376](https://github.com/OctopusGarage/mesh-talk/pull/376)
  (CI/notification/mailbox work) and
  [PR #381](https://github.com/OctopusGarage/mesh-talk/pull/381)
  (custody retry/reception-source work) were open. They are pending changes, not
  main evidence. T005/T008 must inspect their final source before overlapping
  proposals; do not adopt them implicitly or change their owners' work.
- Source suggests bounded work and correctness mechanisms, but establishes no
  current CPU/memory/disk/energy result. Full app-family membership, representative
  seeded workload, cold/warm environment and repeated return-to-idle evidence are
  still missing (T003/T004). Existing instrumentation overhead is unmeasured.
- Search metadata growth, deletion floors/marker compaction, offline authority and
  compatibility are explicit follow-ups, not defects established by this map.
  Existing native/topology limits remain in the owning network evidence tracker.
- There is no new feature/test/workflow/product edit in T001. Later bounded evidence-task authorization and unique claims are recorded in the
  roadmap; this inventory itself authorizes no downstream implementation, external
  publication or main merge.

## Deliberate design boundaries

- **Pairing authorization:** a one-time 128-bit code binds the linker and joiner
  device keys. Durable enrollment invalidates old sessions; interrupted adoption
  has a restricted code-authenticated retry. There is no separate SAS ceremony.
- **Relay metadata:** production relays store opaque outer events, not readable
  original authors, conversation IDs or channel controls. Connection identities,
  pseudonymous mailboxes, size buckets and timing remain observable. See
  [the exact privacy boundary](../docs/post-office-metadata-privacy.md).
- **Bounded custody:** relay copies have capacity limits and a 30-day maximum age;
  this is not guaranteed minimum retention or permanent storage.
- **Connections:** the client Node has bounded sequential session reuse, not one
  multiplexed socket per relay or an eight-socket ceiling for the whole machine.
- **Reachability and trust:** Tailscale does not merge LANs; explicit relay trust
  and client directory consent are independent of routing.
- **Membership presentation:** removed group members' past reactions no longer
  render under the current-membership visibility rule.
- **Linux dependency constraint:** the maintained
  [GLib compatibility workflow](../.github/workflows/glib-0.20-watch.yml) tracks the
  GTK/Tauri dependency gate. Consult the lockfile and security configuration before
  changing versions; do not treat this note as a vulnerability waiver.

## Evidence and future decisions

The [implementation/evidence tracker](../docs/network-design-reference.md#implementation-and-evidence-tracker)
records named logical and physical checks. Three independent physical LANs, a
separate ordinary client host on the mini's LAN, native macOS WebView media and
physical camera/microphone quality remain distinct acceptance cases.

New protocol capabilities such as true multiplexing, automatic federation trust,
mailbox-backed calling, TURN or stronger replicated-storage guarantees require
an explicit design and new evidence. They are not implied by the implemented
capabilities above.

REQ-001 — Built-in resource monitoring and performance visibility
- **Original user input (restored substantive text):** “第一个需求，现在整个app的性能感觉还是偏低，我希望给这个app建立自带的监控体系，仔细列出这个app的cpu，磁盘，网络等等消耗情况，具体界面的设计可以参考这种形式，用于持续监控，后续逐步往高性能低消耗的IM优化，因为空闲情况，启动时，以及使用期间，对于一个局域网im来说，不应该消耗那么多电脑资源的，现在感觉总莫名其名消耗很多资源，监控界面参考这个来实现”；“监控面板再电脑最上方的图标也可以显示，看起来很挺美观高级优雅的。”
- **Pain point or question:** The user reports unexpectedly high and unexplained resource use and a general perception of low performance. No measurements, root cause or confirmed defect established in this discussion.
- **Additional confirmed panel scope:** Provide an accessible panel showing Mesh Talk app-wide resource and operational metrics, including connection count, memory, write activity and latency to other nodes. Retain the earlier top-bar/menu-bar presentation request; the relationship between its compact view and the fuller panel remains to be designed. Prioritize existing data reuse and avoid extra acquisition cost.
- **Additional original panel clarification:** “应该有个面板，可以进去看到整个meshtalk app的监控指标，连接数，延迟之类的，内存，写入之类的，注意复用，不要增加额外成本 / 和其他节点的延迟之类的”。
- **Confirmed conclusions:**
  - Primary monitoring scope is Mesh Talk itself and its related processes. Whole-computer monitoring is not the primary requested scope.
  - Reuse existing data as much as possible; avoid separate or duplicate monitoring and unnecessary additional resource consumption.
  - Users must be able to disable monitoring work that incurs additional overhead to retain minimal resource use and power consumption.
  - Information already available without extra acquisition need not be disabled. This does not establish that displaying, aggregating or retaining it has zero overhead.
  - No concrete collection implementation or numeric performance budget agreed. Availability of reusable metrics and related-process attribution has not been verified against code.
- **Additional original user clarification:** “尽量复用已有的数据，尽量不应该另外单独监控，免得增加不必要的消耗，而且要支持关闭，这样用户可以保持最小低功耗，当然本来不需要额外获取的信息可以不用关。” Followed by: “主要监控 Mesh Talk 自身及其相关进程”。
- **Visual reference:** [Attached reference image](references/req-001-monitoring-reference.jpg). It shows a macOS menu-bar entry and compact dark/translucent dropdown with resource cards, small charts and a process table. These are observed reference characteristics, not individually confirmed requirements. Whole-machine temperatures, fan controls, battery and cleanup actions visible in the reference are not automatically in scope. Original link: https://x.com/HiTw93/status/2116890236320092498?a=xiwtWvIa7enA_OlbL1Q&s=20 . The link could not be retrieved; visual observations rely on the supplied image.
- **Open questions:**
  1. Which related processes can be reliably attributed to Mesh Talk, and which requested metrics already have reusable data?
  2. What connection-count and peer-latency definitions should be shown, and what existing sources and freshness information can be reused? Requested metrics now explicitly include memory and write activity.
  3. Does continuous monitoring require history across restarts, export or only current-session trends? What sampling and retention are appropriate?
  4. Which operating systems need the menu-bar/tray panel, and what should its compact icon display?
  5. What representative hardware, idle conditions, startup boundaries and active-use scenarios should define later baselines and measurable targets?
  6. Should additional monitoring default to off or on? Should the choice persist across restarts, and should optional acquisition be controlled globally or by metric?

REQ-002 — LAN sharing and collaboration tool exploration
- **Original user input:** “第二个需求，应该是功能想法，不一定完全按照以下描述，大概是可以头脑风暴，看看有什么好的局域网工具可以在机遇这个app上开发”。
- **Pain point or question:** Which LAN collaboration tools would meaningfully complement Mesh Talk? The primary scenario is now confirmed as browser-based viewing and commenting; detailed workflow friction remains to be clarified.
- **Confirmed conclusions:**
  - Primary scenario: colleagues need no Mesh Talk installation and use a browser to view and comment on shared content.
  - Multi-user editing remains a direction for later discussion, outside the currently confirmed primary scenario. Native workspaces and external-tool integrations have not been selected.
  - The sharer can configure either link-only access or link plus an access code. Per-person approval is not a primary scenario. No default mode has been chosen.
  - Commenter identity and whether viewing/commenting permissions are separate remain open; do not add an account or per-person approval requirement to the confirmed browser entry flow.
  - Keep this session in requirements collection and clarification; do not begin development.
  - Content formats, detailed permission behavior, transport and update semantics remain undecided. The inspiration need not be implemented literally.
- **Additional original user clarification:** “先以‘同事无需安装 Mesh Talk，通过浏览器查看和评论我分享的内容’为主要场景，多人编辑保留为待讨论方向。请据此更新 REQ-002，继续澄清关键边界，暂不进入开发。”
- **Open questions:**
  1. Which content families should the main scenario cover: images/PDFs, Markdown/text, HTML/slides bundles, or another concrete format?
  2. Should comments be general discussion, page/slide-specific, or precise region/text annotations?
  3. Is sharing a published snapshot or a live-updating source, and what happens to comments when content changes?
  4. How are commenters identified, and should comments persist, support replies or be moderated?
  5. What are the default access mode, separate view/comment permissions and expiry/code-change/revocation behavior for already-open sessions?
  6. What happens when the host sleeps/exits or the LAN address changes, and how do visitors recover?

        Ok(())
    }
}

from pathlib import Path

s=p.read_text()

The current instruction authorizes evidence\nreconciliation, task-state updates and reprioritization only; product code remains\nout of scope. Existing local evidence work must be preserved and refreshed before\nreuse. The user accepted consolidation into 23 work',1)
s=s.replace('- [Delivery phases](#delivery-phases)','- [Current evidence and execution order](#current-evidence-and-execution-order)\n- [Delivery phases](#delivery-phases)',1)
marker='## Delivery phases\n'
section='''## Current evidence and execution order

This assessment uses product `main` / fetched `origin/main`
`82b8a67eaf160ca43695b3cb741f13d2c3817722` (checked 2026-11-20,
Asia/Singapore), the thirty records in the user-supplied
`/Users/kingsonwu/Downloads/requirements-intake.md`, and the existing local P0
integration tip `e8bba6483511f950170c808a651ba0c2025c56c2` on
`ao/hello-greeting/p0-docs-integration`. The intake remains historical provenance;
its repeated collection-stage restrictions describe the earlier stage. This
instruction opens analysis, not product implementation. The source mapping below
preserves all thirty requirements and their confirmed boundaries.

### T001 evidence refresh and integration boundary

[The capability index](../specifications/TODO.md#roadmap-foundations-and-evidence-boundaries)
records current foundations and representative owners. The existing local branch
already contains a more detailed T001 map and T002/T003/T005/T006 evidence, plus
T004 readiness work. Inspect its exact committed documents with
`git show e8bba648:specifications/TODO.md` and
`git show e8bba648:docs/development-roadmap.md`; these commits are local evidence,
not published GitHub references. Preserve their review/provenance record. This
refresh does not copy that branch wholesale, reassign its claim or endorse every
historical conclusion.

The local evidence uses product baseline `e5133000`. Five later main commits
(#376, #382, #383, #385, #386) change 178 files, including diagnostics, delivery,
relay repair, membership, history/search, media and CI. Therefore:

- Retain the existing source inventory as a starting input; refresh changed
  symbols, callers, test selectors, failure assertions and measurement artifacts.
- The old pending-PR statements are stale. #376 is now merged; no open PRs or
  open issues were returned by the repository queries during this assessment.
  Neither result releases a local task claim or proves another session is idle.
- Recheck T004 candidate/build identity: old Stable artifacts cannot establish
  current-main runtime cost. Preserve historical measurements separately if any
  become available; none were executed in this reconciliation.
- Do not reuse the old count of 175 validation contracts as a current count.
  Relevant `validation.json` files changed. Existing test/source presence and
  historical reviews are not fresh acceptance results.

T001 now has a refreshed static input, with integration/review still open.
T002 has refreshed claim routing below. T003/T005/T006 have prior local inputs to
reconcile, not newly completed tasks. T004 still lacks a measured baseline;
T007/T008 still need dedicated deep investigations; T009 cannot select a proven
performance fix yet. No task checkbox is closed by this document-only refresh.

### Consolidation and splitting decisions

Keep **30 source requirements, 23 topics and 74 stable task IDs**. Merge common
investigation and ownership, not distinct authority, acceptance or product
choices. No extra umbrella rewrite, new SDK program or duplicate monitoring/test
system is justified by this reassessment.

| Source requirements | Organization and ordering decision | Delivery boundary / reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| REQ-001, REQ-011, REQ-016 | Share T003/T004 evidence and existing budget owner; split source/control design T026, panel/tray T027 and regression evals T028. | Measure before choosing optimizations; a finished monitoring UI is not required to profile the app. User alerts/default sampling/history remain decisions. |
| REQ-003, REQ-030 | One validation program: T005 timing/failures and T006 risk/assertion coverage, then T010/T038. | Keep timing collection and coverage analysis independently reviewable. Faster gates require preserved detection evidence; tool installation is not an outcome. |
| REQ-004, REQ-009, REQ-022 | Shared T001 inventory; separate T002 decision/claim lookup and T037/T070 maintained explanations. | Domain/component ownership and decision reasons are related outputs, not three inventories or a required rewrite. Unknown historical rationale stays unknown. |
| REQ-005, REQ-006, REQ-017 | Share runtime evidence; retain separate scheduling, I/O, startup, memory, retention, sync-range, deletion and marker tasks T011–T019/T074. | Loading/caching optimization does not authorize cleanup; marker reduction needs anti-resurrection proof. Existing scheduling rules already apply while later refinements wait. |
| REQ-008, REQ-015, REQ-018 | One internal-foundation topic; separate personal/group sync, announcements, member authority and targeted interface work. | T008 authority/lifecycle evidence precedes affected changes. T022/T072 announcements and T023/T073 membership are different decisions and delivery units; Raft is not selected. |
| REQ-007, REQ-012, REQ-014 | Keep storage suitability, UI comparison and package size separate. | Artifact comparison T033 can proceed without a UI/database migration; T034/T035 need representative runtime evidence. T036 remains conditional P3. |
| REQ-013, REQ-025 | Privacy/exposure T007 precedes affected protection/contact-policy decisions; practical anti-harassment T031/T032 stays P1. | Hidden contacts, transport admission and account blocking differ. Endorsements T066 remain P3 and cannot delay practical protection or grant rights. |
| REQ-002, REQ-010, REQ-023 | Independent bounded P2 lanes: browser review, manual QR and group voice. | Separate view/comments from simultaneous editing; QR encoding is not recognition; one-to-one calls are not group meetings. None requires a global sync rewrite. |
| REQ-019, REQ-024, REQ-026 | Merge forum and forum forwarding; keep selected-contact feed/profile separate. | Forum audience/expiry/pinning/ranking/forwarding are distinct contracts. Do not apply three-day forum expiry to chats or personal feeds. All remain P3. |
| REQ-020, REQ-021, REQ-027 | Separate internal clients, external SDK, marketplace and mobile work. Bring only existing-PWA branch feasibility T047 forward. | CLI/MCP/core already exist; browser pairing/key/transport gaps need evidence. PWA and another internal client need not wait for external SDK extraction or a marketplace. |
| REQ-028, REQ-029 | Keep incentives as conditional P3 and peer-tool discovery as bounded P2 research input. | Neither blocks messenger reliability. No points system, alternate radio or competitor feature is adopted without a demonstrated use case. |

### Immediate sequence and later parallel eligibility

The task table's hard inputs remain authoritative. The following order prioritizes
work that enables other tasks without inventing new global dependencies. Evidence
may be accepted per bounded slice; an unmerged historical input must first be
reconciled by its existing integration owner. These lanes are a dispatch proposal,
not active assignments or permission to start product changes.

| Order / lane | Next bounded output | Owner and conflict boundary | Readiness / remaining gate |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| First: T001/T002 reconciliation | Review the current-main delta, preserve existing local evidence/claims and accept the refreshed inventory/decision routes. | Existing P0 integrator; this session edits only the current-checkout roadmap and capability index for reconciliation. | Static refresh prepared; review/integration open. Do not create a duplicate T004 claim. |
| P0 runtime: T003 → T004 | Reconcile scenario/build/dataset/process identity, then comparable startup/idle/active/return-to-idle measurements. | Existing mesh-talk-2 T004/performance-guide writer; reserve native measurement windows. | Prior scenario/readiness inputs exist; current-source artifact, reproducible workload and usable metrics need qualification. No new app/profiling run in this pass. |
| P0 validation: T005 and T006 | Refresh timing/failure sample and method-to-risk/assertion applicability; hand off a small finding list. | Existing integration writer for testing-feedback-loop.md / ci-maintenance.md; timing and assertion inspection can be read-only lanes. | Prior local evidence exists; update changed selectors/runner source, include failed attempts and missing logs. No gate changes or reruns. |
| P0 privacy: T007 | Asset/observer/peer/relay/storage/log exposure matrix with verified, partial and unknown claims. | Unclaimed; propose one privacy evidence owner, coordinating shared network-guide edits. | Can investigate alongside T008 after acceptance of relevant T001 inputs. No anonymity or cryptographic audit completion claim. |
| P0 sync: T008 | Trace authority, pending/committed transitions, personal/group replay, deletion and recovery/compatibility. | Unclaimed; propose one sync evidence owner; share read-only facts with T007. | Refresh recent delivery/relay/membership changes first; deep partition, stale/revoked and restore cases remain open. |
| First P1 preparation | After accepted relevant inputs, prepare T016/T022/T023/T031 contracts; compare T033 artifacts and inspect T047 existing work independently. | Storage/group/privacy owners coordinate shared interfaces; artifact/PWA inspection owns no product mutations. | These enable later delivery but do not all wait for T009; implementation remains outside current authorization. |
| T009 / first delivery choice | Rank a small slice by measured user impact, correctness risk, invariant, scope and acceptance. Prefer practical IM/feedback improvements over speculative platform work. | Integration/product owner, using accepted T004/T005/T006/T007/T008 outputs. | Needs evidence. Urgent verified security/data-loss/freeze findings retain the existing override. |
| Later P2 / parked P3 | P2 only when its contract and reviewer capacity are ready. Keep T036/T046/T053–T068 as conditional future work. | No new claims; named product/authority owner required at promotion. | P3 revisit requires a real scenario/consumer, accepted privacy/authority/resource model and an independently testable slice. No dates or short-term implementation promise. |

P1 preparation is a priority emphasis, not a new P0 classification. Do not start
all P1 tasks or demand completion of the whole M1 program before every safe,
independent decision. Keep runtime profiling free from build/test noise; one
writer integrates shared documents. The evidence pass launches no parallel agents.

### Validation-latency lead, not a root-cause finding

Current-head [CI run 44679794705](https://github.com/OctopusGarage/mesh-talk/actions/runs/44679794705)
reported success. Its Jobs API records `Produce sealed remaining workspace
archive` on macOS from 05:25:05 to 06:03:19 UTC (**38m14s**), before
`macOS remaining tests (2/2)`'s four-worker execution from 06:04:45 to
06:16:22 (**11m37s**). The Linux sealed-workspace-archive step ran
05:25:10–05:35:36 (**10m26s**). These are observed named-step spans, not a
controlled compile benchmark, queue-time attribution or a summed critical path.
They make archive production an early T005 inspection candidate; inspect its
logs, dependencies and comparable attempts before changing concurrency or gates.
One successful main run cannot establish flake rate, cache effectiveness,
local-publication latency or a product performance root cause. Detailed timing
analysis stays in the existing validation owners, not another permanent report.

'''
s=s.replace(marker,section+marker,1)
s=s.replace('All tasks start **unclaimed** and **not started**. Claim readiness is calculated','The initial backlog started **unclaimed** and **not started**. Existing local\nclaims and evidence now take precedence over that initial state; see the claim\ntable and current evidence section. Claim readiness is calculated',1)

| T003 | Original mesh-talk-4; integrated by mesh-talk-2 | Same integration branch; source `00907b30` | docs/performance-requirements.md, existing integrator | Prior scenario input; refresh candidate/source identity before T004 | Historical local review only; no current runtime acceptance |
| T004 | mesh-talk-2, sole recorded ongoing owner | Same integration branch; readiness source `59943286`, continuation tip `e8bba648` | Performance guide and compact roadmap state; preserve unique writer | Needs evidence: no measured baseline established; continue through existing owner | No reassignment or new measurement by this session |
| T005/T006 | Original mesh-talk-3; integrated by mesh-talk-2 | Same integration branch; sources `0882d213` / `4219bd16` | docs/testing-feedback-loop.md and docs/ci-maintenance.md | Historical local inputs; current timing/selector/assertion reconciliation remains | Local review recorded on branch; not Merged/Validated on current main |
| T007/T008 | Unclaimed in inspected records | No new branch | Privacy/sync guide owners proposed; no product paths claimed | Ready for bounded investigation after relevant inventory acceptance | No deep audit completed |
| T009 | Unclaimed | No new branch | Integration decision only | Needs evidence from T004/T005/T006/T007/T008 | No implementation slice selected |'''

requested refinements. **Partial** means foundations exist but do not cover the
whole request. **Missing in inspected entry** is a bounded source observation,
not a claim about all branches. **Unknown** needs a dedicated investigation.
Representative test files/selectors below are present-source leads, not tests
executed in this pass. No user messages, app runtime, native measurement or
product test run was needed for this static reconciliation.

Paths below use `core/` for `crates/mesh-talk-core/src/` and `ui/` for

implementation boundaries; this table does not introduce new owners.

| Topic | Current foundation | Representative owner → consumer / evidence boundary |

Last-seen age is not peer latency; panel/tray and added-cost controls remain unqualified. |
| WORK-02 Performance budgets | Partial | [Performance requirements](../docs/performance-requirements.md) already define startup/idle/active and return-to-idle rules. `core/node/work_observation.rs` and `core/storage/database/observation.rs` provide optional attribution; they do not establish OS physical disk/energy or current budget compliance. |

Existing tests include `useSerialPoll.test.ts`; source presence does not establish every timer is necessary or costly. |
| WORK-04 History/lifecycles | Partial | `ui/store/conversationHistory.ts` defaults to 200 entries → host adapters → `core/node/queries.rs`; `search.rs` documents recent windows and O(history) metadata. `account_suppression.rs` distinguishes indexed device-local deletion facts from legacy in-memory suppression. `conversationHistory.test.ts`, `search_tests.rs` exist; reclamation, marker growth and restore guarantees still need scenario evidence. |
| WORK-05 Domain/ownership | Implemented foundation | [Glossary](../CONTEXT.md), [domain design](../docs/domain-design.md) and [module map](../docs/module-boundaries.md) exist and route core/host/adapter/store/feature responsibilities. Read actual assertions and failures; contract/tool counts are not completeness or defect-detection rates. |
| WORK-08 Stack/storage | Partial | Desktop bootstrap → participant storage → `core/storage/profile/context.rs` / `database.rs`: SQLCipher through rusqlite, FULL synchronous and WAL are concrete current owners. Legacy record logs still exist. No workload comparison justifies replacement; inventory stores separately before changing documentation or persistence. |
| WORK-09 Desktop UI options | Partial | Tauri host + React client and native adapters exist. Alternative-shell resource, accessibility/IME and native parity have not been compared here; the request is a research decision, not an absent production shell. |
| WORK-10 Package size | Partial | Root Cargo release profile and `scripts/release/package-app.sh` own existing build/package behavior; [updates](../docs/updates.md) owns publication. No comparable download/installed-size measurements were collected in this pass. |
| WORK-11 Privacy | Partial | `ui/store/privacy.ts` → privacy adapter → `src-tauri/src/privacy_commands.rs` → `core/node/privacy.rs` and runtime admission. [Relay metadata privacy](../docs/post-office-metadata-privacy.md) preserves explicit IP/identity/timing exposure. Existing `privacy.test.ts` / `privacy_runtime_tests.rs` are not a new threat-model audit or anonymity proof. |
| WORK-12 Anti-harassment | Partial | Existing disclosure permission, manual verification and contact hiding have distinct owners. [Privacy](../docs/privacy-controls.md) / [peer trust](../docs/peer-trust.md) are inputs; hidden contacts do not establish account-wide transport blocking, stranger quarantine or published endorsements. |

REQ-001 — Built-in resource monitoring and performance visibility

- **Discussion state:** Clarifying.
- **Captured / updated:** 2026-11-17 (Asia/Singapore).
- **Original user input (restored substantive text):** “第一个需求，现在整个app的性能感觉还是偏低，我希望给这个app建立自带的监控体系，仔细列出这个app的cpu，磁盘，网络等等消耗情况，具体界面的设计可以参考这种形式，用于持续监控，后续逐步往高性能低消耗的IM优化，因为空闲情况，启动时，以及使用期间，对于一个局域网im来说，不应该消耗那么多电脑资源的，现在感觉总莫名其名消耗很多资源，监控界面参考这个来实现”；“监控面板再电脑最上方的图标也可以显示，看起来很挺美观高级优雅的。”
- **Scenario and affected users:** Desktop users observing resource consumption during startup, idle/background operation and active use of a LAN IM application.
- **Pain point or question:** The user reports unexpectedly high and unexplained resource use and a general perception of low performance. No measurements, root cause or confirmed defect established in this discussion.
- **Desired outcome:** Built-in continuous visibility into Mesh Talk resource consumption, supporting gradual optimization toward a high-performance, low-resource IM. An elegant monitoring surface accessible from an icon at the top of the desktop, following the supplied reference's visual direction.
- **Scope and constraints confirmed by user:** Monitor app CPU, memory, disk/write activity and network consumption, connection counts and latency to other nodes; exact metric definitions remain to clarify. Cover startup, idle and active-use scenarios. Include a desktop top-bar icon/panel presentation. Exact metrics, platforms, sampling cadence, history retention and performance targets remain unconfirmed.
- **Additional confirmed panel scope:** Provide an accessible panel showing Mesh Talk app-wide resource and operational metrics, including connection count, memory, write activity and latency to other nodes. Retain the earlier top-bar/menu-bar presentation request; the relationship between its compact view and the fuller panel remains to be designed. Prioritize existing data reuse and avoid extra acquisition cost.
- **Additional original panel clarification:** “应该有个面板，可以进去看到整个meshtalk app的监控指标，连接数，延迟之类的，内存，写入之类的，注意复用，不要增加额外成本 / 和其他节点的延迟之类的”。
- **Confirmed conclusions:**
  - Primary monitoring scope is Mesh Talk itself and its related processes. Whole-computer monitoring is not the primary requested scope.
  - Reuse existing data as much as possible; avoid separate or duplicate monitoring and unnecessary additional resource consumption.
  - Users must be able to disable monitoring work that incurs additional overhead to retain minimal resource use and power consumption.
  - Information already available without extra acquisition need not be disabled. This does not establish that displaying, aggregating or retaining it has zero overhead.
  - No concrete collection implementation or numeric performance budget agreed. Availability of reusable metrics and related-process attribution has not been verified against code.
- **Additional original user clarification:** “尽量复用已有的数据，尽量不应该另外单独监控，免得增加不必要的消耗，而且要支持关闭，这样用户可以保持最小低功耗，当然本来不需要额外获取的信息可以不用关。” Followed by: “主要监控 Mesh Talk 自身及其相关进程”。
- **Assistant interpretation of the confirmed disable requirement — implementation details unconfirmed:** Disabling additional monitoring must stop its extra collection work, not merely hide the panel. Normal messaging operations and data they already produce remain available. The precise controls, defaults and persistence are still to be clarified.
- **Original attachment provenance:** `.ao/attachments/attachment-596fda23a933023bcbaa7e8a7be25d12.jpg`; preserved supporting copy at `references/req-001-monitoring-reference.jpg`.
- **Visual reference:** [Attached reference image](references/req-001-monitoring-reference.jpg). It shows a macOS menu-bar entry and compact dark/translucent dropdown with resource cards, small charts and a process table. These are observed reference characteristics, not individually confirmed requirements. Whole-machine temperatures, fan controls, battery and cleanup actions visible in the reference are not automatically in scope. Original link: https://x.com/HiTw93/status/2116890236320092498?a=xiwtWvIa7enA_OlbL1Q&s=20 . The link could not be retrieved; visual observations rely on the supplied image.
- **Assistant suggestions / assumptions — unconfirmed:**
  - Interpret the top-of-desktop icon as a macOS menu-bar entry; clarify Windows/Linux tray equivalents and supported platform scope later.
  - Define which backend, WebView and helper processes belong to Mesh Talk, avoiding omissions or double-counting. Primary app-and-related-process scope is confirmed; exact process accounting remains to be designed.
  - Candidate metrics: CPU utilization, memory footprint, disk read/write rates and accumulated I/O, app data/log/cache storage size, network send/receive rates and totals. Disk I/O and storage footprint should be distinguished. Memory tracking is now requested; rate/total definitions and storage-footprint inclusion remain unconfirmed.
  - Reuse existing connection/session state and already-observed communication timing where available. Do not add periodic ping traffic, duplicate connections or independent polling solely for this panel without resolving the added-cost trade-off.
  - Define whether connection count refers to transport sessions, connected devices or distinct accounts; they are not interchangeable. Define peer latency measurement semantics (for example transport RTT versus message acknowledgement time) and freshness. Do not present an absent or stale observation as current zero latency; metric availability is not yet verified.
  - Pair current readings with recent trends and startup/idle/active-use context to make spikes investigable. Historical recording/export, subsystem attribution and regression comparisons are optional proposals, not agreed scope.
  - Before implementation, inventory each metric's existing owner/source, availability, units and incremental cost. Reuse that source rather than add an independent collector. These are proposed implementation checks, not claims that such sources already exist.
  - If CPU/memory/disk or other required metrics lack reusable data, explicitly resolve the trade-off between optional acquisition and metric availability; do not imply that every metric can be obtained for free.
  - Use demand-driven panel refresh and bounded aggregation/history; avoid hidden-panel chart rendering and unnecessary menu-bar refresh. These are proposals requiring design validation.
  - Measure monitoring overhead, including display, aggregation and history writes, with enabled/disabled and panel-open/closed comparisons. Additional sampling, timers, recording and subscriptions introduced solely for optional monitoring should cease when disabled; exact boundaries remain to be designed.
  - Treat monitoring capability and subsequent measured optimization work as distinct outcomes within this discussion record; final task splitting and dependency planning remain deferred.
- **Open questions:**
  1. Which related processes can be reliably attributed to Mesh Talk, and which requested metrics already have reusable data?
  2. What connection-count and peer-latency definitions should be shown, and what existing sources and freshness information can be reused? Requested metrics now explicitly include memory and write activity.
  3. Does continuous monitoring require history across restarts, export or only current-session trends? What sampling and retention are appropriate?
  4. Which operating systems need the menu-bar/tray panel, and what should its compact icon display?
  5. What representative hardware, idle conditions, startup boundaries and active-use scenarios should define later baselines and measurable targets?
  6. Should additional monitoring default to off or on? Should the choice persist across restarts, and should optional acquisition be controlled globally or by metric?
- **Candidate acceptance criteria — unconfirmed:** Verify existing-source reuse and absence of duplicate collectors; demonstrate that disabling extra monitoring stops its work while normal messaging continues; account for related processes without double-counting. Clearly identify metric scope, units and measurement interval; cover startup/idle/active use; make app-wide resource metrics, connection count and per-node latency accessible in the monitoring panel, with the menu-bar/tray relationship to be designed; measure monitoring overhead; show unavailable metrics honestly rather than as zero. Numeric budgets and final criteria remain deferred.
- **Related records and evidence:** REQ-005 concerns event/scheduling reuse and REQ-006 redundant work/I/O; these links are context, not execution dependencies. The screenshot is visual evidence only; no performance profiling or source investigation performed. No specific optimization or root cause asserted.
- **Global planning:** Classification, priority, effort, dependency analysis, roadmap phase and branch allocation deferred until the user closes collection.


### REQ-002 — LAN sharing and collaboration tool exploration

- **Discussion state:** Clarifying; exploratory idea, not a fixed feature specification.
- **Captured / updated:** 2026-11-17 (Asia/Singapore).
- **Original user input:** “第二个需求，应该是功能想法，不一定完全按照以下描述，大概是可以头脑风暴，看看有什么好的局域网工具可以在机遇这个app上开发”。
- **User-supplied inspiration, not independently verified:** “baoyu-design 增加了局域网内的团队共享功能，现在你的设计稿做好了，或者slides写好了，可以在局域网内分享，生成一个内部 IP 地址加端口的 URL（注意防火墙设置），让你的同事、老板也能对你的内容进行编辑、评论，并且实时同步。安全性也不用担心，所有数据都在你本机，你可以控制分享的权限级别：只读、评论、编辑，并且可以随时修改权限设置。deepseek harness 的插件也同步更新了，一样支持这个功能。” These product claims and the security assurance are supplied inspiration only, not verified facts or adopted guarantees.
- **Scenario and affected users:** Colleagues on the LAN open shared content in a browser to view it and leave comments without installing Mesh Talk. Designs and slides remain examples; supported formats are not selected.
- **Pain point or question:** Which LAN collaboration tools would meaningfully complement Mesh Talk? The primary scenario is now confirmed as browser-based viewing and commenting; detailed workflow friction remains to be clarified.
- **Desired outcome:** Let a Mesh Talk user share content with colleagues who can view and comment through a browser without installing the app. Continue clarifying this review workflow while retaining other LAN collaboration ideas for discussion.
- **Confirmed conclusions:**
  - Primary scenario: colleagues need no Mesh Talk installation and use a browser to view and comment on shared content.
  - Multi-user editing remains a direction for later discussion, outside the currently confirmed primary scenario. Native workspaces and external-tool integrations have not been selected.
  - The sharer can configure either link-only access or link plus an access code. Per-person approval is not a primary scenario. No default mode has been chosen.
  - Commenter identity and whether viewing/commenting permissions are separate remain open; do not add an account or per-person approval requirement to the confirmed browser entry flow.
  - Keep this session in requirements collection and clarification; do not begin development.
  - Content formats, detailed permission behavior, transport and update semantics remain undecided. The inspiration need not be implemented literally.
- **Additional original user clarification:** “先以‘同事无需安装 Mesh Talk，通过浏览器查看和评论我分享的内容’为主要场景，多人编辑保留为待讨论方向。请据此更新 REQ-002，继续澄清关键边界，暂不进入开发。”
- **Additional access clarification from user:** “访问方式先保留为可配置：分享者可选择持有链接即可访问，或链接加访问码；逐人审批暂不作为主要场景。请更新 REQ-002，继续澄清分享内容的类型和评论方式，暂不开发。”
- **Assistant suggestions / alternatives — unconfirmed, not ranked for global planning:**
  1. **Share and review existing work:** Publish selected designs, slides, HTML or other supported artifacts into a scoped sharing session; distribute an entry in a conversation and potentially a LAN browser URL. Viewing and comments could address review workflows without requiring an in-app authoring suite. Browser-based viewing and commenting is the confirmed primary direction. Content formats, revisions and entry distribution still require clarification; the detailed solution is not approved.
  2. **Native collaborative workspace:** Shared notes, whiteboard or lightweight team task board associated with a conversation. Allows direct joint work, but introduces editing semantics, concurrent changes, persistence and recovery responsibilities. These are candidate tools, not promised capabilities.
  3. **Integration with existing local tools:** Let authorized external tools publish sharing entries or previews through Mesh Talk, keeping authoring in the original tool. Requires deliberate integration, lifecycle and permission boundaries; do not assume an existing API supports this or that Mesh Talk should expose arbitrary local services.
- **Additional candidate use cases — unconfirmed:** Temporary transfer/download space and team review/decision sessions. Avoid committing to a broad toolbox until real scenarios are clear.
- **Design considerations to resolve, not fixed requirements:**
  - Browser participation without installation and sharer-configurable link-only/link-plus-code entry are confirmed. A reachable IP/port alone is not the scoped sharing link; exact link scope and access-code behavior remain to be designed.
  - In link-only mode forwarding the sharing link can pass access onward; in access-code mode the link and code can both be forwarded. Per-person approval is outside the primary scenario. Expiry, code changes, revocation and view/comment permissions still need decisions; no default mode selected.
  - Comment identity may be a self-entered nickname or verified identity; do not imply a nickname proves who submitted a comment. Comment persistence, replies, deletion/moderation and attachment to a page/region/version remain open.
  - Decide which content is shared and how safely it can be presented. An immutable published snapshot and a live local-file view have different update and comment-anchoring behavior. Do not assume arbitrary HTML can run with host/app privileges or that sharing one item exposes a directory.
  - Local storage alone does not establish confidentiality or safe access. Distinguish host storage, recipient/browser copies, authentication, transport protection and enforced read/comment/edit permissions.
  - Specify permission changes and revocation for already-open sessions; stopping future access cannot recall copies already downloaded. Avoid inheriting the quoted unconditional security assurance.
  - Distinguish viewing the latest published revision, live propagation of host edits, live comments and true simultaneous editing. They have different acceptance boundaries; “real time” alone does not specify which is wanted.
  - Clarify host sleep/exit, network changes, firewall reachability, reconnection and persistence. Host availability and copies on other devices need explicit behavior rather than an assumed always-available service.
  - Prefer reuse of existing identity, conversation, discovery, transport and file capabilities where suitable, subject to later owner/code inspection. This is an architectural proposal, not a verified reuse claim.
  - Keep optional sharing work demand-driven and consider resource budgets, consistent with the user's low-resource product goal. Do not introduce a permanent background service merely from this brainstorming discussion.
- **Content and comment options for clarification — not selected:**
  - Content families: static images/design exports; PDF documents or slide exports; Markdown/text; HTML pages or slide bundles with referenced assets. Original editable office/design files could instead be download attachments; inline preview/conversion is not assumed.
  - Distinguish one file from a multi-file page/bundle and a single artifact from a multi-item sharing session. No arbitrary directory exposure is implied.
  - Comment placement: a general discussion for the whole shared item; page/slide/image comments; precise region or selected-text annotations. These are alternative granularity choices, not all required.
  - A nickname, replies, resolved threads, moderation and live comment updates remain proposals. Comment anchors need explicit behavior if content is republished or replaced; snapshot/version choice is still open.
- **Open questions:**
  1. Which content families should the main scenario cover: images/PDFs, Markdown/text, HTML/slides bundles, or another concrete format?
  2. Should comments be general discussion, page/slide-specific, or precise region/text annotations?
  3. Is sharing a published snapshot or a live-updating source, and what happens to comments when content changes?
  4. How are commenters identified, and should comments persist, support replies or be moderated?
  5. What are the default access mode, separate view/comment permissions and expiry/code-change/revocation behavior for already-open sessions?
  6. What happens when the host sleeps/exits or the LAN address changes, and how do visitors recover?
  7. What update visibility is needed for content and comments? Simultaneous editing stays a separate discussion direction.
- **Candidate acceptance criteria — unconfirmed:** Confirmed outcomes: a colleague can view and comment on shared content in a browser without installing Mesh Talk; the sharer can choose link-only or link-plus-access-code entry, without per-person approval as a primary workflow. Proposed checks still to agree: visitor entry, supported content, permitted actions, comment identity/persistence, update visibility and interrupted-session recovery. Include access denial/revocation and resource behavior where applicable; no protocol, latency target or implementation selected.
- **Related records and evidence:** REQ-001 captures the user's resource-efficiency concerns; relevant as product context, not an established implementation prerequisite. REQ-001's monitoring default remains unanswered. No external product verification, source investigation or working capability demonstrated for REQ-002.
- **Global planning:** Classification, priority, effort, dependency analysis, roadmap phase and branch allocation deferred until collection closes.

### REQ-003 — Research and improve local/PR validation efficiency and reliability

Retention/performance refer to WORK-04/02. Raft remains unselected. |

Performance evals are supplied by WORK-02; advanced methods require explicit later applicability assessment. |

### Original-to-working-topic mapping

Every source has an owning topic. Cross-cutting constraints are linked rather than duplicated as parallel implementation tasks.

| REQ-018 | WORK-06 | Reusable sync evidence may support later features; dependencies still unverified. |

| REQ-020 | WORK-20 | External consumers, not merely another client of the same running app. |
| REQ-021 | WORK-21 | Client/core boundary, adapters and marketplace are separate decisions/deliverables. |
| REQ-022 | WORK-22 | Cross-cutting decision-memory practice; references guides rather than copying them. |
| REQ-023 | WORK-16 | Protocol prerequisite is a hypothesis to verify; video/temp rooms remain later. |
| REQ-024 | WORK-17 | Comment ranking/display/fetch/storage and three-day expiry remain distinct. |
| REQ-025 | WORK-12 | Anti-harassment versus exploratory endorsements remain separable. |
| REQ-026 | WORK-18 | Does not inherit forum audience, retention or propagation. |
| REQ-027 | WORK-19 | REQ-012 optional Web applies only to that desktop comparison. |
| REQ-028 | WORK-13 | Does not override ordinary chat service or content authorization. |
| REQ-029 | WORK-23 | Findings later can propose work; no automatic new scope. |
| REQ-030 | WORK-07 | Performance evidence from WORK-02 plugs into the same validation system. |

### What changed structurally

- Split REQ-016 across monitoring/diagnosis (WORK-01) and performance evals (WORK-02), eliminating duplicated monitoring and regression programs.
- Combined REQ-006/017 into WORK-04 with explicit distinct task boundaries for loading, memory, I/O, retention, sync scope and deletion correctness.

- Combined REQ-019/024 into WORK-17; kept private personal feed/profile WORK-18 distinct.
- Separated related technology/UI, privacy/harassment/incentives and SDK/client/ecosystem topics into independent decision surfaces instead of overlarge umbrella tasks.

### Next discussion state

The merge/split organization is accepted. **Still open:** research order, product/MVP boundaries, priority and risk tolerance, real dependencies, measurable acceptance, estimates, release/branch strategy and final TODO approval. Do not infer that later features require replacing the whole stack or protocol. Do not publish/merge this document or start research/implementation merely because its work topics now have IDs.

A suggested next conversation is the first-phase objective: focus on making the existing IM reliable and resource-efficient before major expansions, or deliberately advance selected new features in parallel. This is a question for discussion, not a chosen priority policy.

## Completion and handoff

- **Final TODO approved:** No — organization accepted; execution detail and sequencing still pending.
- **Repository publication / merge:** Not started; deferred until complete and confirmed.
- **Implementation:** Not started.

After collection closes, evolve this same document into the reviewed global TODO. Determine its maintained repository owner and navigation before proposing the merge. Trace every original item to its final task, explanation, deferral or withdrawal.
