item.aggregated_output:
REQ-001 — Built-in resource monitoring and performance visibility
- **Desired outcome:** Built-in continuous visibility into Mesh Talk resource consumption, supporting gradual optimization toward a high-performance, low-resource IM. An elegant monitoring surface accessible from an icon at the top of the desktop, following the supplied reference's visual direction.
- **Scope and constraints confirmed by user:** Monitor app CPU, memory, disk/write activity and network consumption, connection counts and latency to other nodes; exact metric definitions remain to clarify. Cover startup, idle and active-use scenarios. Include a desktop top-bar icon/panel presentation. Exact metrics, platforms, sampling cadence, history retention and performance targets remain unconfirmed.
- **Additional confirmed panel scope:** Provide an accessible panel showing Mesh Talk app-wide resource and operational metrics, including connection count, memory, write activity and latency to other nodes. Retain the earlier top-bar/menu-bar presentation request; the relationship between its compact view and the fuller panel remains to be designed. Prioritize existing data reuse and avoid extra acquisition cost.
- **Confirmed conclusions:**
  - Primary monitoring scope is Mesh Talk itself and its related processes. Whole-computer monitoring is not the primary requested scope.
  - Reuse existing data as much as possible; avoid separate or duplicate monitoring and unnecessary additional resource consumption.
  - Users must be able to disable monitoring work that incurs additional overhead to retain minimal resource use and power consumption.
  - Information already available without extra acquisition need not be disabled. This does not establish that displaying, aggregating or retaining it has zero overhead.
  - No concrete collection implementation or numeric performance budget agreed. Availability of reusable metrics and related-process attribution has not been verified against code.

REQ-002 — LAN sharing and collaboration tool exploration
- **Desired outcome:** Let a Mesh Talk user share content with colleagues who can view and comment through a browser without installing the app. Continue clarifying this review workflow while retaining other LAN collaboration ideas for discussion.
- **Confirmed conclusions:**
  - Primary scenario: colleagues need no Mesh Talk installation and use a browser to view and comment on shared content.
  - Multi-user editing remains a direction for later discussion, outside the currently confirmed primary scenario. Native workspaces and external-tool integrations have not been selected.
  - The sharer can configure either link-only access or link plus an access code. Per-person approval is not a primary scenario. No default mode has been chosen.
  - Commenter identity and whether viewing/commenting permissions are separate remain open; do not add an account or per-person approval requirement to the confirmed browser entry flow.
  - Keep this session in requirements collection and clarification; do not begin development.
  - Content formats, detailed permission behavior, transport and update semantics remain undecided. The inspiration need not be implemented literally.

REQ-003 — Research and improve local/PR validation efficiency and reliability
- **Desired outcome:** Evidence-backed investigation leading to actionable improvements in feedback speed, reliability and local/CI responsibility boundaries. Explicitly distinguish incremental execution, safely reusable evidence and risks requiring current-candidate confirmation before merge.
- **Confirmed scope from user:** Broad research into mainstream/mature desktop projects; comparison of local versus CI validation and execution placement; diagnosis of Mesh Talk's current workflow; address actual productivity friction rather than deliver generic CI advice.
- **Additional user-confirmed pain points and constraints:**
  - All three problems occur: waiting for local quality gates, waiting for CI after PR updates, and repeated reruns due to instability.
  - Later investigation must use actual elapsed-time measurements and failure records to determine the dominant bottlenecks. Do not presume a root cause or rank these pain points in advance.
  - Continue requirements collection now. Do not modify validation workflows or quality gates during this stage.

REQ-004 — Unify domain language and clarify business module responsibilities
- **Desired outcome:** A coherent understanding of domain concepts and relationships, and a clear mapping from business capabilities to owning modules and interfaces, supporting maintainable future iteration.
- **Confirmed scope from user:**
  - First clarify the existing business concepts, relationships, lifecycles and module responsibilities.
  - Consider extension locations for requirements already collected, without committing to final implementation designs.
  - Record refactoring separately only when a demonstrated need exists. A global refactor is not the default or a prerequisite implied by this item.
  - Use probing skills-assisted discussion to reach shared understanding.
  - Continue collecting requirements; do not implement now.

REQ-005 — Reusable event-driven mechanisms and unified scheduling governance
- **Desired outcome:** Reusable, well-defined events for appropriate state changes; fewer unnecessary polling tasks; a shared way to register legitimate scheduled work; explicit AI coding guidance to sustain the design.
- **Confirmed scope from user:**
  - Define and expose reusable events for actual application scenarios, reducing repeated polling where event triggering is appropriate.
  - Review existing timed fallback mechanisms and when they run, identifying candidates for event-driven behavior.
  - Provide reusable scheduling for different timing scenarios/categories instead of isolated timers or a dedicated thread per need.
  - Incorporate event and scheduling reuse into AI programming standards so future additions follow the same rules.
- **Additional confirmed principles:**
  - First investigate existing events, polling/fallbacks, scheduling and actual resource overhead; do not presume timers are the performance root cause.
  - Prefer reuse of reliable events. Retain necessary timeouts, retries and recovery checks.
  - Manage scheduling and task/subscription lifecycles consistently through reusable mechanisms; concrete architecture remains undecided.
  - Include these reuse requirements in AI coding standards. Detailed wording and enforcement remain to be designed; standards are not modified during intake.
  - Continue collecting requirements without implementing now.

REQ-006 — Incremental processing, reduce redundant I/O and review history handling
- **Desired outcome:** Reduce unnecessary disk and CPU work through appropriate change detection, version comparison and incremental processing; review history handling as part of this concern.
- **Confirmed scope from user:** Investigate inefficient full checks/fetches and avoidable writes; consider version comparison to reduce redundant work; organize the write-reduction effort and clarify history-related work. Specific optimization design, deletion policy and acceptance targets are not selected.

REQ-007 — Review internal technology choices and research desktop IM storage
- **Desired outcome:** A comprehensive, evidence-backed current-state review and relevant industry comparison, followed by joint decisions on what to retain, tune, adapt or replace where justified.
- **Confirmed scope from user:** Review internal technology-stack choices broadly; specifically investigate database/storage selection and actual storage technologies used by mainstream desktop IM clients; determine necessary changes together. The request is not a decision to replace a database or rewrite the stack.
- **Additional user-confirmed scope and boundaries:** Review the entire existing technology stack with database/storage as the focus. Decide whether to retain, optimize or replace based on actual evidence; do not presume migration. Continue requirements collection now, without research or implementation.

REQ-008 — Reliable, reusable foundations for decentralization, synchronization and encryption
- **Desired outcome:** Clear foundational layers and interfaces for decentralized mechanisms, data synchronization protocols and encryption, allowing future reuse with reliable behavior and explicit business integration.
- **Confirmed scope from user:**
  - Focus on reuse across Mesh Talk internal business capabilities for decentralized mechanisms, synchronization and encryption, with reliable contracts and reduced inappropriate coupling.
  - Do not prebuild an externally consumable SDK.
  - Preserve business-specific permission, consistency and conflict-resolution rules rather than force them into one generic policy.
  - Review existing layering before deciding which adjustments are justified; do not assume new layers or a rewrite are required.
  - Continue requirements collection now; do not investigate or implement during this stage.
  - Exact additional foundational concerns beyond the named areas remain open.

REQ-009 — Inventory technical components, document their designs and assess improvements
- **Desired outcome:** A comprehensive technical component inventory and maintained design documentation explaining current implementation, with separately identified evidence-based improvement/refactoring candidates.
- **Confirmed scope from user:** Cover the app's technical components broadly; document principles and implementation details, explicitly including history search and the logging system; evaluate whether optimization or refactoring is appropriate.
- **Additional confirmed organization and boundaries:**
  - Use a unified index plus maintained per-topic documentation.
  - Prioritize completing and correcting existing documentation rather than creating competing copies.
  - Clearly distinguish current implementation, issues awaiting verification and proposed changes. Present current behavior as established only when supported by evidence.
  - Do not presume refactoring; evaluate the need from evidence later.
  - Continue requirements collection now, without investigation or implementation.

REQ-010 — Recognize QR codes in chat images and offer relevant actions
- **Desired outcome:** Recognize QR codes from conversation images, identify supported content and provide appropriate link/contact/chat actions.
- **Confirmed scope from user:** Recognition in the chat-window image context, with URLs and contact-card QR codes as examples, including the possibility of entering a chat. Recognition is explicitly user-invoked from the image menu or large-image preview via “识别二维码”. Do not scan all images in the background. After decoding, display the contents and let the user choose to open a link or enter a supported contact conversation; do not execute automatically. Exact card formats, supported handlers and exceptional cases remain open.

REQ-011 — High-performance, low-power IM and ongoing performance regression prevention
- **Desired outcome:** Make high performance and low power/resource use a maintained product quality requirement, supported by reusable implementations, actionable AI guidance, executable tests and CI feedback rather than prose alone.
- **Confirmed scope from user:**
  - Improve the whole app toward a high-performance, low-power IM, explicitly including low idle resource use.
  - Guide future AI-assisted development to follow performance principles and reuse existing performant components where appropriate.
  - Provide corresponding test scripts, CI and feedback mechanisms to detect and limit future performance regressions.
- **Additional user-confirmed principles and boundaries:**
  - Treat this as a long-term quality requirement covering both improvement of current performance and ongoing regression prevention.
  - Determine performance budgets from actual measurements rather than assumed thresholds.
  - Prioritize reuse of existing components while maintaining validation efficiency and stability.
  - Continue requirements collection now; do not measure or implement during this stage.

REQ-012 — Evaluate desktop UI technologies, resource use and native experience
- **Desired outcome:** Evidence-based future decision on optimizing the existing UI stack, adding another UI implementation/shell, or migrating, improving native experience and resource efficiency without an assumed rewrite.
- **Confirmed scope from user:** Thorough later research into replacement or additional frontend shells/UI technologies, with GPUI and other supplied frameworks as candidates. Current work only captures the requirement under the ongoing intake process.
- **Additional user-confirmed scope and boundaries:**
  - macOS, Windows and Linux desktop are the primary evaluation targets; Web remains an optional reference rather than a required product target for this item.
  - Keep all three routes open: optimize Tauri, add another UI implementation, or migrate.
  - Decide using actual evidence from equivalent scenarios; do not presume replacement.
  - Continue requirements collection without research, measurement or implementation now.

REQ-013 — Review privacy, encryption and resistance to tracking
- **Desired outcome:** A professional evidence-based privacy and encryption assessment across the communication stack and business flows, with justified improvements and explicit guarantees/limits rather than an unconditional untraceability claim.
- **Confirmed scope from user:** Account protection, IP-related information protection and reducing traceability, spanning the entire underlying communication architecture, protocols and business behavior. Reliability and coherent design matter alongside privacy. Exact threat model and meanings of “account encryption” and “IP encryption” remain open.
- **Additional user-confirmed evaluation scope and boundaries:**
  - Include protecting sensitive information from LAN observers.
  - Also evaluate the feasibility and cost of reducing real-IP exposure and identity linkability to communicating nodes. This is an evaluation requirement, not a promise that peers cannot discover an address or correlate identities.
  - Do not promise absolute anonymity. Keep the threat model explicitly pending refinement.
  - After research/analysis, state evidence, feasibility, limitations and trade-offs honestly; select a pragmatic balance rather than assume maximum hiding regardless of cost.
  - Continue collecting requirements now; do not investigate or implement during this stage.

REQ-014 — Investigate release package growth and optimize size
- **Desired outcome:** Evidence-based breakdown of package growth and justified size/compression optimizations, with documented trade-offs.
- **Confirmed scope from user:** Investigate current versus earlier package size and assess optimization/compression opportunities. No mandatory return-to-under-10M target or removal of features selected.
- **Additional user-confirmed scope and boundaries:**
  - Prioritize download package size and also record installed disk footprint as a separate measure.
  - First compare artifacts for the same platform, architecture and package format to identify growth sources.
  - Do not assume the cause or require a return to 10M.
  - Continue requirements collection; do not analyze or implement now.

REQ-015 — Strengthen communication, data retention and performance as reusable modules
- **Desired outcome:** Clear business meanings, explicit module responsibilities and reliable shared mechanisms for communication, retention and resource behavior, leaving open later SDK packaging where justified.
- **Confirmed scope from user:** Cover the communication paths, data retention and performance mechanisms together, emphasizing modularization, appropriate foundational placement, clear responsibility and reuse. SDK capability is mentioned as a future direction, not immediate delivery.

REQ-016 — Resource-consumption diagnosis, performance evals and discoverability
- **Desired outcome:** Repeatable performance evals and CI execution that expose resource regressions, plus useful monitoring and diagnostic feedback rather than unexplained pass/fail results.
- **Confirmed scope from user:** Investigate resource consumption; establish performance-related evals and CI coverage; improve performance-related feedback, monitoring and discoverability. Meaning of “提示性能” remains to clarify rather than assume either notifications or general performance improvement.

REQ-017 — Startup/history loading, memory lifecycle, retention, sync scope and deletion preservation
- **Desired outcome:** Clear expectations and evidence requirements for responsive loading, explainable memory/resource behavior, understandable retention/capacity feedback, explicit synchronization scope and preservation of valid deletion intent without uncontrolled metadata cost.
- **Confirmed topic scope from user:**
  1. **Startup and history loading:** what must be ready initially, what history is loaded and when, and implications for responsiveness.
  2. **Memory growth and reclamation:** working-set growth over use and what should be released when no longer needed.
  3. **Retention and capacity notifications:** data kept, its lifetime/space usage and when/how users are informed about capacity.
  4. **History synchronization range:** what history participates in synchronization and under which circumstances.
  5. **Preventing deleted data from returning:** expected deletion semantics across restart, reconnect and replay.
  6. **Accumulation of deletion markers:** metadata lifetime, growth and any safe reclamation/compaction policy.

REQ-018 — Decentralized multi-device and group synchronization, reusable protocols and validation
- **Desired outcome:** Reliable, performant and documented synchronization protocols with reusable underlying capabilities and explicit per-business data semantics, validated under realistic success/failure conditions.
- **Confirmed scope from user:**
  - Personal multi-device sync and group-message multi-node sync are central product capabilities.
  - Improve/specify underlying communication and synchronization for reuse by future non-chat features; forum posts are an example, not an approved new forum feature.
  - Assess propagation and representation of group announcements and membership, including append, overwrite, full logs, operations and latest-state approaches.
  - Validate performance and reliability. Raft is a comparison/research question, not a selected algorithm.
- **Additional confirmed modeling principles and boundaries:**
  - Model group announcements and member permissions separately.
  - Explicitly distinguish locally pending operations from changes confirmed effective; no particular confirmation mechanism is selected.
  - Keep offline modification policy, conflict resolution and confirmation conditions as research questions rather than prematurely choose behavior.
  - Weigh reliability, performance and decentralization goals using later evidence. Do not preselect Raft.
  - Continue requirements collection now, without investigation or implementation.

REQ-019 — Explore a decentralized forum with local/cross-network sharing and personal retention
- **Desired outcome:** Explore a decentralized forum capability/system, its discovery and exchange model, and bounded storage/personal preservation behavior while retaining control over sharing.
- **Confirmed scope from user:** Brainstorm and clarify a decentralized forum extension; consider LAN sync, movement/Wi-Fi-related opportunities, optional Google Drive/external publication ideas and non-centralized retention choices. “Standalone” may mean separate application/system or a distinct Mesh Talk feature; no packaging choice confirmed.

REQ-020 — Extract reusable communication and security foundations for other projects
- **Desired outcome:** A future externally consumable SDK/package or set of packages with clear layer responsibilities, usable contracts and performance/reliability evidence; product-specific features need not be mandatory dependencies.
- **Confirmed scope from user:** External-project reuse beyond Mesh Talk, including underlying communication and/or encryption protocols and decentralized mechanisms, with performance tests. Networking/encryption/decentralization/business layers are proposed scope questions, not an approved package tree or mandate to expose raw cryptographic primitives.
- **Additional user-confirmed consumer scope and boundaries:**
  - Other Rust projects are the first intended SDK consumers.
  - Cross-language bindings remain a later direction, not part of the initial scope.
  - Validate interfaces through a real external use case; do not expand SDK scope speculatively.
  - Continue requirements collection now, without investigation, package extraction or implementation.

REQ-021 — Official core, interchangeable interaction clients and a community marketplace
- **Desired outcome:** One maintained source of core behavior and supported contracts; an official default client; replaceable/alternative GUI, terminal and automation interfaces; an ecosystem for community contributions and user choice.
- **Additional user-confirmed direction and deferred decisions:**
  - Confirm the product direction: officially maintained core, a default client and community-replaceable interaction clients/integrations.
  - Keep backend service versus SDK form, parallel multi-client operation and marketplace distribution mechanisms pending discussion.
  - Continue requirements collection; do not investigate or implement now.

REQ-022 — Preserve decision rationale and reasons for not implementing alternatives

重新看这 30 条需求，我建议先做一个调整：**保留原始诉求，但不再把每条诉求都当成一个独立开发项目。** 有些应该合并，有些是长期标准，有些只是供未来选择的方向。下面都是讨论建议，尚未写入文件。

**先把直接影响后续工作的基础排在前面：**

| 建议顺序 | 对应需求 | 先得到什么结果 |
|---|---|---|
| 1. 理清概念与责任 | 004、009、022 | 核心概念、模块职责、已有设计理由能查清楚，后续知道在哪里改 |
| 2. 建立性能与验证基线 | 001、003、011、016、030 | 能解释资源消耗、验证等待和失败，并判断改动是否有效 |
| 3. 明确同步、权限与数据生命周期 | 008、013、017、018，以及 015 的相关部分 | 多设备、群同步、删除、恢复和隐私的规则清楚 |
| 4. 按证据优化当前 IM | 005、006、017 的性能部分 | 减少无效工作，改善启动、历史加载、内存与磁盘消耗 |

这里的前置关系应当是**局部的**：改善启动，不必等待整个同步体系整理完；研究群语音，也不必先完成所有底层重构。

**这些需求应该合并整理，但保留内部交付边界：**

- **001＋016＋011：性能可观测与持续优化。** 分成性能诊断、监控数据、面板/菜单栏、回归保护。先能测量和解释，再完善展示；漂亮面板不应成为优化的前置条件。
- **003＋030：验证有效性与开发反馈效率。** 一起考虑“发现问题的能力”和“等待成本”，避免一边提速、一边无限增加检查。
- **004＋009：领域与技术责任整理。** 共用一次梳理，分别输出概念关系和技术说明。022 的决策记录作为持续维护方式贯穿其中。
- **008＋018＋015 的通信部分：内部通信与同步基础。** 015 不再单独成为一项笼统的“大整理”。
- **006＋017 的性能部分：历史与资源效率。** 但保留、删除、同步范围仍需单独讨论。
- **019＋024：论坛及其传播、转发。** 转发和评论筛选属于论坛方案，不必再成立另一套产品方向。

**几个大需求尤其需要拆开：**

| 原需求 | 建议拆法 |
|---|---|
| 017 | 启动/历史加载；内存回收；保留与容量提醒；同步范围；删除防回流；删除标记增长 |
| 018 | 个人多设备同步；群消息同步；公告状态；成员与权限状态 |
| 025 | 实用防骚扰与屏蔽；可选信誉背书。前者靠前，后者远期 |
| 021 | 核心与客户端边界；替代客户端；社区分发/市场。分别决定 |
| 023 | 群语音；视频；独立会议室。近期只讨论群语音是否值得推进 |
| 002 | 浏览器查看；评论与版本；多人编辑。多人编辑暂缓 |

拆分的目的，是让其中一部分能独立完成，而不是把所有部分都排进近期计划。

**近期保留少量独立机会，但不同时铺开：**

- **010 图片二维码识别**：场景较明确，可作为独立的小功能候选。
- **014 包体积分析**：可以独立调查，不需要绑定数据库或 UI 迁移。
- **025 实用防骚扰**：直接影响当前 IM 的使用安全，应排在信誉背书之前。
- **027 移动 PWA**：先明确希望解决的手机使用场景和可接受限制，再决定投入。
- **002 浏览器分享评论、023 群语音**：都有明确用途，建议后续从中选一个作为主要扩展方向，避免同时引入多套权限和生命周期问题。

**这些先作为规划，不进入近期实施队列：**

- 019、024：论坛、跨地点传播、评论筛选。
- 026：个人动态与主页。
- 028：贡献积分与资源激励。
- 020：对外 SDK。
- 021：社区客户端市场。
- 025：信誉背书体系。
- 023：视频和独立会议室。
- 012：第二套生产 UI 或整体迁移。

它们可以保留愿景，但重新启动时应有具体场景和理由，不能仅因为文档里写过就默认要做。

另外，我建议把几种表述从“开发目标”降为“可选手段”：统一调度不等于新建全局框架，内部复用不等于抽取 SDK，优化性能不等于更换数据库或 UI，完善测试不等于把列出的工具全部装上。007 技术栈调查、012 UI 比较、029 同类工具研究，应围绕具体问题展开，避免变成长期无边界调研。

**下一步先讨论一个核心取舍：第一阶段是否以“当前 IM 的可靠性、低消耗和开发反馈效率”为主，只容纳一个独立的新功能方向？** 我建议采用这个边界，再逐项决定哪些进入近期、哪些明确暂缓。

English note:  
“yes，continue” 可以更自然地说：“Yes, go ahead.”  
表示继续深入分析：“Please continue with the analysis.”  
讨论优先级：“Let’s agree on the priorities first.”  
常用搭配：define the scope、identify prerequisites、defer a feature。  
其中 **prerequisite** 指后续工作真正依赖的前置条件。

# Brainstorming Ideas Into Designs

Help turn ideas into fully formed designs and specs through natural collaborative dialogue.

Start by understanding the current project context, then ask questions one at a time to refine the idea. Once you understand what you're building, present the design and get user approval.

<HARD-GATE>
Do NOT invoke any implementation skill, write any code, scaffold any project, or take any implementation action until you have presented a design and the user has approved it. This applies to EVERY project regardless of perceived simplicity.
</HARD-GATE>

## Anti-Pattern: "This Is Too Simple To Need A Design"

Every project goes through this process. A todo list, a single-function utility, a config change — all of them. "Simple" projects are where unexamined assumptions cause the most wasted work. The design can be short (a few sentences for truly simple projects), but you MUST present it and get approval.

## Checklist

You MUST create a task for each of these items and complete them in order:

1. **Explore project context** — check files, docs, recent commits
2. **Offer visual companion** (if topic will involve visual questions) — this is its own message, not combined with a clarifying question. See the Visual Companion section below.
3. **Ask clarifying questions** — one at a time, understand purpose/constraints/success criteria
4. **Propose 2-3 approaches** — with trade-offs and your recommendation
5. **Present design** — in sections scaled to their complexity, get user approval after each section
6. **Write design doc** — save to `docs/superpowers/specs/YYYY-MM-DD-<topic>-design.md` and commit
7. **Spec self-review** — quick inline check for placeholders, contradictions, ambiguity, scope (see below)
8. **User reviews written spec** — ask user to review the spec file before proceeding
9. **Transition to implementation** — invoke writing-plans skill to create implementation plan

## Process Flow

```dot
digraph brainstorming {
    "Explore project context" [shape=box];
    "Visual questions ahead?" [shape=diamond];
    "Offer Visual Companion\n(own message, no other content)" [shape=box];

    "Propose 2-3 approaches" [shape=box];
    "Present design sections" [shape=box];
    "User approves design?" [shape=diamond];
    "Write design doc" [shape=box];
    "Spec self-review\n(fix inline)" [shape=box];
    "User reviews spec?" [shape=diamond];
    "Invoke writing-plans skill" [shape=doublecircle];

    "Explore project context" -> "Visual questions ahead?";
    "Visual questions ahead?" -> "Offer Visual Companion\n(own message, no other content)" [label="yes"];
    "Visual questions ahead?" -> "Ask clarifying questions" [label="no"];
    "Offer Visual Companion\n(own message, no other content)" -> "Ask clarifying questions";
    "Ask clarifying questions" -> "Propose 2-3 approaches";
    "Propose 2-3 approaches" -> "Present design sections";
    "Present design sections" -> "User approves design?";

}
```

**The terminal state is invoking writing-plans.** Do NOT invoke frontend-design, mcp-builder, or any other implementation skill. The ONLY skill you invoke after brainstorming is writing-plans.

**Understanding the idea:**

- Check out the current project state first (files, docs, recent commits)
- Before asking detailed questions, assess scope: if the request describes multiple independent subsystems (e.g., "build a platform with chat, file storage, billing, and analytics"), flag this immediately. Don't spend questions refining details of a project that needs to be decomposed first.
- If the project is too large for a single spec, help the user decompose into sub-projects: what are the independent pieces, how do they relate, what order should they be built? Then brainstorm the first sub-project through the normal design flow. Each sub-project gets its own spec → plan → implementation cycle.
- For appropriately-scoped projects, ask questions one at a time to refine the idea
- Prefer multiple choice questions when possible, but open-ended is fine too
- Only one question per message - if a topic needs more exploration, break it into multiple questions
- Focus on understanding: purpose, constraints, success criteria

**Exploring approaches:**

- Propose 2-3 different approaches with trade-offs
- Present options conversationally with your recommendation and reasoning
- Lead with your recommended option and explain why

**Presenting the design:**

- Once you believe you understand what you're building, present the design
- Scale each section to its complexity: a few sentences if straightforward, up to 200-300 words if nuanced
- Ask after each section whether it looks right so far
- Cover: architecture, components, data flow, error handling, testing
- Be ready to go back and clarify if something doesn't make sense

**Design for isolation and clarity:**

- Break the system into smaller units that each have one clear purpose, communicate through well-defined interfaces, and can be understood and tested independently
- For each unit, you should be able to answer: what does it do, how do you use it, and what does it depend on?
- Can someone understand what a unit does without reading its internals? Can you change the internals without breaking consumers? If not, the boundaries need work.
- Smaller, well-bounded units are also easier for you to work with - you reason better about code you can hold in context at once, and your edits are more reliable when files are focused. When a file grows large, that's often a signal that it's doing too much.

**Working in existing codebases:**

- Explore the current structure before proposing changes. Follow existing patterns.
- Where existing code has problems that affect the work (e.g., a file that's grown too large, unclear boundaries, tangled responsibilities), include targeted improvements as part of the design - the way a good developer improves code they're working in.
- Don't propose unrelated refactoring. Stay focused on what serves the current goal.

## After the Design

**Documentation:**

- Write the validated design (spec) to `docs/superpowers/specs/YYYY-MM-DD-<topic>-design.md`
  - (User preferences for spec location override this default)
- Use elements-of-style:writing-clearly-and-concisely skill if available
- Commit the design document to git

**Spec Self-Review:**
After writing the spec document, look at it with fresh eyes:

1. **Placeholder scan:** Any "TBD", "TODO", incomplete sections, or vague requirements? Fix them.
2. **Internal consistency:** Do any sections contradict each other? Does the architecture match the feature descriptions?
3. **Scope check:** Is this focused enough for a single implementation plan, or does it need decomposition?
4. **Ambiguity check:** Could any requirement be interpreted two different ways? If so, pick one and make it explicit.

Fix any issues inline. No need to re-review — just fix and move on.

**User Review Gate:**
After the spec review loop passes, ask the user to review the written spec before proceeding:

> "Spec written and committed to `<path>`. Please review it and let me know if you want to make any changes before we start writing out the implementation plan."

Wait for the user's response. If they request changes, make them and re-run the spec review loop. Only proceed once the user approves.

- Invoke the writing-plans skill to create a detailed implementation plan
- Do NOT invoke any other skill. writing-plans is the next step.

- **One question at a time** - Don't overwhelm with multiple questions
- **Multiple choice preferred** - Easier to answer than open-ended when possible
- **YAGNI ruthlessly** - Remove unnecessary features from all designs
- **Explore alternatives** - Always propose 2-3 approaches before settling
- **Incremental validation** - Present design, get approval before moving on
- **Be flexible** - Go back and clarify when something doesn't make sense

## Visual Companion

A browser-based companion for showing mockups, diagrams, and visual options during brainstorming. Available as a tool — not a mode. Accepting the companion means it's available for questions that benefit from visual treatment; it does NOT mean every question goes through the browser.

**Offering the companion:** When you anticipate that upcoming questions will involve visual content (mockups, layouts, diagrams), offer it once for consent:
> "Some of what we're working on might be easier to explain if I can show it to you in a web browser. I can put together mockups, diagrams, comparisons, and other visuals as we go. This feature is still new and can be token-intensive. Want to try it? (Requires opening a local URL)"

**This offer MUST be its own message.** Do not combine it with clarifying questions, context summaries, or any other content. The message should contain ONLY the offer above and nothing else. Wait for the user's response before continuing. If they decline, proceed with text-only brainstorming.

**Per-question decision:** Even after the user accepts, decide FOR EACH QUESTION whether to use the browser or the terminal. The test: **would the user understand this better by seeing it than reading it?**

- **Use the browser** for content that IS visual — mockups, wireframes, layout comparisons, architecture diagrams, side-by-side visual designs
- **Use the terminal** for content that is text — requirements questions, conceptual choices, tradeoff lists, A/B/C/D text options, scope decisions

A question about a UI topic is not automatically a visual question. "What does personality mean in this context?" is a conceptual question — use the terminal. "Which wizard layout works better?" is a visual question — use the browser.

If they agree to the companion, read the detailed guide before proceeding:
`skills/brainstorming/visual-companion.md`

# Writing Plans

## Overview

Write comprehensive implementation plans assuming the engineer has zero context for our codebase and questionable taste. Document everything they need to know: which files to touch for each task, code, testing, docs they might need to check, how to test it. Give them the whole plan as bite-sized tasks. DRY. YAGNI. TDD. Frequent commits.

Assume they are a skilled developer, but know almost nothing about our toolset or problem domain. Assume they don't know good test design very well.

**Announce at start:** "I'm using the writing-plans skill to create the implementation plan."

**Context:** This should be run in a dedicated worktree (created by brainstorming skill).

**Save plans to:** `docs/superpowers/plans/YYYY-MM-DD-<feature-name>.md`
- (User preferences for plan location override this default)

## Scope Check

If the spec covers multiple independent subsystems, it should have been broken into sub-project specs during brainstorming. If it wasn't, suggest breaking this into separate plans — one per subsystem. Each plan should produce working, testable software on its own.

## File Structure

Before defining tasks, map out which files will be created or modified and what each one is responsible for. This is where decomposition decisions get locked in.

- Design units with clear boundaries and well-defined interfaces. Each file should have one clear responsibility.
- You reason best about code you can hold in context at once, and your edits are more reliable when files are focused. Prefer smaller, focused files over large ones that do too much.
- Files that change together should live together. Split by responsibility, not by technical layer.
- In existing codebases, follow established patterns. If the codebase uses large files, don't unilaterally restructure - but if a file you're modifying has grown unwieldy, including a split in the plan is reasonable.

This structure informs the task decomposition. Each task should produce self-contained changes that make sense independently.

## Bite-Sized Task Granularity

**Each step is one action (2-5 minutes):**
- "Write the failing test" - step
- "Run it to make sure it fails" - step
- "Implement the minimal code to make the test pass" - step
- "Run the tests and make sure they pass" - step
- "Commit" - step

## Plan Document Header

**Every plan MUST start with this header:**

```markdown
# [Feature Name] Implementation Plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal:** [One sentence describing what this builds]

**Architecture:** [2-3 sentences about approach]

**Tech Stack:** [Key technologies/libraries]

---
```

## Task Structure

````markdown
### Task N: [Component Name]

**Files:**
- Create: `exact/path/to/file.py`
- Modify: `exact/path/to/existing.py:123-145`
- Test: `tests/exact/path/to/test.py`

- [ ] **Step 1: Write the failing test**

```python
def test_specific_behavior():
    result = function(input)
    assert result == expected
```

- [ ] **Step 2: Run test to verify it fails**

Run: `pytest tests/path/test.py::test_name -v`
Expected: FAIL with "function not defined"

- [ ] **Step 3: Write minimal implementation**

```python
def function(input):
    return expected
```

- [ ] **Step 4: Run test to verify it passes**

Run: `pytest tests/path/test.py::test_name -v`
Expected: PASS

- [ ] **Step 5: Commit**

```bash
git add tests/path/test.py src/path/file.py
git commit -m "feat: add specific feature"
```
````

## No Placeholders

Every step must contain the actual content an engineer needs. These are **plan failures** — never write them:
- "TBD", "TODO", "implement later", "fill in details"
- "Add appropriate error handling" / "add validation" / "handle edge cases"
- "Write tests for the above" (without actual test code)
- "Similar to Task N" (repeat the code — the engineer may be reading tasks out of order)
- Steps that describe what to do without showing how (code blocks required for code steps)
- References to types, functions, or methods not defined in any task

## Remember
- Exact file paths always
- Complete code in every step — if a step changes code, show the code
- Exact commands with expected output
- DRY, YAGNI, TDD, frequent commits

## Self-Review

After writing the complete plan, look at the spec with fresh eyes and check the plan against it. This is a checklist you run yourself — not a subagent dispatch.

**1. Spec coverage:** Skim each section/requirement in the spec. Can you point to a task that implements it? List any gaps.

**2. Placeholder scan:** Search your plan for red flags — any of the patterns from the "No Placeholders" section above. Fix them.

**3. Type consistency:** Do the types, method signatures, and property names you used in later tasks match what you defined in earlier tasks? A function called `clearLayers()` in Task 3 but `clearFullLayers()` in Task 7 is a bug.

If you find issues, fix them inline. No need to re-review — just fix and move on. If you find a spec requirement with no task, add the task.

## Execution Handoff

After saving the plan, offer execution choice:

**"Plan complete and saved to `docs/superpowers/plans/<filename>.md`. Two execution options:**

**1. Subagent-Driven (recommended)** - I dispatch a fresh subagent per task, review between tasks, fast iteration

**2. Inline Execution** - Execute tasks in this session using executing-plans, batch execution with checkpoints

**Which approach?"**

**If Subagent-Driven chosen:**
- **REQUIRED SUB-SKILL:** Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development
- Fresh subagent per task + two-stage review

**If Inline Execution chosen:**
- **REQUIRED SUB-SKILL:** Use superpowers:executing-plans
- Batch execution with checkpoints for review

description: Use when you have a spec or requirements for a multi-step task, before touching code
---

# Writing Plans

## Overview

Write comprehensive implementation plans assuming the engineer has zero context for our codebase and questionable taste. Document everything they need to know: which files to touch for each task, code, testing, docs they might need to check, how to test it. Give them the whole plan as bite-sized tasks. DRY. YAGNI. TDD. Frequent commits.

Assume they are a skilled developer, but know almost nothing about our toolset or problem domain. Assume they don't know good test design very well.

**Announce at start:** "I'm using the writing-plans skill to create the implementation plan."

**Context:** This should be run in a dedicated worktree (created by brainstorming skill).

**Save plans to:** `docs/superpowers/plans/YYYY-MM-DD-<feature-name>.md`
- (User preferences for plan location override this default)

## Scope Check

If the spec covers multiple independent subsystems, it should have been broken into sub-project specs during brainstorming. If it wasn't, suggest breaking this into separate plans — one per subsystem. Each plan should produce working, testable software on its own.

## File Structure

Before defining tasks, map out which files will be created or modified and what each one is responsible for. This is where decomposition decisions get locked in.

- Design units with clear boundaries and well-defined interfaces. Each file should have one clear responsibility.
- You reason best about code you can hold in context at once, and your edits are more reliable when files are focused. Prefer smaller, focused files over large ones that do too much.
- Files that change together should live together. Split by responsibility, not by technical layer.
- In existing codebases, follow established patterns. If the codebase uses large files, don't unilaterally restructure - but if a file you're modifying has grown unwieldy, including a split in the plan is reasonable.

This structure informs the task decomposition. Each task should produce self-contained changes that make sense independently.

## Bite-Sized Task Granularity

**Each step is one action (2-5 minutes):**
- "Write the failing test" - step
- "Run it to make sure it fails" - step
- "Implement the minimal code to make the test pass" - step
- "Run the tests and make sure they pass" - step
- "Commit" - step

## Plan Document Header

**Every plan MUST start with this header:**

```markdown
# [Feature Name] Implementation Plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal:** [One sentence describing what this builds]

**Architecture:** [2-3 sentences about approach]

**Tech Stack:** [Key technologies/libraries]

---
```

## Task Structure

````markdown
### Task N: [Component Name]

**Files:**
- Create: `exact/path/to/file.py`
- Modify: `exact/path/to/existing.py:123-145`
- Test: `tests/exact/path/to/test.py`

- [ ] **Step 1: Write the failing test**

```python
def test_specific_behavior():
    result = function(input)
    assert result == expected
```

- [ ] **Step 2: Run test to verify it fails**

Run: `pytest tests/path/test.py::test_name -v`
Expected: FAIL with "function not defined"

- [ ] **Step 3: Write minimal implementation**

```python
def function(input):
    return expected
```

- [ ] **Step 4: Run test to verify it passes**

Run: `pytest tests/path/test.py::test_name -v`
Expected: PASS

- [ ] **Step 5: Commit**

```bash
git add tests/path/test.py src/path/file.py
git commit -m "feat: add specific feature"
```
````

## No Placeholders

Every step must contain the actual content an engineer needs. These are **plan failures** — never write them:
- "TBD", "TODO", "implement later", "fill in details"
- "Add appropriate error handling" / "add validation" / "handle edge cases"
- "Write tests for the above" (without actual test code)
- "Similar to Task N" (repeat the code — the engineer may be reading tasks out of order)
- Steps that describe what to do without showing how (code blocks required for code steps)
- References to types, functions, or methods not defined in any task

## Remember
- Exact file paths always
- Complete code in every step — if a step changes code, show the code
- Exact commands with expected output
- DRY, YAGNI, TDD, frequent commits

## Self-Review

After writing the complete plan, look at the spec with fresh eyes and check the plan against it. This is a checklist you run yourself — not a subagent dispatch.

**1. Spec coverage:** Skim each section/requirement in the spec. Can you point to a task that implements it? List any gaps.

**2. Placeholder scan:** Search your plan for red flags — any of the patterns from the "No Placeholders" section above. Fix them.

**3. Type consistency:** Do the types, method signatures, and property names you used in later tasks match what you defined in earlier tasks? A function called `clearLayers()` in Task 3 but `clearFullLayers()` in Task 7 is a bug.

If you find issues, fix them inline. No need to re-review — just fix and move on. If you find a spec requirement with no task, add the task.

## Execution Handoff

After saving the plan, offer execution choice:

**"Plan complete and saved to `docs/superpowers/plans/<filename>.md`. Two execution options:**

**1. Subagent-Driven (recommended)** - I dispatch a fresh subagent per task, review between tasks, fast iteration

**2. Inline Execution** - Execute tasks in this session using executing-plans, batch execution with checkpoints

**Which approach?"**

**If Subagent-Driven chosen:**
- **REQUIRED SUB-SKILL:** Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development
- Fresh subagent per task + two-stage review

**If Inline Execution chosen:**
- **REQUIRED SUB-SKILL:** Use superpowers:executing-plans
- Batch execution with checkpoints for review
"}

你的方向是合理的：**先把当前 IM 的性能、模块边界、通信同步和数据生命周期建设好，再让后续功能复用这些基础。论坛、PWA、客户端市场等先进入远期 roadmap，当前不启动开发。**

我建议采用“**分阶段建设基础，每阶段内部有序并行，基础验收后再开放功能开发**”的安排。同时给基础建设明确终点，避免一直拆模块、做抽象，却迟迟没有可交付成果。

以下只依据需求文件提出讨论稿，不涉及现有实现判断，也暂不修改文件。

### 一、先把 30 条需求分成四类

| 类别 | 包含内容 | 安排 |
|---|---|---|
| 基础建设 | 领域与模块、通信与同步、事件调度、存储与生命周期、隐私权限 | 当前主要投入 |
| 持续质量能力 | 性能测量、回归保护、验证效率、设计理由与文档 | 从一开始建设，贯穿后续 |
| 当前 IM 的完善 | 监控面板、防骚扰、二维码、包体积等 | 基础验收后按依赖并行 |
| 功能展望 | 论坛、PWA、动态、群会议、外部 SDK、客户端市场等 | 先记录方向与启动条件 |

其中，**性能优化不是一个做完就结束的任务**。基础阶段应完成主要问题治理和回归机制，后续功能仍要遵守同一套资源约束。

### 二、阶段 0：明确基础建设范围

先回答“当前有什么、应该由谁负责、哪些规则不能破坏”，再决定拆什么、优化什么。

| 工作 | 对应需求 | 交付结果 |
|---|---|---|
| 业务概念与模块责任梳理 | 004、009 | 概念、模块、调用关系和责任边界 |
| 技术与存储现状整理 | 007、009 | 实际技术栈、存储类别及其用途 |
| 核心业务规则整理 | 008、013、017、018 | 身份、权限、同步、删除、恢复和隐私边界 |
| 设计理由与决策记录 | 022 | 已选方案、未决问题、暂缓理由和重启条件 |

这一阶段不要求把所有文档补到百科全书的程度。重点是形成一张能指导后续工作的责任地图。

**完成条件：**每项基础工作有明确问题、所属模块、受影响业务和验收方式；“需要核实”和“已经确认”分开记录。

### 三、阶段 1：建立测量与验证能力，确定基础设计

这一阶段有三条可以并行的工作线。

| 工作线 | 主要内容 | 后续作用 |
|---|---|---|
| 性能基线 | 启动、空闲、消息收发、历史加载、搜索、同步、使用后回到空闲 | 确定性能问题和优化顺序 |
| 验证基线 | 本地与 CI 等待、失败与重跑、测试覆盖和断言质量 | 让后面的基础改造能快速、可信地验证 |
| 基础契约 | 模块接口、通道职责、同步权限、数据生命周期、任务取消和资源上限 | 防止拆分后出现多套规则 |

对应 001、003、005、008、011、013、016、017、018、030。

这里有两个顺序需要坚持：

- **先有可比较的性能证据，再决定主要优化和技术替换。**
- **先明确权限、持久化和恢复规则，再改同步、调度与存储路径。**

监控面板可以晚一点做。开发者能够测量和定位问题，不需要以完整的菜单栏和图表界面为前提。

**完成条件：**有可重复的代表性场景、必要的正确性检查，以及按影响排序的基础改造清单。此时再确定具体指标，不在需求讨论阶段编造数字。

### 四、阶段 2：建设可复用的基础，完成主要性能治理

这是本轮计划的核心。我建议分为五个工作包。

| 工作包 | 应完成什么 | 前置依赖 |
|---|---|---|
| A. 模块与接口整理 | 按责任拆分，明确核心、宿主、客户端适配边界；迁移现有调用者 | 责任地图、基础契约 |
| B. 事件与调度治理 | 复用事件、合并重复工作、统一必要调度的接入和生命周期 | 工作触发/取消规则、性能证据 |
| C. 通信与同步基础 | 明确连接、传输、同步、投递等职责；分别整理个人同步、群同步、公告和成员权限 | 身份权限、同步与恢复契约 |
| D. 存储与数据生命周期 | 优化增量读写、启动和历史加载；明确缓存回收、保留、删除和同步范围 | 数据语义、同步契约、性能证据 |
| E. 性能与质量保护 | 将改造后的关键场景纳入回归；落实 AI 编程规则与维护文档 | 随 A—D 的每个交付逐步完成 |

“通道拆好”需要先解释清楚：连接和传输解决如何通信，同步解决交换哪些数据，业务层决定谁有权写入、读取和删除。它们可以复用机制，但不能把业务权限也混成一个通用规则。

模块拆分也应以这些结果验收：

- 调用者通过清晰接口使用能力。
- 业务规则有唯一负责人。
- 生命周期、错误、取消和资源限制明确。
- 现有业务经过迁移和验证。
- 确认的问题得到改善，必要时保留原实现。

仅仅把大文件拆成小文件，不能算基础建设完成。

**这阶段怎样并行：**

- A 先确定共享接口和迁移顺序，其他工作包随相关接口稳定逐步接入，不必等待全部模块整理完成。
- B 与 C 可以并行，但不能各自修改同一个任务调度或重试负责人。
- D 的加载与缓存优化可以独立推进；删除防回流、同步范围、标记回收必须与 C 协调。
- E 跟随每个工作包交付，不留到最后集中补测试。
- 原生性能测量单独安排，避免并发编译和测试污染结果。

**不建议预先决定：**更换数据库、整体迁移 UI、引入某个共识协议、抽取公共 SDK。只有现状证据证明需要时，才成为这一阶段的具体方案。

### 五、阶段 3：验收基础，形成稳定的复用版本

你提出“基础全部做好后再开发功能”，我赞同将它作为一个明确关口。但“全部做好”应当是**约定范围内的基础已验收**，而不是要求所有架构问题永久解决。

建议验收以下内容：

| 验收面 | 达标含义 |
|---|---|
| 模块 | 责任和接口清楚，现有调用者已迁移，没有两套并行权威 |
| 性能 | 约定场景有前后对比，主要目标达成，剩余问题有明确处置 |
| 空闲与回收 | 使用完成后能停止额外工作，缓存、队列和任务增长有界 |
| 同步与数据 | 关键断网、重连、重启、重复、乱序、撤销、删除与恢复场景有证据 |
| 隐私权限 | 实际保证和暴露边界清楚，权限在正确层执行 |
| 验证 | 本地、CI、原生验收分工明确，反馈效率和缺口可解释 |
| 复用 | 后续功能知道应该接入哪个接口、遵守什么规则 |

严重权限、数据丢失或恢复问题必须解决。其余问题可以在理由明确、影响受控的情况下保留，避免基础阶段无限延期。

### 六、基础验收后，先并行完善当前 IM

这时可以形成几条相对独立的开发线：

| 开发线 | 对应需求 | 使用的基础 |
|---|---|---|
| 监控面板与菜单栏入口 | 001、016 | 指标来源、低成本采集、事件订阅、关闭与回收机制 |
| 实用防骚扰与屏蔽 | 025 的实用部分 | 身份、账号/设备权限、接收策略、跨设备状态 |
| 手动图片二维码识别 | 010 | 图片获取、受保护内容处理、异步任务和安全动作 |
| 包体积优化 | 014 | 可比较的构建产物、依赖和资源清单、安装更新验证 |
| 当前业务的小范围完善 | 前述验收留下的明确问题 | 已稳定的模块及其回归检查 |

这些工作可以并行，是因为各自结果可以独立验收。共享接口仍需由一个负责人协调，不能因为分支独立就同时改变同一份契约。

包体积的**调查**可以在基础阶段提前完成；影响运行能力的优化仍需按证据安排。

### 七、功能展望单独放进 roadmap，当前不启动

建议将这些需求从近期执行队列移出，只保留用途、关键依赖和启动条件。

| 方向 | 对应需求 | 基础完成后，还需要满足什么 |
|---|---|---|
| 浏览器分享与评论 | 002 | 明确内容格式、链接授权、评论版本和宿主离线行为 |
| 群语音，之后再考虑视频 | 023 | 明确规模、成员准入、媒体路径和原生资源预算 |
| 移动 PWA | 027 | 明确手机场景、配对与密钥、浏览器限制、节点访问和离线承诺 |
| 去中心论坛与转发 | 019、024 | 明确受众、传播授权、保留/置顶、评论和删除含义 |
| 私人动态与主页 | 026 | 明确每条内容和主页的独立可见范围 |
| 可替换客户端与前端市场 | 021 | 先稳定客户端契约，再讨论分发、兼容、安装和信任 |
| 外部 Rust SDK | 020 | 有真实外部使用者，明确支持范围和兼容责任 |
| 信誉背书与贡献激励 | 025 的背书部分、028 | 有实际滥用或资源分配问题，且能说明隐私、公平和防作弊成本 |
| 替代 UI 或迁移 | 012 | 现有方案经过优化后，仍有值得替换的明确问题 |
| 同类工具机会研究 | 029 | 有具体用户问题，再做针对性比较 |

这些方向未来也不必排成一条长队。例如，PWA、论坛和群语音在各自契约就绪后，可以使用共同基础分别开发。**客户端市场应晚于客户端契约与真实替代客户端；激励应晚于真实的可选资源服务和分配问题。**

### 八、合并后的全局关系

最终建议保留原始需求编号追溯，但执行上归入以下几个项目：

| 执行项目 | 来源需求 | 主要位置 |
|---|---|---|
| 领域、责任与技术说明 | 004、009；007 的现状部分 | 阶段 0，随后持续维护 |
| 性能诊断、优化和回归 | 001、005、006、011、016、017 的性能部分 | 阶段 1—3 |
| 验证效率与质量 | 003、030 | 阶段 1 起持续建设 |
| 内部通信与同步基础 | 008、018；015 的通信部分 | 阶段 1—3 |
| 数据生命周期 | 017；015 的保留部分 | 阶段 1—3 |
| 隐私、身份与权限 | 013；025 的相关规则 | 阶段 1—3，实用控制随后交付 |

- 业务规则有唯一负责人。

- 现有业务经过迁移和验证。
- 确认的问题得到改善，必要时保留原实现。

- 生命周期、错误、取消和资源限制明确。
- 现有业务经过迁移和验证。
- 确认的问题得到改善，必要时保留原实现。

仅仅把大文件拆成小文件，不能算基础建设完成。

**这阶段怎样并行：**

- A 先确定共享接口和迁移顺序，其他工作包随相关接口稳定逐步接入，不必等待全部模块整理完成。
- B 与 C 可以并行，但不能各自修改同一个任务调度或重试负责人。
- D 的加载与缓存优化可以独立推进；删除防回流、同步范围、标记回收必须与 C 协调。
- E 跟随每个工作包交付，不留到最后集中补测试。
- 原生性能测量单独安排，避免并发编译和测试污染结果。

**不建议预先决定：**更换数据库、整体迁移 UI、引入某个共识协议、抽取公共 SDK。只有现状证据证明需要时，才成为这一阶段的具体方案。

### 五、阶段 3：验收基础，形成稳定的复用版本

你提出“基础全部做好后再开发功能”，我赞同将它作为一个明确关口。但“全部做好”应当是**约定范围内的基础已验收**，而不是要求所有架构问题永久解决。

建议验收以下内容：

| 验收面 | 达标含义 |
|---|---|
| 模块 | 责任和接口清楚，现有调用者已迁移，没有两套并行权威 |
| 性能 | 约定场景有前后对比，主要目标达成，剩余问题有明确处置 |
| 空闲与回收 | 使用完成后能停止额外工作，缓存、队列和任务增长有界 |
| 同步与数据 | 关键断网、重连、重启、重复、乱序、撤销、删除与恢复场景有证据 |
| 隐私权限 | 实际保证和暴露边界清楚，权限在正确层执行 |
| 验证 | 本地、CI、原生验收分工明确，反馈效率和缺口可解释 |
| 复用 | 后续功能知道应该接入哪个接口、遵守什么规则 |

严重权限、数据丢失或恢复问题必须解决。其余问题可以在理由明确、影响受控的情况下保留，避免基础阶段无限延期。

### 六、基础验收后，先并行完善当前 IM

这时可以形成几条相对独立的开发线：

| 开发线 | 对应需求 | 使用的基础 |
|---|---|---|
| 监控面板与菜单栏入口 | 001、016 | 指标来源、低成本采集、事件订阅、关闭与回收机制 |
| 实用防骚扰与屏蔽 | 025 的实用部分 | 身份、账号/设备权限、接收策略、跨设备状态 |
| 手动图片二维码识别 | 010 | 图片获取、受保护内容处理、异步任务和安全动作 |
| 包体积优化 | 014 | 可比较的构建产物、依赖和资源清单、安装更新验证 |
| 当前业务的小范围完善 | 前述验收留下的明确问题 | 已稳定的模块及其回归检查 |

这些工作可以并行，是因为各自结果可以独立验收。共享接口仍需由一个负责人协调，不能因为分支独立就同时改变同一份契约。

包体积的**调查**可以在基础阶段提前完成；影响运行能力的优化仍需按证据安排。

### 七、功能展望单独放进 roadmap，当前不启动

建议将这些需求从近期执行队列移出，只保留用途、关键依赖和启动条件。

| 方向 | 对应需求 | 基础完成后，还需要满足什么 |
|---|---|---|
| 浏览器分享与评论 | 002 | 明确内容格式、链接授权、评论版本和宿主离线行为 |
| 群语音，之后再考虑视频 | 023 | 明确规模、成员准入、媒体路径和原生资源预算 |
| 移动 PWA | 027 | 明确手机场景、配对与密钥、浏览器限制、节点访问和离线承诺 |
| 去中心论坛与转发 | 019、024 | 明确受众、传播授权、保留/置顶、评论和删除含义 |
| 私人动态与主页 | 026 | 明确每条内容和主页的独立可见范围 |
| 可替换客户端与前端市场 | 021 | 先稳定客户端契约，再讨论分发、兼容、安装和信任 |
| 外部 Rust SDK | 020 | 有真实外部使用者，明确支持范围和兼容责任 |
| 信誉背书与贡献激励 | 025 的背书部分、028 | 有实际滥用或资源分配问题，且能说明隐私、公平和防作弊成本 |
| 替代 UI 或迁移 | 012 | 现有方案经过优化后，仍有值得替换的明确问题 |
| 同类工具机会研究 | 029 | 有具体用户问题，再做针对性比较 |

这些方向未来也不必排成一条长队。例如，PWA、论坛和群语音在各自契约就绪后，可以使用共同基础分别开发。**客户端市场应晚于客户端契约与真实替代客户端；激励应晚于真实的可选资源服务和分配问题。**

### 八、合并后的全局关系

最终建议保留原始需求编号追溯，但执行上归入以下几个项目：

| 执行项目 | 来源需求 | 主要位置 |
|---|---|---|
| 领域、责任与技术说明 | 004、009；007 的现状部分 | 阶段 0，随后持续维护 |
| 性能诊断、优化和回归 | 001、005、006、011、016、017 的性能部分 | 阶段 1—3 |
| 验证效率与质量 | 003、030 | 阶段 1 起持续建设 |
| 内部通信与同步基础 | 008、018；015 的通信部分 | 阶段 1—3 |
| 数据生命周期 | 017；015 的保留部分 | 阶段 1—3 |
| 隐私、身份与权限 | 013；025 的相关规则 | 阶段 1—3，实用控制随后交付 |
| 决策记录 | 022 | 全阶段维护 |
| 当前 IM 完善 | 010、014、监控界面、实用防骚扰 | 基础验收后并行 |
| 技术替换决策 | 007 的替换部分、012 | 有证据才启动 |
| 功能展望 | 002、019—021、023—029 中的扩展部分 | 后续 roadmap |

REQ-015 的内容分别归入通信、保留和性能，不再单独安排一个范围模糊的“全局重构”。

我建议我们接下来先讨论**阶段 2 的五个基础工作包是否完整、范围是否合适**。这会决定基础建设的终点；等这个边界明确，再细化包内顺序，比现在直接列几十项开发任务更可靠。

English note:  
原意：“先做好基础，后续在这个基础上并行开发。”  
Better: “Establish the foundations first, then develop independent features in parallel.”  
**build on** 表示基于已有成果继续建设。  
可复用：“Future features should build on these shared foundations.”  
常用搭配：define dependencies、set acceptance criteria、sequence the work。

description: Use when starting feature work that needs isolation from current workspace or before executing implementation plans - creates isolated git worktrees with smart directory selection and safety verification

# Using Git Worktrees

## Overview

Git worktrees create isolated workspaces sharing the same repository, allowing work on multiple branches simultaneously without switching.

**Core principle:** Systematic directory selection + safety verification = reliable isolation.

**Announce at start:** "I'm using the using-git-worktrees skill to set up an isolated workspace."

## Directory Selection Process

Follow this priority order:

### 1. Check Existing Directories

```bash
# Check in priority order
ls -d .worktrees 2>/dev/null     # Preferred (hidden)
ls -d worktrees 2>/dev/null      # Alternative
```

**If found:** Use that directory. If both exist, `.worktrees` wins.

### 2. Check CLAUDE.md

```bash
grep -i "worktree.*director" CLAUDE.md 2>/dev/null
```

**If preference specified:** Use it without asking.

### 3. Ask User

If no directory exists and no CLAUDE.md preference:

```
No worktree directory found. Where should I create worktrees?

1. .worktrees/ (project-local, hidden)
2. ~/.config/superpowers/worktrees/<project-name>/ (global location)

Which would you prefer?
```

## Safety Verification

### For Project-Local Directories (.worktrees or worktrees)

**MUST verify directory is ignored before creating worktree:**

```bash
# Check if directory is ignored (respects local, global, and system gitignore)
git check-ignore -q .worktrees 2>/dev/null || git check-ignore -q worktrees 2>/dev/null
```

**If NOT ignored:**

Per Jesse's rule "Fix broken things immediately":
1. Add appropriate line to .gitignore
2. Commit the change
3. Proceed with worktree creation

**Why critical:** Prevents accidentally committing worktree contents to repository.

### For Global Directory (~/.config/superpowers/worktrees)

No .gitignore verification needed - outside project entirely.

## Creation Steps

### 1. Detect Project Name

```bash
project=$(basename "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)")
```

### 2. Create Worktree

```bash
# Determine full path
case $LOCATION in
  .worktrees|worktrees)
    path="$LOCATION/$BRANCH_NAME"
    ;;
  ~/.config/superpowers/worktrees/*)
    path="~/.config/superpowers/worktrees/$project/$BRANCH_NAME"
    ;;
esac

# Create worktree with new branch
git worktree add "$path" -b "$BRANCH_NAME"
cd "$path"
```

### 3. Run Project Setup

Auto-detect and run appropriate setup:

```bash
# Node.js
if [ -f package.json ]; then npm install; fi

# Rust
if [ -f Cargo.toml ]; then cargo build; fi

# Python
if [ -f requirements.txt ]; then pip install -r requirements.txt; fi
if [ -f pyproject.toml ]; then poetry install; fi

# Go
if [ -f go.mod ]; then go mod download; fi
```

### 4. Verify Clean Baseline

Run tests to ensure worktree starts clean:

```bash
# Examples - use project-appropriate command
npm test
cargo test
pytest
go test ./...
```

**If tests fail:** Report failures, ask whether to proceed or investigate.

**If tests pass:** Report ready.

### 5. Report Location

```
Worktree ready at <full-path>
Tests passing (<N> tests, 0 failures)
Ready to implement <feature-name>
```

## Quick Reference

| Situation | Action |
|-----------|--------|
| `.worktrees/` exists | Use it (verify ignored) |
| `worktrees/` exists | Use it (verify ignored) |
| Both exist | Use `.worktrees/` |
| Neither exists | Check CLAUDE.md → Ask user |
| Directory not ignored | Add to .gitignore + commit |
| Tests fail during baseline | Report failures + ask |
| No package.json/Cargo.toml | Skip dependency install |

## Common Mistakes

### Skipping ignore verification

- **Problem:** Worktree contents get tracked, pollute git status
- **Fix:** Always use `git check-ignore` before creating project-local worktree

### Assuming directory location

- **Problem:** Creates inconsistency, violates project conventions
- **Fix:** Follow priority: existing > CLAUDE.md > ask

### Proceeding with failing tests

- **Problem:** Can't distinguish new bugs from pre-existing issues
- **Fix:** Report failures, get explicit permission to proceed

### Hardcoding setup commands

- **Problem:** Breaks on projects using different tools
- **Fix:** Auto-detect from project files (package.json, etc.)

## Example Workflow

```
You: I'm using the using-git-worktrees skill to set up an isolated workspace.

[Check .worktrees/ - exists]
[Verify ignored - git check-ignore confirms .worktrees/ is ignored]
[Create worktree: git worktree add .worktrees/auth -b feature/auth]
[Run npm install]
[Run npm test - 47 passing]

Worktree ready at /Users/jesse/myproject/.worktrees/auth
Tests passing (47 tests, 0 failures)
Ready to implement auth feature
```

## Red Flags

**Never:**
- Create worktree without verifying it's ignored (project-local)
- Skip baseline test verification
- Proceed with failing tests without asking
- Assume directory location when ambiguous
- Skip CLAUDE.md check

**Always:**
- Follow directory priority: existing > CLAUDE.md > ask
- Verify directory is ignored for project-local
- Auto-detect and run project setup
- Verify clean test baseline

## Integration

**Called by:**
- **brainstorming** (Phase 4) - REQUIRED when design is approved and implementation follows
- **subagent-driven-development** - REQUIRED before executing any tasks
- **executing-plans** - REQUIRED before executing any tasks
- Any skill needing isolated workspace

**Pairs with:**
- **finishing-a-development-branch** - REQUIRED for cleanup after work complete

case $LOCATION in
  .worktrees|worktrees)
    path="$LOCATION/$BRANCH_NAME"
    ;;
  ~/.config/superpowers/worktrees/*)
    path="~/.config/superpowers/worktrees/$project/$BRANCH_NAME"
    ;;
esac

# Create worktree with new branch
git worktree add "$path" -b "$BRANCH_NAME"
cd "$path"
```

### 3. Run Project Setup

Auto-detect and run appropriate setup:

```bash
# Node.js
if [ -f package.json ]; then npm install; fi

# Rust
if [ -f Cargo.toml ]; then cargo build; fi

# Python
if [ -f requirements.txt ]; then pip install -r requirements.txt; fi
if [ -f pyproject.toml ]; then poetry install; fi

# Go
if [ -f go.mod ]; then go mod download; fi
```

### 4. Verify Clean Baseline

Run tests to ensure worktree starts clean:

```bash
# Examples - use project-appropriate command
npm test
cargo test
pytest
go test ./...
```

**If tests fail:** Report failures, ask whether to proceed or investigate.

**If tests pass:** Report ready.

### 5. Report Location

```
Worktree ready at <full-path>
Tests passing (<N> tests, 0 failures)
Ready to implement <feature-name>
```

## Quick Reference

| Situation | Action |
|-----------|--------|
| `.worktrees/` exists | Use it (verify ignored) |
| `worktrees/` exists | Use it (verify ignored) |
| Both exist | Use `.worktrees/` |
| Neither exists | Check CLAUDE.md → Ask user |
| Directory not ignored | Add to .gitignore + commit |
| Tests fail during baseline | Report failures + ask |
| No package.json/Cargo.toml | Skip dependency install |

## Common Mistakes

### Skipping ignore verification

- **Problem:** Worktree contents get tracked, pollute git status
- **Fix:** Always use `git check-ignore` before creating project-local worktree

### Assuming directory location

- **Problem:** Creates inconsistency, violates project conventions
- **Fix:** Follow priority: existing > CLAUDE.md > ask

### Proceeding with failing tests

- **Problem:** Can't distinguish new bugs from pre-existing issues
- **Fix:** Report failures, get explicit permission to proceed

### Hardcoding setup commands

- **Problem:** Breaks on projects using different tools
- **Fix:** Auto-detect from project files (package.json, etc.)

## Example Workflow

```
You: I'm using the using-git-worktrees skill to set up an isolated workspace.

[Check .worktrees/ - exists]
[Verify ignored - git check-ignore confirms .worktrees/ is ignored]
[Create worktree: git worktree add .worktrees/auth -b feature/auth]
[Run npm install]
[Run npm test - 47 passing]

Worktree ready at /Users/jesse/myproject/.worktrees/auth
Tests passing (47 tests, 0 failures)
Ready to implement auth feature
```

## Red Flags

**Never:**
- Create worktree without verifying it's ignored (project-local)
- Skip baseline test verification
- Proceed with failing tests without asking
- Assume directory location when ambiguous
- Skip CLAUDE.md check

**Always:**
- Follow directory priority: existing > CLAUDE.md > ask
- Verify directory is ignored for project-local
- Auto-detect and run project setup
- Verify clean test baseline

## Integration

**Called by:**
- **brainstorming** (Phase 4) - REQUIRED when design is approved and implementation follows
- **subagent-driven-development** - REQUIRED before executing any tasks
- **executing-plans** - REQUIRED before executing any tasks
- Any skill needing isolated workspace

**Pairs with:**
- **finishing-a-development-branch** - REQUIRED for cleanup after work complete

## Foundation acceptance checklist

The foundation program is complete when the agreed outputs below are accepted,
not when every hypothetical architecture improvement has been attempted.

- **Ownership and reuse:** current consumers use the accepted interfaces; no
  competing policy owner or abandoned duplicate implementation remains.
- **Resource behavior:** comparable startup/idle/active/return-to-idle results
  meet the agreed budgets or an explicitly reviewed exception. Work queues,
  caches and retained metadata have limits and reclamation/recovery rules.
- **Sync and durability:** agreed current-IM cases cover interruption, reconnect,
  duplicate/reordered data, membership/revocation, deletion, restart and restore;
  outstanding topology/platform limitations are named.
- **Privacy and authority:** account/device meanings, accepted operations and
  observer/peer/relay exposure are explicit and enforced at the owning boundary.
- **Verification:** checks have meaningful assertions and local/CI/native roles;
  feedback latency and failure causes are observable. Missing evidence is not a pass.
- **Maintainability:** current behavior and important decisions are documented at
  their owners; future features can locate the contract and its regression checks.
- **Residual risk:** severe security/data-loss/recovery defects are resolved.
  Other gaps have an impact, owner and explicit disposition. Optional extensions
  cannot indefinitely delay foundation acceptance.

Numeric targets, representative data sizes, platforms and the mandatory scenario
set must be agreed from F01–F04 evidence before construction scope is accepted.
The existing [performance requirements](performance-requirements.md) and
[testing workflow](testing-feedback-loop.md) remain their authoritative owners;
this draft introduces no competing budget or gate policy.

from pathlib import Path
import json,hashlib
p=Path('docs/development-roadmap.md');s=p.read_text()
marker='## Foundation acceptance checklist\n'
section='''## Proposed mandatory versus optional scope

Use this boundary to make F10 finite. These are proposed classifications for the
next discussion, not assertions that a capability is currently missing or broken.
An existing implementation may satisfy the mandatory outcome through evidence.

| Area | Mandatory foundation outcome | Separate later feature or conditional work |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Module boundaries | Existing IM consumers have clear responsibility, policy ownership and lifecycle at the affected seams. | A generic framework for hypothetical consumers, public SDK packaging or arbitrary extension points. |
| Performance | Establish representative baselines, address the agreed high-impact findings and protect against recurrence. | Unlimited micro-optimization, new UI implementation or an unmeasured rewrite. |
| Monitoring | Obtain enough attributable observations to explain and verify the selected costs, including disabled-mode overhead. | Polished panel/menu-bar views, persistent chart history and user alerts. |
| Sync and transport | Qualify current personal/group exchange, authorized recovery, progress/resource bounds and compatibility in the agreed scenarios. | New transport families, global consensus, forum replication or browser gateways without a current-IM need. |
| Announcements and membership | Keep their authority/state semantics separate; define the transitions required by the selected current-IM scope, including pending/effective meanings. | A new announcement editor/history/confirmation UX solely to complete an architecture program. |
| Retention and capacity | Explain existing data categories, authority, limits, cleanup/recovery and their measured growth. | New quota-management screens, notification UX or automatic cleanup policies not yet agreed. |
| Deletion | Qualify the agreed local/account/recall meanings against relevant replay/restart/restore cases; preserve required deletion authority. | Marker compaction without measured need and a safe reclamation argument. |
| Privacy and unwanted contact | Establish identity, disclosure/admission and revocation boundaries; fix severe verified enforcement defects. | New stranger-request UX, broad product policy modes or endorsement counts. Practical controls remain prioritized after F10. |
| Verification and documentation | Maintain risk-based checks, resource regressions, source-bound evidence and discoverable rules/decisions. | Every named atlas tool on every PR, an exhaustive competitor survey or a second documentation system. |

If investigation reveals that a deferred interface is required to make an
existing invariant usable or enforceable, promote only that necessary slice with
its rationale and acceptance. Conversely, a desirable new feature does not become
mandatory merely because it could reuse a foundation module.

'''

# Development roadmap and requirements

## Discussion status and scope

This is the foundation-first roadmap discussion draft. The user requested a new
integration branch for this discussion and its document changes, with any later
parallel task branches returning to that branch. This draft replaces the earlier
execution ordering, task numbers and claim tables for the purpose of this
replanning exercise. It does not cancel other sessions' work, reassign their
claims, assert implementation status or authorize product changes.

The sole requirements input for this discussion is the user-supplied
`/Users/kingsonwu/Downloads/requirements-intake.md`, containing REQ-001–REQ-030.
That external file remains unchanged while discussion continues. Preserve the
original intent, confirmed constraints and reference leads when replacing its
outdated planning sections after agreement. The old roadmap, branch history and
task claims are not inputs to the proposed ordering below.

**Agreed direction:** establish the current messenger's foundations, performance
and reliable verification before starting major feature expansion. Forum, PWA,
client marketplace and similar extensions belong to future planning for now.

**Still proposed:** the exact foundation work packages, their dependencies,
acceptance scope, resource budgets and later feature order. There are no approved
implementation assignments, measurements, delivery dates or effort estimates in
this draft. Source inspection will determine whether each package requires a
change, qualification of existing behavior or a supported retain decision.

[Implementation status](../specifications/TODO.md) remains separate. This document
owns future requirements, sequencing, decisions and readiness; existing topic
guides own product rules, tests and operating procedures.

## Delivery policy

1. Define a finite foundation scope around current IM scenarios and real reuse.
   Do not implement speculative forum, browser or SDK architecture in advance.
2. Establish reproducible correctness and performance evidence before selecting
   major optimization, module extraction, database or UI changes.
3. Make boundaries useful: one policy owner, explicit inputs/results/errors,
   lifecycle and cancellation, durable commit authority and bounded resource use.
   A file split alone is not a completed module boundary.
4. Deliver and validate small changes to existing consumers. Preserve identity,
   privacy, wire/storage compatibility, delivery and recovery guarantees.
5. Accept the agreed foundation release before opening feature development.
   Severe verified security, data-loss or hard-freeze defects take precedence
   whenever discovered. Optional future ideas do not extend the foundation gate.
6. Keep performance, verification and decision records active throughout later
   work. Foundation acceptance does not mean these concerns are permanently done.

## Phases and exit criteria

| Phase                                 | Purpose and scope                                                                                                                | Exit evidence                                                                                                                                                           | Parallelism                                                                                                      |
| ------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 0. ### Sequencing within foundation construction

- Start with F01, then prepare F02/F03/F04 in parallel. Do not wait for an
  elaborate monitoring UI to collect performance evidence.
- Select the smallest useful F05 boundary changes. Publish their contract and
  migration order before other packages change the same callers or state owners.
- F06/F07/F08 can overlap once their required interface slices are accepted.
  Communication correctness improvements may proceed independently from history
  pagination; deletion semantics cannot proceed independently from replay rules.
- Pair each module/interface change with qualification of its existing consumer;
  optimize measured costs in the same or a following bounded slice. Do not defer
  every performance improvement until after an app-wide refactor.
- Deliver F09 with each slice. Assess F10 only after all mandatory scoped
  foundation outputs are accepted. Reopen an upstream contract deliberately when
  evidence invalidates it; do not silently patch incompatible rules downstream.

## Foundation acceptance checklist

The foundation program is complete when the agreed outputs below are accepted,
not when every hypothetical architecture improvement has been attempted.

- **Ownership and reuse:** current consumers use the accepted interfaces; no
  competing policy owner or abandoned duplicate implementation remains.
- **Resource behavior:** comparable startup/idle/active/return-to-idle results
  meet the agreed budgets or an explicitly reviewed exception. Work queues,
  caches and retained metadata have limits and reclamation/recovery rules.
- **Sync and durability:** agreed current-IM cases cover interruption, reconnect,
  duplicate/reordered data, membership/revocation, deletion, restart and restore;
  outstanding topology/platform limitations are named.
- **Privacy and authority:** account/device meanings, accepted operations and
  observer/peer/relay exposure are explicit and enforced at the owning boundary.
- **Verification:** checks have meaningful assertions and local/CI/native roles;
  feedback latency and failure causes are observable. Missing evidence is not a pass.
- **Maintainability:** current behavior and important decisions are documented at
  their owners; future features can locate the contract and its regression checks.
- **Residual risk:** severe security/data-loss/recovery defects are resolved.
  Other gaps have an impact, owner and explicit disposition. Optional extensions
  cannot indefinitely delay foundation acceptance.

Numeric targets, representative data sizes, platforms and the mandatory scenario
set must be agreed from F01–F04 evidence before construction scope is accepted.
The existing [performance requirements](performance-requirements.md) and
[testing workflow](testing-feedback-loop.md) remain their authoritative owners;
this draft introduces no competing budget or gate policy.
