from pathlib import Path
p=Path('docs/development-roadmap.md');s=p.read_text()
marker='## Proposed mandatory versus optional scope\n'
section='''## Proposed first waves and concrete handoffs

These waves turn package dependencies into a dispatch order without assigning
workers or authorizing implementation. They refine the draft, not the user's
confirmed product scope. Each accepted output is reusable; no lane must finish an
exhaustive survey before another lane can make a bounded change.

| Wave | Work admitted | Required handoff before the next wave |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A. Bound the current-IM program | F01: identify account/device/session meanings, current messaging/sync/file/history flows, storage categories and real owners. Select representative scenarios below. | One scoped list separating existing qualified behavior, unknowns, mandatory fixes/qualification and parked extensions. Assign a decision owner, not an assumed new module, to every boundary. |
| B. Prepare safe, measurable changes | F02 minimal affected safety checks and timing/failure baseline; F03 reproducible resource observations; F04 the authority/lifecycle rules needed by the selected scenarios. These three lanes may overlap. | A ranked first change list. Each entry names its user impact or measurable cost, invariant, actual owner/consumer, accepted input contract, test/recovery evidence and stop condition. Broad verification-method assessment continues through F09. |
| C. Integrate small foundation slices | Begin with the F05 seam needed by the highest-impact current-IM change; then execute independently ready F06/F07/F08 slices, each with F09. Keep instrumentation only where it supports diagnosis/regression with bounded cost. | One reviewed result per slice: change or retained behavior, migrated consumer, comparable resource result where affected, exercised failure/recovery cases and explicit remaining limits. Revisit the finding order after each meaningful result. |
| D. Qualify the integrated foundations | F10 rechecks the accepted scenarios on the integrated candidate and closes cross-lane compatibility gaps. | A clear accepted-scope result and residual-risk disposition before any post-foundation feature is activated. No automatic release, SDK publication or future-feature assignment. |

The first construction slice is intentionally not named as a timer rewrite,
database migration or networking replacement: requirement concerns do not prove
which mechanism is costly. Use measured user impact, risk and dependency value to
choose it. A clear high-impact optimization can precede unrelated module cleanup,
provided its own owner/contract and safety checks are understood. F05 is incremental,
not an app-wide rewrite that must finish before performance work can begin.

### Representative scenario proposal

This is the proposed minimum scenario inventory for scoping, not executed tests
or a claim that every scenario needs a new suite. F01–F04 must bind actual owners,
supported platforms, representative scales, observation windows and expected
outcomes before acceptance. Reuse existing adequate checks and record gaps.

| Scenario | Correctness and recovery observation | Cost / lifecycle observation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Startup and unlock with retained history | Usable current conversation, correct authority and durable history; interrupted initialization has a defined outcome. | Cold/warm identity, time to usable UI, peak working set and reads/writes; separate migrations and catch-up. |
| Settled visible and hidden idle | Message reception and required liveness remain available without unrelated history/setting reloads. | App process family, wakeups/CPU, disk/network work and unbounded queue/metadata growth; observe after real settling. |
| Direct and group messaging | Durable acceptance versus custody/recipient evidence, duplicate handling and policy checks remain distinct. | Interaction/reception latency and work/bytes as the chosen recipient scale changes; settle after delivery or bounded blocked retry. |
| Linked-device and group catch-up | Relevant duplicate/reordered/interrupted replay, membership/revocation and legitimate missing-history recovery. | Incremental transfer, progress and backpressure; no unchanged replay loop after completion. |
| History, search and repeated navigation | Bounded current view and correct access; stale results cannot replace another conversation/session. | Query/decode/render work and cache growth across repeated use, including return to idle. |
| Attachment transfer and media use | Chosen consent, cancellation, failed-source/retry and integrity/completion cases. | Transfer/decode bounds, temporary resources and memory/task cleanup after leave or replacement. |
| Delete, restart and restore | Agreed local/account/recall intent survives the relevant replay/recovery cases; unauthorized scope expansion is rejected. | Retained deletion evidence, index/marker growth and safe reclamation limits. No age-only marker deletion assumption. |
| Lock, logout, sleep/resume and owner replacement | Stale work loses commit authority; required recovery remains possible when the owner returns. | Work/subscriptions stop with their owner; background retry, cached state and outstanding workers have bounded lifetimes. |

### Parallel admission and integration rule

Read-only analysis may overlap. Before code changes, each slice must have an
accepted shared contract, nonoverlapping mutation ownership, an existing-consumer
migration plan and an integration order. F07/F08 share persisted sync/deletion
rules; F06/F07 share retry/progress ownership; metric and validation lanes share
measurement resources. Those are coordination boundaries, not permission for
concurrent conflicting edits. If an interface is still moving, parallelize
consumer/test preparation read-only or serialize the dependent mutations.

Do not turn a quiet-host measurement window into a blanket ban on parallel work:
other lanes can continue on separate machines or noninterfering inputs. Do not
interpret unlimited worker availability as unlimited review/native-test capacity.
After each merge to the integration branch, dependent branches consume the
accepted new interface before final qualification.

'''
assert marker in s;s=s.replace(marker,section+marker,1)
old='''First agree the finite mandatory scope of F05/F06/F07/F08: what must be improved
or qualified before F10, and what belongs to optional later work. In particular,
decide whether new announcement UX, capacity reminders and stranger-contact
policy UI are foundation deliverables or post-foundation IM improvements. Their
underlying authority, durability and resource rules belong in the foundation
either way. Then select representative scenarios and budgets from evidence and
approve the first bounded investigation/implementation plan separately.
'''
new='''Next agree the proposed scenario inventory and mandatory/optional boundary,
then start only the separately authorized Wave A/B investigation. A useful scope
decision is whether the foundation program qualifies current authority/data
behavior and fixes evidenced gaps while deferring new announcement, capacity and
stranger-request UI. This is the recommended draft boundary, not a completed user
decision. Select a construction slice only after its owner, safety checks,
resource evidence and acceptance criteria exist; complete those investigations
before asking for a product choice that the evidence can resolve.
'''
assert old in s;s=s.replace(old,new,1);p.write_text(s)
PY

| C：逐项建设 | 整理必要模块边界，并行推进调度、同步、存储优化 | 每项都有调用者迁移、效果和恢复验证 |
| D：整体验收 | 在同一集成版本上验证基础能力 | 达到约定标准，再开放功能开发 |

进一步明确了三点：

- **拆模块与性能优化交错推进**，避免先做一次漫长的全局重构。
- **并行取决于接口和责任是否稳定**。同步与存储涉及删除规则、调度与通信涉及重试规则时，需要统一协调。
- **基础必须有终点**：围绕启动、空闲、消息、同步、历史、附件、删除恢复和会话退出验收；论坛、PWA、市场不进入这一轮。

M docs/development-roadmap.md
# Development roadmap and requirements

## Discussion status and scope

This is the foundation-first roadmap discussion draft. The user requested a new
integration branch for this discussion and its document changes, with any later
parallel task branches returning to that branch. This draft replaces the earlier
execution ordering, task numbers and claim tables for the purpose of this
replanning exercise. It does not cancel other sessions' work, reassign their
claims, assert implementation status or authorize product changes.

The sole requirements input for this discussion is the user-supplied
`/Users/kingsonwu/Downloads/requirements-intake.md`, containing REQ-001–REQ-030.
That external file remains unchanged while discussion continues. Preserve the
original intent, confirmed constraints and reference leads when replacing its
outdated planning sections after agreement. The old roadmap, branch history and
task claims are not inputs to the proposed ordering below.

**Agreed direction:** establish the current messenger's foundations, performance
and reliable verification before starting major feature expansion. Forum, PWA,
client marketplace and similar extensions belong to future planning for now.

**Still proposed:** the exact foundation work packages, their dependencies,
acceptance scope, resource budgets and later feature order. There are no approved
implementation assignments, measurements, delivery dates or effort estimates in
this draft. Source inspection will determine whether each package requires a
change, qualification of existing behavior or a supported retain decision.

[Implementation status](../specifications/TODO.md) remains separate. This document
owns future requirements, sequencing, decisions and readiness; existing topic
guides own product rules, tests and operating procedures.

## Delivery policy

1. Define a finite foundation scope around current IM scenarios and real reuse.
   Do not implement speculative forum, browser or SDK architecture in advance.
2. Establish reproducible correctness and performance evidence before selecting
   major optimization, module extraction, database or UI changes.
3. Make boundaries useful: one policy owner, explicit inputs/results/errors,
   lifecycle and cancellation, durable commit authority and bounded resource use.
   A file split alone is not a completed module boundary.
4. Deliver and validate small changes to existing consumers. Preserve identity,
   privacy, wire/storage compatibility, delivery and recovery guarantees.
5. Accept the agreed foundation release before opening feature development.
   Severe verified security, data-loss or hard-freeze defects take precedence
   whenever discovered. Optional future ideas do not extend the foundation gate.
6. Keep performance, verification and decision records active throughout later
   work. Foundation acceptance does not mean these concerns are permanently done.

## Phases and exit criteria

## Branch and parallel-work agreement

The user requested `codex/requirements-foundation-plan` as the integration branch
for this replanning discussion and its resulting edits, in the registered
`.worktrees/requirements-foundation-plan` worktree. Retain it while discussion is
active. This does not replace other sessions' existing branches or claims.

- Keep the evolving discussion decisions in this roadmap. Temporary plans,
  provenance snapshots and ownership notes stay in ignored `tmp/`.
- Do not overwrite the Downloads intake until discussion is complete and the
  consolidated requirements/phase decisions are ready to replace stale content.
- No parallel workers are currently assigned. If useful, branch each independent
  document/research task from the accepted integration tip, recording its real
  parent, owned paths, inputs and interface/integration owner before edits.
- Merge reviewed, validated task results back into this integration branch in
  dependency order. One writer integrates shared roadmap/interface decisions.
  A child branch cannot silently broaden scope or start a parked feature.
- Integration into `main`, public PR/release activity and product implementation
  are separate actions under the repository's existing authorization and gates.
- Preserve and clean task-owned worktrees under [repository rules](../AGENTS.md).
  Keep branches needed by ongoing discussion or review; never sweep unrelated
  worktrees, force removal or discard changes to finish cleanup.

## Next discussion

Next agree the proposed scenario inventory and mandatory/optional boundary,
then start only the separately authorized Wave A/B investigation. A useful scope
decision is whether the foundation program qualifies current authority/data
behavior and fixes evidenced gaps while deferring new announcement, capacity and
stranger-request UI. This is the recommended draft boundary, not a completed user
decision. Select a construction slice only after its owner, safety checks,
resource evidence and acceptance criteria exist; complete those investigations
before asking for a product choice that the evidence can resolve.
- The `Node` (`node/node.rs`) wires identity + signed UDP **multicast** discovery
  (group `224.0.0.167`, port 47474) + Noise-encrypted TCP transport (`transport/`,
  low-level socket in `transport/net.rs`) + the content-addressed event log + DM/channel/
  file crypto. Messages are events synced as a bounded append-only log, account-addressed
  across a user's devices; optional offline custody via equal eligible post offices.
  Routed discovery and opt-in post-office federation connect reachable sites without
  joining their IP subnets. Wire formats are versioned bincode.
- See **`docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`** before changing crypto, sync, or transport;
  **`docs/network-design-reference.md`** owns the communication invariants,
  module contracts, resource budgets and topology acceptance boundaries.

## Maintaining standards as requirements change

- Before changing tests, fixtures, dependencies or workflows in ways that affect
  CI cost or reliability, read [CI maintenance](docs/ci-maintenance.md). Reuse
  existing owners, measure the affected cost, and preserve acceptance evidence;
  keep required-check policy in its existing owner.
- Before implementation, identify the existing decision owner, authoritative rule,
  observable acceptance criteria, affected consumers and required boundary evidence.
  Extend the owning implementation and `validation.json`; new business capabilities
  should link their guide and invariants. Explain an unchanged contract in the PR.
- Run `make standards-check` after adding/moving source or changing contracts. It
  checks structural ownership and maintained references, including new files; it
  does not prove assertion quality, semantic completeness or candidate readiness.
  Hooks inspect the working tree, so partially staged commits still need a clean
  committed-candidate check in CI. Frontend dependencies must be installed.
- When CI exposes a local omission or flaky fixture, fix the owning selector, task
  or fixture and add a focused regression. Review timing and selection evidence
  before changing policy. Follow the maintained
  [requirement maintenance loop](docs/testing-feedback-loop.md#maintaining-standards-across-requirements).

## Testing Guidelines

- Integration coverage in `crates/mesh-talk-core/tests/` and `node/node_tests.rs`; embed
  unit tests near the code. Networking/crypto changes ship a loopback integration assertion.
- Backend multi-process E2E via `make e2e` (CI: `e2e-backend.yml`); Playwright UI E2E via
  `cd frontend && npm run e2e` (CI: `e2e-ui.yml`).
- Do not run full suites or E2E automatically during ordinary feature work. Run
  the affected unit or integration tests as changes are made; run E2E and the
  comprehensive health gate on explicit request, for optional full local preparation,
  or in CI.
- See `docs/testing-feedback-loop.md` for selection examples and escalation triggers.
- Document executed validation commands in every PR; ensure `make test` passes
  locally or through its matching CI workspace suite before merge.

## Commit & Pull Request Guidelines

- Before changing product versions or release automation, read [the version lifecycle](docs/updates.md#version-ownership-and-lifecycle).
  Root `Cargo.toml` `[workspace.package].version` is authoritative. Use
  `node scripts/release/version.mjs check|sync|prepare VERSION` (the `VERSION` argument belongs
  to `prepare` only); do not hand-edit generated npm/Cargo lock metadata or introduce another
  version constant. Root private npm metadata is a checked release-tooling projection;
  frontend private metadata is versionless and Tauri inherits Cargo. Never broadly replace
  matching dependency, fixture, history, wire or schema versions. Keep source builds `BASE-dev`,
  Nightlies `BASE-nightly.RUN.ATTEMPT`, official tagged builds `BASE`, and standard SemVer ordering.
- Version/changelog preparation and next-development-target changes use reviewed PRs. Ordinary main

The user explicitly confirmed the complete objective for this round:

1. Finish and agree the global plan before beginning its product tasks. Resolve
   consolidation, mandatory foundation scope, priorities, phases, dependency and
   parallel-execution rules, acceptance and future-roadmap placement.
2. Once that plan is agreed, update **both** `AGENTS.md` and this roadmap on the
   planning integration branch. `AGENTS.md` owns durable agent execution and
   coordination rules and links here; this roadmap owns requirements, sequencing,
   task readiness and decision state. Do not duplicate the whole backlog in both.
3. Validate the concrete documentation candidate, publish through the existing
   PR process, obtain required reviews/current-head checks and squash-merge the
   planning changes into `main`. Do not directly push to main or bypass gates.
4. Re-read the accepted plan from the resulting main commit and begin a fresh
   task-execution cycle from that source. Select, claim, investigate/design,
   implement and validate tasks in dependency order; do not continue product work
   from an unmerged planning snapshot.
5. Permit parallel execution only when accepted inputs/interfaces are stable,
   mutation ownership is independent and the integration order is understood.
   Do not start a dependent task early when an upstream change is expected to
   invalidate it or require reimplementation after merge. Serialize uncertain
   shared-boundary work. An absence of foreseeable rework is an admission check,
   not a promise that incidental textual conflicts are impossible.

execution remain ahead. A request to continue this discussion is not evidence

future feature decision during this documentation round.

name: finishing-a-development-branch
description: Use when implementation is complete, all tests pass, and you need to decide how to integrate the work - guides completion of development work by presenting structured options for merge, PR, or cleanup
---

# Finishing a Development Branch

## Overview

Guide completion of development work by presenting clear options and handling chosen workflow.

**Core principle:** Verify tests → Present options → Execute choice → Clean up.

**Announce at start:** "I'm using the finishing-a-development-branch skill to complete this work."

## The Process

### Step 1: Verify Tests

**Before presenting options, verify tests pass:**

```bash
# Run project's test suite
npm test / cargo test / pytest / go test ./...
```

**If tests fail:**
```
Tests failing (<N> failures). Must fix before completing:

[Show failures]

Cannot proceed with merge/PR until tests pass.
```

Stop. Don't proceed to Step 2.

**If tests pass:** Continue to Step 2.

### Step 2: Determine Base Branch

```bash
# Try common base branches
git merge-base HEAD main 2>/dev/null || git merge-base HEAD master 2>/dev/null
```

Or ask: "This branch split from main - is that correct?"

### Step 3: Present Options

Present exactly these 4 options:

```
Implementation complete. What would you like to do?

1. Merge back to <base-branch> locally
2. Push and create a Pull Request
3. Keep the branch as-is (I'll handle it later)
4. Discard this work

Which option?
```

**Don't add explanation** - keep options concise.

### Step 4: Execute Choice

#### Option 1: Merge Locally

```bash
# Switch to base branch
git checkout <base-branch>

# Pull latest
git pull

# Merge feature branch
git merge <feature-branch>

# Verify tests on merged result
<test command>

# If tests pass
git branch -d <feature-branch>
```

Then: Cleanup worktree (Step 5)

#### Option 2: Push and Create PR

```bash
# Push branch
git push -u origin <feature-branch>

# Create PR
gh pr create --title "<title>" --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
## Summary
<2-3 bullets of what changed>

## Test Plan
- [ ] <verification steps>
EOF
)"
```

Then: Cleanup worktree (Step 5)

#### Option 3: Keep As-Is

Report: "Keeping branch <name>. Worktree preserved at <path>."

**Don't cleanup worktree.**

#### Option 4: Discard

**Confirm first:**
```
This will permanently delete:
- Branch <name>
- All commits: <commit-list>
- Worktree at <path>

Type 'discard' to confirm.
```

Wait for exact confirmation.

If confirmed:
```bash
git checkout <base-branch>
git branch -D <feature-branch>
```

Then: Cleanup worktree (Step 5)

### Step 5: Cleanup Worktree

**For Options 1, 2, 4:**

Check if in worktree:
```bash
git worktree list | grep $(git branch --show-current)
```

If yes:
```bash
git worktree remove <worktree-path>
```

**For Option 3:** Keep worktree.

## Quick Reference

| Option | Merge | Push | Keep Worktree | Cleanup Branch |
|--------|-------|------|---------------|----------------|
| 1. Merge locally | ✓ | - | - | ✓ |
| 2. Create PR | - | ✓ | ✓ | - |
| 3. Keep as-is | - | - | ✓ | - |
| 4. Discard | - | - | - | ✓ (force) |

## Common Mistakes

**Skipping test verification**
- **Problem:** Merge broken code, create failing PR
- **Fix:** Always verify tests before offering options

**Open-ended questions**
- **Problem:** "What should I do next?" → ambiguous
- **Fix:** Present exactly 4 structured options

**Automatic worktree cleanup**
- **Problem:** Remove worktree when might need it (Option 2, 3)
- **Fix:** Only cleanup for Options 1 and 4

**No confirmation for discard**
- **Problem:** Accidentally delete work
- **Fix:** Require typed "discard" confirmation

## Red Flags

**Never:**
- Proceed with failing tests
- Merge without verifying tests on result
- Delete work without confirmation
- Force-push without explicit request

**Always:**
- Verify tests before offering options
- Present exactly 4 options
- Get typed confirmation for Option 4
- Clean up worktree for Options 1 & 4 only

## Integration

**Called by:**
- **subagent-driven-development** (Step 7) - After all tasks complete
- **executing-plans** (Step 5) - After all batches complete

**Pairs with:**
- **using-git-worktrees** - Cleans up worktree created by that skill

# labali-git-auto-commit-rewrite

## NEVER

- **Never fabricate diff content** or invent changes not present in `git diff` output — a fabricated commit message is worse than no message; it destroys trust in git history.
- **Never amend a previous commit** — always create a new commit. Amending rewrites history and can silently overwrite commits that others (or hooks) have already acted on.
- **Never use `--no-verify`** to bypass pre-commit hooks — the hooks are the project's safety net; bypassing them defeats their purpose and masks real issues.
- **Never write a body that only lists filenames** — `- update core.ts` tells nothing; name the intent behind the change, not the file that changed.

## Commit Type Selection

| Type | When to use |
|------|-------------|
| `feat` | New capability or behavior visible to users/agents |
| `fix` | Corrects wrong behavior (not just wrong output) |
| `docs` | Documentation, examples, references only — no behavior change |
| `chore` | Housekeeping: structure, config, scripts, CI — no behavior change |
| `refactor` | Code restructure with no behavior change |
| `improve` | Meaningful enhancement to existing behavior (not a new feature, not a bug fix) |
| `perf` | Performance improvement |
| `test` | Test additions or changes only |

**Scope selection:** use a scope when the change is confined to one clear subsystem — `fix(browser): ...`, `feat(skill): ...`. Omit scope for cross-cutting changes that span multiple subsystems.

**When types conflict:** if a commit spans both a behavior change and a structural change, use the behavior-change type (`feat`/`fix`/`improve`) — structural changes are secondary to their purpose. If the two concerns are truly independent, split into two commits.

## Execution Contract

1. Inspect working tree changes (`git status --short`, `git diff --name-status`) before writing message.
2. Before writing the subject, determine: is this a behavior change (`feat`/`fix`/`improve`) or a structural change (`docs`/`chore`/`refactor`)? This choice drives the type.
   Generate a commit message that is both clear and elegant:
   - Subject format: `<type>(<scope>): <subject>` or `<type>: <subject>`
   - Subject is concise, action-oriented, and specific to the dominant change set.
   - Body contains 2-6 bullet points, each tied to real grouped changes from diff.
   - Avoid vague wording like only `update`/`align` when multiple meaningful changes exist.
   - **MANDATORY — load `examples/good.md` before writing the message** to calibrate quality. Load `examples/anti-pattern.md` if the draft message feels vague or generic.
3. Stage all changes with `git add -A`.
4. Commit once with the generated subject and body. The commit command MUST be prefixed with `LABALI_SKILL_COMMIT=1` so the repository's pre-commit hook recognizes it as skill-authorized:
   ```bash
   LABALI_SKILL_COMMIT=1 git commit -m "..."
   ```
5. MUST run `<skill_base_dir>/scripts/clean_commit.sh` immediately after commit (non-optional).
   The skill base directory is provided in the `Base directory for this skill:` line at the top of the invocation header.
   `clean_commit.sh` may rewrite the subject — read the final hash and subject from its output, not from the original commit.

## Message Quality Rules

- Body bullets must reflect actual file-level intent, not generic placeholders.
- Prefer aggregate summaries when many files changed, then include concrete sub-actions in body.

## Failure Handling

- If repository is not a Git repo, fail fast with explicit message.
- If there are no changes to commit, return `No changes to commit.`.

## Resources

| When | Must load | Do NOT load |
|------|-----------|-------------|
| Always — before writing the message | `examples/good.md` | `examples/anti-pattern.md` |

# Finishing a Development Branch

## Overview

Guide completion of development work by presenting clear options and handling chosen workflow.

**Core principle:** Verify tests → Present options → Execute choice → Clean up.

**Announce at start:** "I'm using the finishing-a-development-branch skill to complete this work."

## The Process

### Step 1: Verify Tests

**Before presenting options, verify tests pass:**

```bash
# Run project's test suite
npm test / cargo test / pytest / go test ./...
```

**If tests fail:**
```
Tests failing (<N> failures). Must fix before completing:

[Show failures]

Cannot proceed with merge/PR until tests pass.
```

Stop. Don't proceed to Step 2.

**If tests pass:** Continue to Step 2.

### Step 2: Determine Base Branch

```bash
# Try common base branches
git merge-base HEAD main 2>/dev/null || git merge-base HEAD master 2>/dev/null
```

Or ask: "This branch split from main - is that correct?"

### Step 3: Present Options

Present exactly these 4 options:

```
Implementation complete. What would you like to do?

1. Merge back to <base-branch> locally
2. Push and create a Pull Request
3. Keep the branch as-is (I'll handle it later)
4. Discard this work

Which option?
```

**Don't add explanation** - keep options concise.

### Step 4: Execute Choice

#### Option 1: Merge Locally

```bash
# Switch to base branch
git checkout <base-branch>

# Pull latest
git pull

# Merge feature branch
git merge <feature-branch>

# Verify tests on merged result
<test command>

# If tests pass
git branch -d <feature-branch>
```

Then: Cleanup worktree (Step 5)

#### Option 2: Push and Create PR

```bash
# Push branch
git push -u origin <feature-branch>

# Create PR
gh pr create --title "<title>" --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
## Summary
<2-3 bullets of what changed>

## Test Plan
- [ ] <verification steps>
EOF
)"
```

Then: Cleanup worktree (Step 5)

#### Option 3: Keep As-Is

Report: "Keeping branch <name>. Worktree preserved at <path>."

**Don't cleanup worktree.**

#### Option 4: Discard

**Confirm first:**
```
This will permanently delete:
- Branch <name>
- All commits: <commit-list>
- Worktree at <path>

Type 'discard' to confirm.
```

Wait for exact confirmation.

If confirmed:
```bash
git checkout <base-branch>
git branch -D <feature-branch>
```

Then: Cleanup worktree (Step 5)

### Step 5: Cleanup Worktree

**For Options 1, 2, 4:**

Check if in worktree:
```bash
git worktree list | grep $(git branch --show-current)
```

If yes:
```bash
git worktree remove <worktree-path>
```

**For Option 3:** Keep worktree.

## Quick Reference

| Option | Merge | Push | Keep Worktree | Cleanup Branch |
|--------|-------|------|---------------|----------------|
| 1. Merge locally | ✓ | - | - | ✓ |
| 2. Create PR | - | ✓ | ✓ | - |
| 3. Keep as-is | - | - | ✓ | - |
| 4. Discard | - | - | - | ✓ (force) |

## Common Mistakes

**Skipping test verification**
- **Problem:** Merge broken code, create failing PR
- **Fix:** Always verify tests before offering options

**Open-ended questions**
- **Problem:** "What should I do next?" → ambiguous
- **Fix:** Present exactly 4 structured options

**Automatic worktree cleanup**
- **Problem:** Remove worktree when might need it (Option 2, 3)
- **Fix:** Only cleanup for Options 1 and 4

**No confirmation for discard**
- **Problem:** Accidentally delete work
- **Fix:** Require typed "discard" confirmation

## Red Flags

**Never:**
- Proceed with failing tests
- Merge without verifying tests on result
- Delete work without confirmation
- Force-push without explicit request

**Always:**
- Verify tests before offering options
- Present exactly 4 options
- Get typed confirmation for Option 4
- Clean up worktree for Options 1 & 4 only

## Integration

**Called by:**
- **subagent-driven-development** (Step 7) - After all tasks complete
- **executing-plans** (Step 5) - After all batches complete

**Pairs with:**
- **using-git-worktrees** - Cleans up worktree created by that skill

# labali-git-auto-commit-rewrite

## NEVER

- **Never fabricate diff content** or invent changes not present in `git diff` output — a fabricated commit message is worse than no message; it destroys trust in git history.
- **Never amend a previous commit** — always create a new commit. Amending rewrites history and can silently overwrite commits that others (or hooks) have already acted on.
- **Never use `--no-verify`** to bypass pre-commit hooks — the hooks are the project's safety net; bypassing them defeats their purpose and masks real issues.
- **Never write a body that only lists filenames** — `- update core.ts` tells nothing; name the intent behind the change, not the file that changed.

## Commit Type Selection

| Type | When to use |
|------|-------------|
| `feat` | New capability or behavior visible to users/agents |
| `fix` | Corrects wrong behavior (not just wrong output) |
| `docs` | Documentation, examples, references only — no behavior change |
| `chore` | Housekeeping: structure, config, scripts, CI — no behavior change |
| `refactor` | Code restructure with no behavior change |
| `improve` | Meaningful enhancement to existing behavior (not a new feature, not a bug fix) |
| `perf` | Performance improvement |
| `test` | Test additions or changes only |

**Scope selection:** use a scope when the change is confined to one clear subsystem — `fix(browser): ...`, `feat(skill): ...`. Omit scope for cross-cutting changes that span multiple subsystems.

**When types conflict:** if a commit spans both a behavior change and a structural change, use the behavior-change type (`feat`/`fix`/`improve`) — structural changes are secondary to their purpose. If the two concerns are truly independent, split into two commits.

## Execution Contract

1. Inspect working tree changes (`git status --short`, `git diff --name-status`) before writing message.
2. Before writing the subject, determine: is this a behavior change (`feat`/`fix`/`improve`) or a structural change (`docs`/`chore`/`refactor`)? This choice drives the type.
   Generate a commit message that is both clear and elegant:
   - Subject format: `<type>(<scope>): <subject>` or `<type>: <subject>`
   - Subject is concise, action-oriented, and specific to the dominant change set.
   - Body contains 2-6 bullet points, each tied to real grouped changes from diff.
   - Avoid vague wording like only `update`/`align` when multiple meaningful changes exist.
   - **MANDATORY — load `examples/good.md` before writing the message** to calibrate quality. Load `examples/anti-pattern.md` if the draft message feels vague or generic.
3. Stage all changes with `git add -A`.
4. Commit once with the generated subject and body. The commit command MUST be prefixed with `LABALI_SKILL_COMMIT=1` so the repository's pre-commit hook recognizes it as skill-authorized:
   ```bash
   LABALI_SKILL_COMMIT=1 git commit -m "..."
   ```
5. MUST run `<skill_base_dir>/scripts/clean_commit.sh` immediately after commit (non-optional).
   The skill base directory is provided in the `Base directory for this skill:` line at the top of the invocation header.
   `clean_commit.sh` may rewrite the subject — read the final hash and subject from its output, not from the original commit.

## Message Quality Rules

- Body bullets must reflect actual file-level intent, not generic placeholders.
- Prefer aggregate summaries when many files changed, then include concrete sub-actions in body.

## Failure Handling

- If repository is not a Git repo, fail fast with explicit message.
- If there are no changes to commit, return `No changes to commit.`.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Publish promptly after cheap checks; comprehensive validation runs in PR CI.
set -euo pipefail

repo_root="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
cd "$repo_root"

preflight_args=()
affected_args=()
full_preflight=0
separator=0
while [ "$#" -gt 0 ]; do
    if [ "$1" = "--" ]; then
        separator=1
        shift
        break
    fi
    if [ "$1" = "--full-preflight" ]; then
        full_preflight=1
        shift
        continue
    fi
    if [ "$1" = "--owner" ] || [ "$1" = "--reason" ]; then
        if [ "$#" -lt 2 ]; then
            echo "$1 requires a literal value." >&2
            exit 2
        fi
        affected_args+=("$1" "$2")
        shift 2
        continue
    fi
    preflight_args+=("$1")
    shift
done
if [ "$separator" -ne 1 ]; then
    echo "Usage: scripts/create-pr.sh [--full-preflight] [--owner ID --reason TEXT] [preflight selectors and UI specs] -- [gh pr create options]" >&2
    exit 2
fi
if [ -n "${GH_REPO:-}" ]; then
    echo "Unset GH_REPO: verified PR creation uses this checkout's repository." >&2
    exit 2
fi
for arg in "$@"; do
    case "$arg" in
        --head|--head=*|-H*|--repo|--repo=*|-R*|--base|--base=*|-B*)
            echo "Head/repository overrides are forbidden. Select the shared comparison/PR base before --." >&2
            exit 2
            ;;
    esac
done

# Bash 3.2 treats an empty array as unset under nounset.
base_ref="$(node --input-type=module - ${preflight_args[@]+"${preflight_args[@]}"} <<'JS'
import { parseFlags } from './scripts/pr-platform/plan.mjs';
const flags = parseFlags(['--base', process.env.PATCH_COVERAGE_BASE ?? 'origin/main', ...process.argv.slice(2)]);
if (flags.planOnly) throw Error('Preview with scripts/pr-platform/run.mjs --plan; creation publishes a PR.');
console.log(flags.base);
JS
)"
case "$base_ref" in
    origin/*) pr_base="${base_ref#origin/}" ;;
    *)
        echo "The PR base must be an origin/<branch> tracking ref, not a local revision." >&2
        exit 2
        ;;
esac
git check-ref-format --branch "$pr_base" >/dev/null

base_sha="$(git rev-parse --verify "$base_ref")"
candidate="$(git rev-parse HEAD)"
if [ -n "$(git status --porcelain)" ]; then
    echo "Commit or stash changes before creating a PR." >&2

fi

mkdir -p target/validation
if ! node scripts/validation/changed.mjs --cheap --base "$base_ref" ${affected_args[@]+"${affected_args[@]}"} --json > target/validation/pr-plan.json; then
    echo "PR readiness is blocked. Resolve the cheap-check failures or affected-plan blockers in target/validation/pr-plan.json before publishing." >&2
    exit 1
fi

    echo "The candidate or comparison base changed during PR checks. Retry with the committed revision." >&2

fi
exec gh pr create --base "$pr_base" "$@"

# Git Commit Standards for Mesh-Talk

To maintain clear and consistent commit history, we follow professional Git commit standards.

## Commit Message Format

```
<type>(<scope>): <subject>

<body>

<footer>
```

## Commit Types

- `feat`: New feature
- `fix`: Bug fix
- `bug`: Bug fix (synonymous with `fix`)
- `docs`: Documentation update
- `style`: Code formatting adjustment
- `refactor`: Code refactoring
- `perf`: Performance optimization
- `test`: Test-related
- `build`: Build system or external dependency changes
- `ci`: CI configuration files and script changes
- `chore`: Other changes that don't modify src or test files
- `revert`: Rollback previous commit

## Scope

Scope should identify the component or module affected by the commit:

- `network`
- `crypto`
- `ui`
- `db`
- `core`
- `cli`
- `tests`
- `config`

## Commit Message Standards

1. Write commit messages in English
2. First line is a brief description (<72 characters)
3. Second line must be a genuine blank line
4. Third line onwards is detailed description (optional)
5. Detailed description can include change reasons, impact scope, and other information
6. Make sure not to include temporary files generated during builds

## Examples

```
feat(discovery): sign UDP announce and group devices by account

- Add Ed25519 signature over the announce payload
- Carry the device certificate and verify it against the account key
- Group discovered devices by account in the roster
```

```
fix(ratchet): resolve session establishment failure

- Fix race condition in double ratchet initialization
- Add proper error handling for key exchange failures
- Update unit tests to cover edge cases
```

## Signing & Hooks

Commits **must be GPG-signed**. `scripts/setup-hooks.sh` (run by `make dev`) points
`core.hooksPath` at `hooks/` and enables `commit.gpgsign`; the `pre-push` hook rejects any
commit lacking a `gpgsig`. The `pre-commit` hook checks staged whitespace and
source formatting, ownership, hygiene and changed-script/workflow syntax; run
affected tests during development and the required gates before merge. Hook
installation does not run comprehensive health. Generate a key with `gpg --full-generate-key` and set it via
`git config --global user.signingkey <KEY_ID>` if you don't have one.

## Pull Request Merge Strategy

When the user asks to merge a pull request, use **squash merge by default**
(`gh pr merge --squash <PR>`), unless the user explicitly requests another
strategy. Use a clear Conventional Commit title and a final message describing
the completed change rather than its intermediate debugging history.

A merge request authorizes the merge only after the current PR head passes all
required checks and repository review requirements. Recheck the exact head before
merging; local checks, earlier green runs and the default strategy do not bypass
those gates. Follow the repository's worktree cleanup and branch-preservation
rules after integration.
# Repository Guidelines

## Reliability before implementation

- For background work, synchronization, storage, caching or UI-state changes, read
  [performance requirements](docs/performance-requirements.md). Identify the work
  trigger, resource budget, accumulation/reclamation policy and applicable
  performance regression before editing; record measured limits and remaining
  gaps. Apply its [startup, idle and active-business checklist](docs/performance-requirements.md#apply-to-every-feature)
  to every affected phase, including return to idle after use. Extend its general
  rules when a confirmed defect reveals a new pattern.

- Before implementing, refactoring, fixing or reviewing code, read the
  [AI coding reliability guide](docs/ai-coding-reliability.md), select the rules
  triggered by the changed boundaries, and inspect the owning code and callers.
  For concurrency/lifecycle changes, trace lock order, wait dependencies, actual
  work ownership, cancellation and commit authority before editing.
- Validate the applicable failure and recovery paths, not only the happy path.
  Record concrete evidence and remaining limits; a timeout, successful build or
  passing subset is not proof that UI freezes or all deadlocks are impossible.
- When a confirmed defect exposes a reusable failure pattern, update that guide's
  existing rule or add a distinct rule with its owner and regression evidence.
  Maintain the owning contract and test selectors; keep incident logs out of the guide.

## Project Structure & Module Organization

- Four-crate Rust workspace. `crates/mesh-talk-core/` is the UI-free protocol core (lib
  `mesh_talk_core` + the `mesh-talk-node` CLI bin in `src/bin/`): feature modules `node/`,
  `identity/`, `transport/`, `discovery/`, `eventlog/`, `ratchet/`, `channel/`, `dm.rs`,
  `file/`, `postoffice/`, `storage/`. `src-tauri/` is the Tauri desktop app: entry
  `src/main.rs` → `lib.rs`, IPC glue in `commands.rs` (auth) + `chat_commands/` (messaging)
  - `events.rs`, plus `state.rs`, `tray.rs`, `services/` (auth only).
- `crates/mesh-talk-integrations/` owns scoped local messaging grants, private IPC,
  and the dedicated bot host/admin CLI; `crates/mesh-talk-mcp/` adapts its four
  send/context/status tools to the official MCP SDK. Neither owns mesh crypto.
- Integration/e2e suites live in `crates/mesh-talk-core/tests/` (`two_node_cli`,
  `persistent_history`, `post_office_offline`, `decoder_smoke`); keep unit tests inline via
  `mod tests` (e.g. `node/node_tests.rs`).
- React client sits in `frontend/src`; Vite tooling in `frontend/package.json`.
- Operational scripts in `scripts/` (`setup-hooks.sh`, `check-health.sh`); architecture in
  `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`; conventions in `specifications/`. The
  [documentation map](docs/README.md) routes readers to maintained guides; the
  [documentation guidelines](docs/DOCUMENTATION_GUIDELINES.md) define ownership
  across the README, guides, and project site.

## Build, Test, and Development Commands

- `make dev` primes Rust + Node deps and installs git hooks.
- `make build` / `make frontend-build` — release build / Vite production build.
- During feature development, preview changed-boundary validation with `make test-plan`
  and run it with `make test-changed`. Unmapped changes require an explicit owner
  and reason; inspect escalation notes for browser/native or consumer checks.
  Use `make verify-plan` / `make verify-changed` at task completion to compose the
  same affected tests with applicable formatting, lint/types and builds. The
  test-only commands do not include static checks; neither mode replaces required
  PR/review, browser/native or release gates. `make validation-report` separates
  queue and execution costs; `make validation-audit` compares a clean affected
  plan with same-source broader failure evidence before narrowing any gate.
  Read selected capability references and inspect pending browser/native requirements.
  Execution prints a structured feedback report; follow the
  [validation protocol](docs/testing-feedback-loop.md#validation-stages-and-agent-responsibilities)
  for completed work, remaining evidence and additive semantic selections.
- During feature development, run affected tests only: `make test-focused
TEST_PACKAGE=mesh-talk-core TEST_FILTER=node::account_sync` selects Rust unit
  tests; add `TEST_TARGET=bridge_cross_lan` to select one integration target.
  `cd frontend && npm test -- src/features/chat/settingsDialogSession.test.ts`
  selects a frontend unit file. `make test` runs the full workspace suite
  (`cargo test --workspace`) for pre-PR and CI gates;
  `make e2e` runs the `#[ignore]`d multi-process backend rigs; `cd frontend && npm run e2e`
  runs the Playwright UI suite. Test builds use cheap KDF params (the `fast-test-kdf`
  feature), and `.cargo/config.toml` caps test/compile parallelism.
- UI / node spot checks: `make tauri-dev`, `make frontend-dev`,
  `cargo run -p mesh-talk-core --bin mesh-talk-node -- --keystore /tmp/a.keystore
--password pw --name alice` (add `--post-office` for relay mode).

## Coding Style & Naming Conventions

- Rust: `cargo fmt` (4-space, `snake_case` modules, `UpperCamelCase` types) +
  **`cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`** (must match CI — `--all-targets` covers
  tests/benches).
- Frontend: `npm run format` (Prettier) + `npm run lint` (ESLint flat config).
- Write documentation and reusable prompts in English unless a specific exception is needed.
- Reference `specifications/development_conventions.md` for naming nuances.

## Domain Language

- `CONTEXT.md` is the canonical domain glossary. `docs/domain-design.md` indexes
  the modeling references and defines DDD vocabulary and naming translations.

repo_root="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
cd "$repo_root"

preflight_args=()
affected_args=()
full_preflight=0
separator=0
while [ "$#" -gt 0 ]; do
    if [ "$1" = "--" ]; then
        separator=1
        shift
        break
    fi
    if [ "$1" = "--full-preflight" ]; then
        full_preflight=1
        shift
        continue
    fi
    if [ "$1" = "--owner" ] || [ "$1" = "--reason" ]; then
        if [ "$#" -lt 2 ]; then
            echo "$1 requires a literal value." >&2
            exit 2
        fi
        affected_args+=("$1" "$2")
        shift 2
        continue
    fi
    preflight_args+=("$1")
    shift
done
if [ "$separator" -ne 1 ]; then
    echo "Usage: scripts/create-pr.sh [--full-preflight] [--owner ID --reason TEXT] [preflight selectors and UI specs] -- [gh pr create options]" >&2
    exit 2
fi
if [ -n "${GH_REPO:-}" ]; then

for arg in "$@"; do
    case "$arg" in

import { parseFlags } from './scripts/pr-platform/plan.mjs';

console.log(flags.base);

)"
case "$base_ref" in

    *)

        exit 2
        ;;
esac
git check-ref-format --branch "$pr_base" >/dev/null

# Git Commit Standards for Mesh-Talk

To maintain clear and consistent commit history, we follow professional Git commit standards.

## Commit Message Format

```
<type>(<scope>): <subject>

<body>

<footer>
```

## Commit Types

- `feat`: New feature
- `fix`: Bug fix
- `bug`: Bug fix (synonymous with `fix`)
- `docs`: Documentation update
- `style`: Code formatting adjustment
- `refactor`: Code refactoring
- `perf`: Performance optimization
- `test`: Test-related
- `build`: Build system or external dependency changes
- `ci`: CI configuration files and script changes
- `chore`: Other changes that don't modify src or test files
- `revert`: Rollback previous commit

## Scope

Scope should identify the component or module affected by the commit:

- `network`
- `crypto`
- `ui`
- `db`
- `core`
- `cli`
- `tests`
- `config`

## Commit Message Standards

1. Write commit messages in English
2. First line is a brief description (<72 characters)
3. Second line must be a genuine blank line
4. Third line onwards is detailed description (optional)
5. Detailed description can include change reasons, impact scope, and other information
6. Make sure not to include temporary files generated during builds

## Examples

```
feat(discovery): sign UDP announce and group devices by account

- Add Ed25519 signature over the announce payload
- Carry the device certificate and verify it against the account key
- Group discovered devices by account in the roster
```

```
fix(ratchet): resolve session establishment failure

- Fix race condition in double ratchet initialization
- Add proper error handling for key exchange failures
- Update unit tests to cover edge cases
```

## Signing & Hooks

Commits **must be GPG-signed**. `scripts/setup-hooks.sh` (run by `make dev`) points
`core.hooksPath` at `hooks/` and enables `commit.gpgsign`; the `pre-push` hook rejects any
commit lacking a `gpgsig`. The `pre-commit` hook checks staged whitespace and
source formatting, ownership, hygiene and changed-script/workflow syntax; run
affected tests during development and the required gates before merge. Hook
installation does not run comprehensive health. Generate a key with `gpg --full-generate-key` and set it via
`git config --global user.signingkey <KEY_ID>` if you don't have one.

## Pull Request Merge Strategy

When the user asks to merge a pull request, use **squash merge by default**
(`gh pr merge --squash <PR>`), unless the user explicitly requests another
strategy. Use a clear Conventional Commit title and a final message describing
the completed change rather than its intermediate debugging history.

A merge request authorizes the merge only after the current PR head passes all
required checks and repository review requirements. Recheck the exact head before
merging; local checks, earlier green runs and the default strategy do not bypass
those gates. Follow the repository's worktree cleanup and branch-preservation
rules after integration.
# Repository Guidelines

## Reliability before implementation

- For background work, synchronization, storage, caching or UI-state changes, read
  [performance requirements](docs/performance-requirements.md). Identify the work
  trigger, resource budget, accumulation/reclamation policy and applicable
  performance regression before editing; record measured limits and remaining
  gaps. Apply its [startup, idle and active-business checklist](docs/performance-requirements.md#apply-to-every-feature)
  to every affected phase, including return to idle after use. Extend its general
  rules when a confirmed defect reveals a new pattern.

- Before implementing, refactoring, fixing or reviewing code, read the
  [AI coding reliability guide](docs/ai-coding-reliability.md), select the rules
  triggered by the changed boundaries, and inspect the owning code and callers.
  For concurrency/lifecycle changes, trace lock order, wait dependencies, actual
  work ownership, cancellation and commit authority before editing.
- Validate the applicable failure and recovery paths, not only the happy path.
  Record concrete evidence and remaining limits; a timeout, successful build or
  passing subset is not proof that UI freezes or all deadlocks are impossible.
- When a confirmed defect exposes a reusable failure pattern, update that guide's
  existing rule or add a distinct rule with its owner and regression evidence.
  Maintain the owning contract and test selectors; keep incident logs out of the guide.

## Project Structure & Module Organization

- Four-crate Rust workspace. `crates/mesh-talk-core/` is the UI-free protocol core (lib
  `mesh_talk_core` + the `mesh-talk-node` CLI bin in `src/bin/`): feature modules `node/`,
  `identity/`, `transport/`, `discovery/`, `eventlog/`, `ratchet/`, `channel/`, `dm.rs`,
  `file/`, `postoffice/`, `storage/`. `src-tauri/` is the Tauri desktop app: entry
  `src/main.rs` → `lib.rs`, IPC glue in `commands.rs` (auth) + `chat_commands/` (messaging)
  - `events.rs`, plus `state.rs`, `tray.rs`, `services/` (auth only).
- `crates/mesh-talk-integrations/` owns scoped local messaging grants, private IPC,
  and the dedicated bot host/admin CLI; `crates/mesh-talk-mcp/` adapts its four
  send/context/status tools to the official MCP SDK. Neither owns mesh crypto.
- Integration/e2e suites live in `crates/mesh-talk-core/tests/` (`two_node_cli`,
  `persistent_history`, `post_office_offline`, `decoder_smoke`); keep unit tests inline via
  `mod tests` (e.g. `node/node_tests.rs`).
- React client sits in `frontend/src`; Vite tooling in `frontend/package.json`.
- Operational scripts in `scripts/` (`setup-hooks.sh`, `check-health.sh`); architecture in
  `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`; conventions in `specifications/`. The
  [documentation map](docs/README.md) routes readers to maintained guides; the
  [documentation guidelines](docs/DOCUMENTATION_GUIDELINES.md) define ownership
  across the README, guides, and project site.

## Build, Test, and Development Commands

- `make dev` primes Rust + Node deps and installs git hooks.
- `make build` / `make frontend-build` — release build / Vite production build.
- During feature development, preview changed-boundary validation with `make test-plan`
  and run it with `make test-changed`. Unmapped changes require an explicit owner
  and reason; inspect escalation notes for browser/native or consumer checks.
  Use `make verify-plan` / `make verify-changed` at task completion to compose the
  same affected tests with applicable formatting, lint/types and builds. The
  test-only commands do not include static checks; neither mode replaces required
  PR/review, browser/native or release gates. `make validation-report` separates
  queue and execution costs; `make validation-audit` compares a clean affected
  plan with same-source broader failure evidence before narrowing any gate.
  Read selected capability references and inspect pending browser/native requirements.
  Execution prints a structured feedback report; follow the
  [validation protocol](docs/testing-feedback-loop.md#validation-stages-and-agent-responsibilities)
  for completed work, remaining evidence and additive semantic selections.
- During feature development, run affected tests only: `make test-focused
TEST_PACKAGE=mesh-talk-core TEST_FILTER=node::account_sync` selects Rust unit
  tests; add `TEST_TARGET=bridge_cross_lan` to select one integration target.
  `cd frontend && npm test -- src/features/chat/settingsDialogSession.test.ts`
  selects a frontend unit file. `make test` runs the full workspace suite
  (`cargo test --workspace`) for pre-PR and CI gates;
  `make e2e` runs the `#[ignore]`d multi-process backend rigs; `cd frontend && npm run e2e`
  runs the Playwright UI suite. Test builds use cheap KDF params (the `fast-test-kdf`
  feature), and `.cargo/config.toml` caps test/compile parallelism.
- UI / node spot checks: `make tauri-dev`, `make frontend-dev`,
  `cargo run -p mesh-talk-core --bin mesh-talk-node -- --keystore /tmp/a.keystore
--password pw --name alice` (add `--post-office` for relay mode).

## Coding Style & Naming Conventions

- Rust: `cargo fmt` (4-space, `snake_case` modules, `UpperCamelCase` types) +
  **`cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`** (must match CI — `--all-targets` covers
  tests/benches).
- Frontend: `npm run format` (Prettier) + `npm run lint` (ESLint flat config).
- Write documentation and reusable prompts in English unless a specific exception is needed.
- Reference `specifications/development_conventions.md` for naming nuances.

## Domain Language

- `CONTEXT.md` is the canonical domain glossary. `docs/domain-design.md` indexes
  the modeling references and defines DDD vocabulary and naming translations.
- Distinguish local users, accounts and devices; desktop, transport and ratchet
  sessions; discovery, presence, custody, recipient delivery and read state.
