# Development roadmap and requirements

## Plan ownership and execution boundary

This is the maintained global plan for the thirty user-supplied requirements,
REQ-001–REQ-030. It owns consolidation, priority, dependencies, phase exits,
readiness, task claims and future directions. The original intake is provenance,
not a competing execution backlog. The complete source mapping below preserves
all thirty requirements. The previous T-numbered execution proposal is superseded;
its numbers or historical claims are not evidence of readiness in this plan.
Existing work owned by other sessions must still be checked before claiming a task.

The delivery order is **foundations → integrated foundation acceptance → current
IM improvements → separately activated future features**. Performance, security,
verification and maintained decisions apply throughout. Forum, mobile PWA,
marketplace, external SDK and other extensions are not current assignments.

This planning change updates [agent rules](../AGENTS.md) and this roadmap together.
It must pass the existing PR/review/current-head gates and merge into `main`
before execution starts. After merge, read the accepted main revision afresh,
claim F01 and follow the dependency rules below. A planning merge does not prove
that foundations, measurements or product acceptance are complete. No public
release or product implementation belongs in the planning PR.

[Implementation status](../specifications/TODO.md) owns implemented capabilities;
[module ownership](module-boundaries.md) owns implementation responsibilities.
Existing topic guides retain authority over product/security/resource rules.
Do not invent historical rationale, measurements, deadlines or effort estimates.
Unknown implementation facts are explicit inputs to bounded investigations.

## Priority and readiness

| Priority     | Scope                                                                             | Admission rule                                                                                                                                                                        |
| ------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| P0           | F01–F10: finite foundations for current IM, including performance and validation. | First F01; then independent evidence/contract lanes; construction follows accepted relevant inputs. Verified urgent security, data-loss or hard-freeze defects override normal order. |
| P1           | M01–M04: practical current-messenger improvements after foundation acceptance.    | F10 and each task's product/interface decisions accepted; independent ready tasks may run together.                                                                                   |
| Roadmap only | Future capabilities and conditional platform replacements.                        | No implementation claim until a concrete scenario, product decision, relevant contract, budget and first-slice acceptance are recorded. Their dependencies do not enlarge P0.         |

Priority is program order, not a claim that every foundation change has identical
risk/value. Within construction, rank findings by measured user impact, correctness
risk and enabling value. Choose retain/qualify, targeted fix, feature or experiment
from evidence. A no-change decision can satisfy a task when its acceptance is met;
otherwise name the unverified scenario and keep it open.

## Delivery policy

1. Define a finite foundation scope around current IM scenarios and real reuse.
   Do not implement speculative forum, browser or SDK architecture in advance.
2. Establish reproducible correctness and performance evidence before selecting
   major optimization, module extraction, database or UI changes.
3. Make boundaries useful: one policy owner, explicit inputs/results/errors,
   lifecycle and cancellation, durable commit authority and bounded resource use.
   A file split alone is not a completed module boundary.
4. Deliver and validate small changes to existing consumers. Preserve identity,
   privacy, wire/storage compatibility, delivery and recovery guarantees.
5. Accept the agreed foundation release before opening feature development.
   Severe verified security, data-loss or hard-freeze defects take precedence
   whenever discovered. Optional future ideas do not extend the foundation gate.
6. Keep performance, verification and decision records active throughout later
   work. Foundation acceptance does not mean these concerns are permanently done.

## Phases and exit criteria

| Phase                                 | Purpose and scope                                                                                                                | Exit evidence                                                                                                                                                           | Parallelism                                                                                                      |
| ------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 0. Bound the foundations              | F01: current concepts, owners, consumers, stores and critical scenarios; identify gaps without assuming defects.                 | Accepted responsibility map, existing/reusable/unknown distinctions, bounded foundation scope and authoritative guide for each work package.                            | Read-only inventories may run independently; one coordinator reconciles shared concepts.                         |
| 1. Establish evidence and contracts   | F02 verification baseline, F03 runtime baseline, F04 authority/lifecycle/interface contracts.                                    | Reproducible scenarios, representative timing/failure evidence, correctness checks and a ranked, scoped foundation change list. Unknowns have an owner and next action. | F02/F03/F04 can proceed together after relevant F01 inputs. Measurement windows stay free from build/test noise. |
| 2. Build and optimize the foundations | F05 module boundaries, F06 events/scheduling, F07 communication/sync, F08 storage/lifecycles; F09 protects each delivered slice. | Current consumers use accepted boundaries; selected costs improve or current behavior is retained with evidence; failure/recovery and compatibility remain qualified.   | Integrate F05 interfaces incrementally, then admit independent F06/F07/F08 slices. F09 accompanies every slice.  |
| 3. Accept the foundation release      | F10: qualify the agreed current-IM scenarios across the affected boundaries.                                                     | Foundation acceptance checklist met; severe risks resolved; remaining bounded gaps explicitly accepted or owned. No implied public release or publication.              | Independent acceptance scenarios may run together if their environments and data do not interfere.               |
| 4. Improve the current messenger      | Approved monitoring UI, practical anti-harassment, manual QR and package-size slices.                                            | Each feature meets its own contract, failure/recovery and resource criteria using the accepted foundations.                                                             | Separate feature lanes after F10, with one owner for any shared interface.                                       |
| Future roadmap                        | Browser review, meetings, PWA, forum/feed, alternative clients/market, external SDK and incentives.                              | Separate product decision, relevant foundation evidence and an independently testable first slice before activation.                                                    | No current assignments. Future independent features may run together after their own gates.                      |

Phase progression is evidence-based, not calendar-based. Existing working
capabilities can satisfy a package through inspection and qualification; every
package is not a mandate to replace its implementation.

## Foundation work packages and dependencies

F identifiers name the foundation program. They do not convert previous task
states. All tasks begin **unclaimed and unstarted** until the execution cycle
begins from the merged planning baseline. A dependency requires an accepted
relevant output, not the completion of an unrelated whole document or subsystem.
For construction packages, select one bounded real-consumer slice per delivery
branch; a broad package is not permission for an all-app rewrite.

| Package                                             | Outcome / scope                                                                                                                                                                          | Required inputs                                                                                               | Acceptance / boundary                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| --------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| F01 — Concepts and responsibility map               | Explain current business concepts, module responsibilities, real callers, stores and extension points. Identify authoritative rules and existing evidence.                               | The thirty source requirements and later authorized implementation inspection.                                | Each foundation package has an owner, real consumers, invariant and inspection gap; no blanket refactor or duplicated inventory.                                                                          |
| F02 — Effective and timely verification             | Map local/CI/native/release checks; measure waiting, setup, compilation, execution, failures and retries; assess actual assertion gaps.                                                  | Relevant F01 ownership and scenarios.                                                                         | A reproducible baseline and check-allocation proposal preserving meaningful failure detection. Evaluate supplied methods explicitly; not every tool becomes a mandatory gate.                             |
| F03 — Runtime baseline and attribution              | Measure startup, idle, active IM and return to idle, including app-related processes, CPU/memory/disk/network and available energy/wakeup evidence. Inventory reusable observations.     | Relevant F01 workload/store/process owners.                                                                   | Comparable build/platform/data/window provenance, resource attribution, ranked findings and measurement limits. No assumption that timers, SQLite or UI technology are the root cause.                    |
| F04 — Authority, lifecycle and interface contracts  | Specify identity/privacy/permissions, personal and group sync, announcement/member distinctions, pending/effective state, retention/deletion/recovery and operation lifetime.            | Relevant F01 ownership and current behavior inspection.                                                       | Resolve rules needed by the selected foundation slices; name remaining decisions. Business-specific authority stays explicit. No preselected Raft, global deletion, anonymity or external SDK.            |
| F05 — Useful module boundaries                      | Clarify/extract the necessary interfaces and migrate actual existing consumers. Separate core policy, host adaptation and presentation; define transport/sync/business responsibilities. | Relevant F01/F04 outputs, an adequate F02 safety check and F03 baseline for affected performance paths.       | One authoritative policy owner, explicit errors/cancellation/commit boundary and tested real consumers. Retain good existing seams. No SDK packaging or cosmetic file-count target.                       |
| F06 — Event and scheduling governance               | Reuse meaningful events and shared scheduling admission; remove evidenced duplicate polling/work; preserve required timeout, retry and recovery.                                         | Relevant F02/F03/F04 outputs and F05 interfaces used by the slice.                                            | Trigger, coalescing, bounded work, progress, cancellation and return-to-idle evidence; no duplicate legacy worker left active. A single universal scheduler is not presumed necessary.                    |
| F07 — Communication and synchronization foundations | Qualify and improve needed connection/transport/sync/delivery boundaries; personal replay, group propagation/recovery, announcements and member authority remain distinct.               | Relevant F02/F03/F04 outputs and F05 interfaces used by the slice.                                            | Agreed duplicate/reorder/partition/restart/revoke/compatibility scenarios with bounded resource behavior. Share transfer mechanisms without erasing business-specific permissions or merge rules.         |
| F08 — Storage and resource lifecycles               | Improve selected incremental I/O, startup/history/search, cache/memory reclamation, retention/capacity and deletion behavior.                                                            | Relevant F02/F03/F04 outputs and F05 interfaces; accepted F07 rules for sync-range/deletion-dependent slices. | Measured targeted costs and repeated recovery/return-to-idle checks. Separate local visibility, durable deletion, account decisions and recall. Marker reclamation requires safe replay/restore evidence. |
| F09 — Regression protection and maintained rules    | Bind each foundation change to reusable correctness/performance scenarios, efficient validation selection, AI reuse guidance and supported decision rationale.                           | F02/F03/F04 plus each selected F05–F08 delivery.                                                              | Tests detect relevant failures, resource observations are attributable, selectors/docs match behavior and recurring verification cost is recorded. Deliver continuously, not as a final testing backlog.  |
| F10 — Foundation acceptance                         | Integrate accepted packages and verify current IM behavior, performance, authority, lifecycle and reuse on the agreed source/platform scope.                                             | Accepted F01–F09 outputs for the agreed scope.                                                                | The checklist below is satisfied. This gate opens feature planning/development; it does not publish a build or complete future features.                                                                  |

### Sequencing within foundation construction

- Start with F01, then prepare F02/F03/F04 in parallel. Do not wait for an
  elaborate monitoring UI to collect performance evidence.
- Select the smallest useful F05 boundary changes. Publish their contract and
  migration order before other packages change the same callers or state owners.
- F06/F07/F08 can overlap once their required interface slices are accepted.
  Communication correctness improvements may proceed independently from history
  pagination; deletion semantics cannot proceed independently from replay rules.
- Pair each module/interface change with qualification of its existing consumer;
  optimize measured costs in the same or a following bounded slice. Do not defer
  every performance improvement until after an app-wide refactor.
| Performance                    | Establish representative baselines, address the agreed high-impact findings and protect against recurrence.                                            | Unlimited micro-optimization, new UI implementation or an unmeasured rewrite.                                               |
| Monitoring                     | Obtain enough attributable observations to explain and verify the selected costs, including disabled-mode overhead.                                    | Polished panel/menu-bar views, persistent chart history and user alerts.                                                    |
| Sync and transport             | Qualify current personal/group exchange, authorized recovery, progress/resource bounds and compatibility in the agreed scenarios.                      | New transport families, global consensus, forum replication or browser gateways without a current-IM need.                  |
| Announcements and membership   | Keep their authority/state semantics separate; define the transitions required by the selected current-IM scope, including pending/effective meanings. | A new announcement editor/history/confirmation UX solely to complete an architecture program.                               |
| Retention and capacity         | Explain existing data categories, authority, limits, cleanup/recovery and their measured growth.                                                       | New quota-management screens, notification UX or automatic cleanup policies not yet agreed.                                 |
| Deletion                       | Qualify the agreed local/account/recall meanings against relevant replay/restart/restore cases; preserve required deletion authority.                  | Marker compaction without measured need and a safe reclamation argument.                                                    |
| Privacy and unwanted contact   | Establish identity, disclosure/admission and revocation boundaries; fix severe verified enforcement defects.                                           | New stranger-request UX, broad product policy modes or endorsement counts. Practical controls remain prioritized after F10. |
| Verification and documentation | Maintain risk-based checks, resource regressions, source-bound evidence and discoverable rules/decisions.                                              | Every named atlas tool on every PR, an exhaustive competitor survey or a second documentation system.                       |

If investigation reveals that a deferred interface is required to make an
existing invariant usable or enforceable, promote only that necessary slice with
its rationale and acceptance. Conversely, a desirable new feature does not become
mandatory merely because it could reuse a foundation module.

## Foundation acceptance checklist

The foundation program is complete when the agreed outputs below are accepted,
not when every hypothetical architecture improvement has been attempted.

- **Ownership and reuse:** current consumers use the accepted interfaces; no
  competing policy owner or abandoned duplicate implementation remains.
- **Resource behavior:** comparable startup/idle/active/return-to-idle results
  meet the agreed budgets or an explicitly reviewed exception. Work queues,
  caches and retained metadata have limits and reclamation/recovery rules.
- **Sync and durability:** agreed current-IM cases cover interruption, reconnect,
  duplicate/reordered data, membership/revocation, deletion, restart and restore;
  outstanding topology/platform limitations are named.
- **Privacy and authority:** account/device meanings, accepted operations and
  observer/peer/relay exposure are explicit and enforced at the owning boundary.
- **Verification:** checks have meaningful assertions and local/CI/native roles;
  feedback latency and failure causes are observable. Missing evidence is not a pass.
- **Maintainability:** current behavior and important decisions are documented at
  their owners; future features can locate the contract and its regression checks.
- **Residual risk:** severe security/data-loss/recovery defects are resolved.
  Other gaps have an impact, owner and explicit disposition. Optional extensions
  cannot indefinitely delay foundation acceptance.

Numeric targets, representative data sizes, platforms and the mandatory scenario
set must be agreed from F01–F04 evidence before construction scope is accepted.
The existing [performance requirements](performance-requirements.md) and
[testing workflow](testing-feedback-loop.md) remain their authoritative owners;
this draft introduces no competing budget or gate policy.

## Current-IM work after foundation acceptance

M tasks remain unclaimed until F10 and their own decisions are accepted.
Their order below is the default priority within P1; independent ready work may
run together without consuming a constrained higher-priority owner. Package-size
attribution can be researched earlier without changing artifacts; optimization
still needs affected runtime/install/update evidence.

| Lane                                            | Sources          | Foundation inputs and remaining product choices                                                                                                                                    | Conflict boundary                                                                                                          |
| ----------------------------------------------- | ---------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| M01 — Practical anti-harassment                 | REQ-025          | F04 identity/permissions and F07 enforcement. Decide account/device blocking, stranger policy, group effects and linked-device behavior.                                           | Core enforcement and UI presentation have distinct owners; endorsements are not an input dependency.                       |
| M02 — Monitoring panel and native compact entry | REQ-001, REQ-016 | Reusable F03 metrics, F06 lifecycle, F09 overhead checks. Decide units/freshness, acquisition defaults, history and panel/tray relationship. Extra collection must be disableable. | One metric pipeline; no separate collector for each view or whole-machine-monitoring expansion.                            |
| M03 — Manual image QR                           | REQ-010          | F05 image/contact interfaces, bounded F06 work and F04 sensitive-content rules. Decide supported cards and multiple/invalid-code behavior.                                         | Explicit image-menu/preview trigger; display results before chosen action; no background scanning or automatic navigation. |
| M04 — Package-size optimization                 | REQ-014          | F01 dependency/resource inventory and F02/F09 packaging checks. Compare same OS/architecture/format and record installed size separately.                                          | Coordinate shared dependency/build owners; no forced 10M target or assumed UI migration.                                   |

## Future roadmap and activation conditions

Keep these directions visible without assigning dates, workers or immediate
implementation. F10 is the common program gate. Each direction also needs the
specific decisions below; completing foundations alone does not settle them.

| Direction                           | Sources          | Additional activation conditions and first-slice boundary                                                                                                                                                                            |
| ----------------------------------- | ---------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Browser sharing/review              | REQ-002          | Select formats, link/link+code access, separate permissions, comments/revisions and host availability. Start with no-install viewing/comments; simultaneous editing remains later.                                                   |
| Group voice meetings                | REQ-023          | Agree participant scale, voluntary join, member admission, initiator exit and media/native resource evidence. Video and independent rooms are later separate decisions.                                                              |
| Mobile PWA                          | REQ-027          | Define real mobile scenarios, supported browser limits, authorized-node pairing/key ownership, reachable transport and offline behavior; assess suitable existing work when activated. No assumed JS rewrite or direct browser mDNS. |
| Decentralized forum and forwarding  | REQ-019, REQ-024 | Resolve product form, audience/propagation consent, post/comment provenance, three-day disappearance/manual pinning, local versus retained copies and selection costs. Hot/latest/own counts remain proposals.                       |
| Private feed and profile visibility | REQ-026          | Selected-contact audience per post and independent profile visibility; define later audience changes, interactions and retained/offline copies. Do not inherit forum TTL.                                                            |
| Alternative interaction clients     | REQ-021          | Define a supported core/client contract and real alternative consumer, lifecycle and compatibility; service versus embedded form remains open.                                                                                       |
| Client catalog/marketplace          | REQ-021          | First qualify the client contract and an actual alternative adapter; then choose listing versus installation, publisher trust, compatibility, update and revocation.                                                                 |
| External Rust SDK                   | REQ-020          | A real external Rust consumer, minimal supported surface, storage/runtime/key ownership and compatibility obligations. Internal modularity does not itself require public packaging; bindings remain later.                          |

Future branches may proceed independently when their own inputs are accepted.

import assert from "node:assert/strict";
import {
  copyFileSync,
  chmodSync,
  mkdirSync,
  mkdtempSync,
  readFileSync,
  rmSync,
  writeFileSync,
} from "node:fs";
import { tmpdir } from "node:os";
import { join, resolve } from "node:path";
import { spawnSync } from "node:child_process";
import test from "node:test";

function fixture(t) {
  const root = mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), "mesh standards wiring "));
  t.after(() => rmSync(root, { recursive: true, force: true }));
  mkdirSync(join(root, "scripts/validation"), { recursive: true });
  writeFileSync(
    join(root, "scripts/validation/standards.mjs"),
    "console.error('fixture standards gap');process.exit(23);\n",
  );
  return root;
}

test(
  "pre-commit stops on structural gaps before formatting or success",
  { skip: process.platform === "win32" },
  (t) => {
    const root = fixture(t);
    spawnSync("git", ["init", "-q"], { cwd: root });
    writeFileSync(join(root, "scripts/check-repository-hygiene.mjs"), "");
    copyFileSync(resolve("hooks/pre-commit"), join(root, "hook"));
    const run = spawnSync("bash", ["hook"], { cwd: root, encoding: "utf8" });
    assert.equal(run.status, 23, run.stderr || run.stdout);
    assert.match(run.stderr, /fixture standards gap/);
    assert.doesNotMatch(run.stdout, /Source checks passed/);
  },
);

test("health rejects standards gaps before acquiring managed build resources", (t) => {
  const root = fixture(t);
  for (const dir of ["frontend/node_modules", "src-tauri"])
    mkdirSync(join(root, dir), { recursive: true });
  writeFileSync(join(root, "frontend/node_modules/.package-lock.json"), "{}");
  writeFileSync(join(root, "Makefile"), "");
  copyFileSync(resolve("scripts/check-health.sh"), join(root, "health.sh"));
  const run = spawnSync("bash", ["health.sh", "--fast"], {
    cwd: root,
    encoding: "utf8",
    env: { ...process.env, MESH_VALIDATION_HEALTH_GUARDED: "0" },
  });
  assert.equal(run.status, 23, run.stderr || run.stdout);
  assert.match(run.stderr, /fixture standards gap/);
});

test(
  "make standards-check propagates checker failure",
  { skip: process.platform === "win32" },
  (t) => {
    const root = fixture(t);
    copyFileSync(resolve("Makefile"), join(root, "Makefile"));
    const run = spawnSync("make", ["standards-check"], {
      cwd: root,
      encoding: "utf8",

name: Dependency Review

# Blocks a PR that introduces a dependency with a known vulnerability (or a disallowed
# license) before it ever lands on main. Complements cargo-deny / cargo-audit (which guard
# the whole tree on every push) by reviewing exactly what a PR changes.
on:
  merge_group:
    types: [checks_requested]
  pull_request:

permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.event_name }}-${{ github.event.pull_request.number || github.ref }}-${{ github.event_name == 'push' && github.run_id || 'candidate' }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' || github.event_name == 'merge_group' }}

jobs:
  review:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - name: Dependency review
        uses: actions/dependency-review-action@v5
        with:
          # Merge groups have no pull_request payload: scan the actual queued delta.
          base-ref: ${{ github.event.merge_group.base_sha || github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}
          head-ref: ${{ github.event.merge_group.head_sha || github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
          fail-on-severity: high
          # MIT-licensed project; flag copyleft/unknown licenses pulled in by a PR.
          deny-licenses: GPL-2.0, GPL-3.0, AGPL-3.0
          comment-summary-in-pr: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' && 'on-failure' || 'never' }}

from pathlib import Path
p=Path('docs/development-roadmap.md');s=p.read_text().replace('this draft introduces no competing budget or gate policy.','this roadmap introduces no competing budget or gate policy.')
marker='## Task claims, branches and integration\n'
section='''## Evidence-dependent decisions and their owners

These are scheduled outputs, not reasons to reopen global ordering or assume a
technology choice. Resolve facts through investigation first; involve the product
owner for actual user-policy trade-offs. An unresolved decision blocks only its
affected child slices and must name an owner and next action.

| Decision | Resolving task / owner | Closure evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| First bottleneck and construction slice | F02/F03/F04 → F05; integration owner with validation/runtime/core owners | Comparable cost or verified correctness risk, invariant, bounded change and failure/recovery acceptance. |
| Runtime budgets and supported evidence scope | F03; performance owner with product/integration owner for exceptions | Existing authoritative budgets, build/process/data/platform identity, reliable observations and named misses; no competing invented target table. |
| Sync, announcement/member, deletion and privacy rules | F04; relevant core/storage/privacy owner and product owner for user semantics | Current behavior and authority/recovery trace, accepted per-domain rule, compatibility and selected failure cases. No Raft choice by default. |
| Retain, tune or replace storage/interfaces/UI | F01/F03/F05/F08; owning module and integration owner | Demonstrated current-IM need and measured benefit versus migration/rollback/cost. New production UI remains roadmap-only. |
| Verification methods and local/CI/native allocation | F02/F09; validation owner | Risk/assertion coverage, actual failure/attempt evidence and recurring cost. Existing protected checks are not weakened by this plan. |
| Monitoring, contact and QR product choices | M02/M01/M03; relevant feature/core owner and product owner | Supported metric/default/retention behavior, account/device/contact policy or supported card/actions, with accepted scope and bounded cost before implementation. |
| Future capability activation | Relevant future direction; product/integration and authority owner | Concrete user/consumer scenario, accepted contracts and resources, first-slice acceptance and an explicit activation record. |

### Preserved research leads and verification landscape

The intake's references are leads, not verified claims, adopted technologies or
required dependencies. Verify primary sources when their owning task activates.
Do not install tools or expand scope merely to reproduce a supplied example.

- REQ-001: [monitoring visual reference](https://x.com/HiTw93/status/2116890236320092498?a=xiwtWvIa7enA_OlbL1Q&s=20).
  The supplied image suggests a compact native entry/detail view; whole-computer
  fan/battery controls are outside the app/process-family scope. The earlier post
  retrieval was unsuccessful; the visual does not establish metric availability.
- REQ-012: [GPUI](https://gpui.rs/), [GPUI Kit](https://gpui-kit.com/),
  [Kit source](https://github.com/longbridge/gpui-kit),
  [Slint](https://github.com/slint-ui/slint), [Iced](https://github.com/iced-rs/iced)
  and [Rune](https://github.com/anomalyco/rune). Their suitability is unverified.
  Compare desktop macOS/Windows/Linux parity; Web is optional for this comparison
  and does not cancel the separate mobile PWA direction.
- REQ-029: [Columba](https://github.com/torlando-tech/columba),
  [Bitchat](https://github.com/permissionlesstech/bitchat),
  [LAN Messenger source](https://github.com/lanmessenger/lanmessenger) and
  [site](https://lanmessenger.github.io/), [LANChat](https://github.com/cap153/LANChat),
  [Mesh-Talk source](https://github.com/OctopusGarage/mesh-talk) and
  [site](https://octopusgarage.github.io/mesh-talk/),
  [Squiggle](https://github.com/hasankhan/Squiggle),
  [BeeBEEP](https://www.beebeep.net/) and [BLIP](https://github.com/krwg/blip).
  Technitium Mesh/HostTalk exact sources remain unknown. Quoted rankings,
  platform/security claims, Bluetooth/LoRa and Reticulum ideas are not adopted.
- Other named leads: baoyu-design/deepseek harness browser sharing, Google Drive
  external copies, Raft comparison and existing `feature/mobile-pwa` work.
  Existing-work inspection must check source/PR/owner before duplication; a named
  service or branch does not prove support or authorize exposing a local service.

For REQ-030, F02/F09 must explicitly classify applicability, existing evidence,
gaps/defer reasons and owners across static/type/semantic/SAST/formal methods;
unit/integration/E2E/contract checks; property/fuzz/mutation methods; runtime/DAST;
load/stress/spike/soak/capacity; memory/leak/undefined-behavior/race checks;
statement/branch/condition/function/path/MC/DC coverage; maintainability/review;
CVE/secrets/dependency/supply chain; licenses/relevant compliance; fault injection,
degradation/recovery/chaos; and actual agent tool/format/authorization/multi-turn/
factuality surfaces. RAG/ML evaluations apply only if that surface actually exists.
Separate method, scope, purpose and quality; tool counts or coverage percentages
alone do not demonstrate meaningful fault detection. Named tools remain examples,
not a requirement to run every tool on every PR.

'''
assert marker in s;s=s.replace(marker,section+marker,1);p.write_text(s)

# Pre-push hook: push session logs alongside user's push

        fi
    elif [ -x "$_entire_hook_dir/pre-push.pre-entire" ]; then
        "$_entire_hook_dir/pre-push.pre-entire" "$@"
    fi
fi

---
name: babysit-pr
description: Monitor a pull request through review and CI. Use when the user asks to monitor, watch, or babysit a PR.
---

# Babysit PR

Many repos have AI review bots. They're helpful, even if they are not always
right.

## Waiting

Never write your own watcher, polling loop, or `sleep` loop. Use one watcher
per PR: `watch_pull_request` in T3 Code, `pr-wait` everywhere else. Never run
both on the same PR. Every watcher on a GitHub account shares one rate limit.

### In T3 Code: `watch_pull_request`

Handle the existing checks and comments first. Then call
`watch_pull_request` and end your turn. T3 Code wakes you with a message when
a check fails, the required checks pass, someone comments or reviews, or the
branch conflicts.

- **Only the thread that owns the PR watches it.** If you are a delegated
  child task (a reviewer, a Sol round, any `delegate_task` child), never call
  `watch_pull_request`. The parent owns the PR. Do not watch PRs you are not
  working on.
- **A wake is news, not a merge decision.** Check the merge gate yourself.
- **Unwatch when you hand off.** A watched thread stays in Working and out of
  the user's inbox. When you stop (ready, blocked, or asking the user a question),
  call `unwatch_pull_request` first. A merge or close ends the watch on its
  own.
- **"Stopped watching, could not read it"** usually means GitHub's rate limit
  is used up. Run `gh api rate_limit --jq .resources.graphql` before you
  watch again. If `remaining` is near 0, wait for `reset` with one background
  command, then watch again. Never watch again in a tight loop.

### Everywhere else: `pr-wait`

Wait with `scripts/pr-wait` from this skill's directory (use its absolute
path).

```bash
pr-wait <pr> [--repo owner/name] [--until ready|green|any-change]
```

It prints one line per real event. It exits 0 when the `--until` condition is
met or the PR merges, 1 when it needs you (a required check failed, conflicts,
unresolved threads, PR closed), and 2 on bad input.

- `ready` (default): required checks green, Greptile or Macroscope reviewed the
  head, and no unresolved threads. Use this to babysit.
- `green`: required checks only. Use it when the repo has no Greptile or
  Macroscope.
- `any-change`: exit on the first event.

In Claude Code, run it with the Monitor tool (`timeout_ms: 3600000`), so each
line wakes you. Without a monitor, run it as one long command. It ends on its
own.

Start it again after you push, after you handle an exit 1, and after a resume.
It remembers what it already reported, so nothing that arrived in between is
lost. If it says another pid already watches the PR, do not start a second one.
Kill the old one only if its events do not reach you.

With either watcher: when an event needs no action, end your turn without a
message. Never post or say "still waiting".

## GitHub rate limits

`gh pr create`, `gh pr view`, and `gh pr checks` use GraphQL. When GraphQL is
used up, the REST limit is separate and usually still has room. Use
`gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/pulls/<n>` to read a PR, and
`gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/commits/<sha>/check-runs` for checks.

## Reviews

Only act on checks and comments newer than the latest push. Verify every bot
finding against the source before changing code. Fix real findings and CI
failures, distinguish repository failures from infrastructure flakes, and reply
with a written reason when dismissing false positives.

If the repo has `.macroscope/check-run-agents/*.md`, read those rules before you
reply to a Macroscope finding. Its findings cite them.

CodeRabbit is advisory. Treat its findings like any other finding, but never
wait for it and never hold a merge for it.

If a review bot leaves feedback you believe is not worth addressing, reply with
a written reason and resolve the comment. Use the `leaving-pr-comments` skill
for every comment posted on the user's behalf.

Screenshots and videos help as well, when you have a way to upload them.

Keep the PR at the size the user's goal needs. Review loops tend to grow a
PR one cheap-looking fix at a time. Fix real bugs in the intended case.
Decline the rest with a written reason, and list them as follow-ups:
unneeded tests, guards for edge cases that do not matter, extra integration
or compatibility, and small performance costs. Prefer the fix that deletes or
narrows code.

## Base branch and merging

Keep an eye on changes to `main` and rebase when needed. `pr-wait` reports when
new base commits touch this PR's files, and when the PR becomes BEHIND or DIRTY.
`watch_pull_request` reports conflicts only, so check for BEHIND yourself
before you call the PR ready.
If an overlapping PR makes this one obsolete, stop monitoring, report it to the
user, and ask before closing the PR unless closure was explicitly authorized.

If nothing has changed, stay quiet rather than posting filler comments. Stop
when `pr-wait` exits 0, or in T3 Code when the merge gate passes on the latest
head. Merge only when the user explicitly requested it;
otherwise report that the PR is ready. Right before a merge, run `git fetch` and
check the PR again. Never merge when it is BEHIND or DIRTY, or when base commits
that landed after the last green run touch this PR's files. Rebase, push, and
wait for green again.

description: Monitor a pull request through review and CI. Use when the user asks to monitor, watch, or babysit a PR.

# Babysit PR

Many repos have AI review bots. They're helpful, even if they are not always
right.

## Waiting

Never write your own watcher, polling loop, or `sleep` loop. Use one watcher
per PR: `watch_pull_request` in T3 Code, `pr-wait` everywhere else. Never run
both on the same PR. Every watcher on a GitHub account shares one rate limit.

### In T3 Code: `watch_pull_request`

Handle the existing checks and comments first. Then call
`watch_pull_request` and end your turn. T3 Code wakes you with a message when
a check fails, the required checks pass, someone comments or reviews, or the
branch conflicts.

- **Only the thread that owns the PR watches it.** If you are a delegated
  child task (a reviewer, a Sol round, any `delegate_task` child), never call
  `watch_pull_request`. The parent owns the PR. Do not watch PRs you are not
  working on.
- **A wake is news, not a merge decision.** Check the merge gate yourself.
- **Unwatch when you hand off.** A watched thread stays in Working and out of
  the user's inbox. When you stop (ready, blocked, or asking the user a question),
  call `unwatch_pull_request` first. A merge or close ends the watch on its
  own.
- **"Stopped watching, could not read it"** usually means GitHub's rate limit
  is used up. Run `gh api rate_limit --jq .resources.graphql` before you
  watch again. If `remaining` is near 0, wait for `reset` with one background
  command, then watch again. Never watch again in a tight loop.

### Everywhere else: `pr-wait`

Wait with `scripts/pr-wait` from this skill's directory (use its absolute
path).

```bash
pr-wait <pr> [--repo owner/name] [--until ready|green|any-change]
```

It prints one line per real event. It exits 0 when the `--until` condition is
met or the PR merges, 1 when it needs you (a required check failed, conflicts,
unresolved threads, PR closed), and 2 on bad input.

- `ready` (default): required checks green, Greptile or Macroscope reviewed the
  head, and no unresolved threads. Use this to babysit.
- `green`: required checks only. Use it when the repo has no Greptile or
  Macroscope.
- `any-change`: exit on the first event.

In Claude Code, run it with the Monitor tool (`timeout_ms: 3600000`), so each
line wakes you. Without a monitor, run it as one long command. It ends on its
own.

Start it again after you push, after you handle an exit 1, and after a resume.
It remembers what it already reported, so nothing that arrived in between is
lost. If it says another pid already watches the PR, do not start a second one.
Kill the old one only if its events do not reach you.

With either watcher: when an event needs no action, end your turn without a
message. Never post or say "still waiting".

## GitHub rate limits

`gh pr create`, `gh pr view`, and `gh pr checks` use GraphQL. When GraphQL is
used up, the REST limit is separate and usually still has room. Use
`gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/pulls/<n>` to read a PR, and
`gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/commits/<sha>/check-runs` for checks.

## Reviews

Only act on checks and comments newer than the latest push. Verify every bot
finding against the source before changing code. Fix real findings and CI
failures, distinguish repository failures from infrastructure flakes, and reply
with a written reason when dismissing false positives.

If the repo has `.macroscope/check-run-agents/*.md`, read those rules before you
reply to a Macroscope finding. Its findings cite them.

CodeRabbit is advisory. Treat its findings like any other finding, but never
wait for it and never hold a merge for it.

If a review bot leaves feedback you believe is not worth addressing, reply with
a written reason and resolve the comment. Use the `leaving-pr-comments` skill
for every comment posted on the user's behalf.

Screenshots and videos help as well, when you have a way to upload them.

Keep the PR at the size the user's goal needs. Review loops tend to grow a
PR one cheap-looking fix at a time. Fix real bugs in the intended case.
Decline the rest with a written reason, and list them as follow-ups:
unneeded tests, guards for edge cases that do not matter, extra integration
or compatibility, and small performance costs. Prefer the fix that deletes or
narrows code.

## Base branch and merging

Keep an eye on changes to `main` and rebase when needed. `pr-wait` reports when
new base commits touch this PR's files, and when the PR becomes BEHIND or DIRTY.
`watch_pull_request` reports conflicts only, so check for BEHIND yourself
before you call the PR ready.
If an overlapping PR makes this one obsolete, stop monitoring, report it to the
user, and ask before closing the PR unless closure was explicitly authorized.

If nothing has changed, stay quiet rather than posting filler comments. Stop
when `pr-wait` exits 0, or in T3 Code when the merge gate passes on the latest
head. Merge only when the user explicitly requested it;
otherwise report that the PR is ready. Right before a merge, run `git fetch` and
check the PR again. Never merge when it is BEHIND or DIRTY, or when base commits
that landed after the last green run touch this PR's files. Rebase, push, and
wait for green again.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""pr-wait: watch one GitHub pull request and print one line per real event.

  pr-wait <pr> [--repo owner/name] [--until green|ready|any-change] [--interval 20]

<pr> is a PR number or PR URL. Without --repo, the repo comes from the URL or
from the current checkout. Stdout carries only events, one line each, so a
monitor (Claude Code's Monitor tool) wakes the agent once per real event.
Progress and errors that do not end the run go to stderr.

--until
  green       required checks passed on the current head (every CI check when
              the base branch requires none)
  ready      green, Greptile or Macroscope reviewed the current head, and no
              review thread is unresolved (default)
  any-change  stop after the first poll that prints an event

Exit codes
  0  the --until condition is met, or the PR merged
  1  the condition cannot be met without action: a required check failed, the
     branch conflicts with its base, the PR closed, `ready` is blocked by
     unresolved threads or a BEHIND branch, or GitHub stayed unreachable
  2  bad arguments, unknown PR, or another pr-wait already watches this PR

Events
  - a required check failed (name and link)
  - all checks finished on the head (one summary line)
  - a new comment, review, thread, or thread reply from someone other than the
    PR author or the gh user
  - Greptile, Macroscope, or CodeRabbit finished on the head, or a Greptile or
    Macroscope summary changed after that
  - the base branch moved and the new commits touch files in this PR
  - merge state became BEHIND or DIRTY
  - the PR merged or closed

CodeRabbit is advisory: pr-wait reports it but never waits for it. Comment
edits are never events, and top-level comments from CI and deploy bots
(github-actions, Vercel) are skipped, because checks already carry that news.

State lives in ~/.local/state/pr-wait/. A lock makes a second watcher for the
same PR exit at once. A state file lets a restarted watcher report what arrived
while no watcher ran. The first run for a PR records what already exists and
reports only what comes after.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import fcntl
import hashlib
import html
import json
import os
import re
import subprocess
import sys
import time
from collections.abc import Sequence
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any, NoReturn

GATING_BOTS = ("greptile", "macroscope")
ADVISORY_BOTS = ("coderabbit",)
# CI and deploy bots report through checks. Their PR comments are status reports.
STATUS_BOTS = ("github-actions", "vercel", "netlify", "railway", "cloudflare")
STATE_DIR = Path.home() / ".local" / "state" / "pr-wait"
# A state file older than this describes an old session. Start a fresh baseline
# instead of replaying hours of comments as new events.
STALE_STATE_SECONDS = 6 * 3600
MAX_FAILED_POLLS = 10
TRANSIENT = re.compile(
    r"HTTP (5\d\d|429)|rate limit|timed? ?out|connection (reset|refused)|EOF|"
    r"temporar|could not resolve host|TLS handshake|Something went wrong",
    re.IGNORECASE,
)
FAILED = ("fail", "cancel")
# gh pr checks buckets, worst first. Duplicate names (push and pull_request runs
# of one job) collapse to the worst bucket.
RANK = {"fail": 4, "cancel": 3, "pending": 2, "pass": 1, "skipping": 0}

可以。下面是当前提交到 [PR #387](https://github.com/OctopusGarage/mesh-talk/pull/387) 的完整规划摘要。**这是后续工作的执行计划，不代表这些任务已经完成。** PR 的 CI 继续运行；如你提出调整，我会修改同一 PR 并重新验证。

**整体顺序**

| 阶段 | 主要工作 | 完成后才能进入什么 |
|---|---|---|
| 规划交付 | 定稿路线图、同步 `AGENTS.md`、评审与检查、合入 main | 从合入后的 main 开始任务 |
| 第一阶段：摸清基础 | 梳理概念、模块、调用者、存储与业务规则 | 开展有明确对象的测量和契约整理 |
| 第二阶段：建立依据 | 验证效率、性能基线、权限与生命周期契约 | 决定具体改什么、如何验收 |
| 第三阶段：基础建设 | 按证据整理模块，优化事件调度、通信同步、存储与资源生命周期 | 集成验收基础能力 |
| 第四阶段：基础验收 | 在同一版本上验证当前 IM 的关键场景 | 开放后续功能开发 |
| 第五阶段：完善当前 IM | 防骚扰、监控面板、手动二维码、包体积 | 各自独立交付 |
| 远期 roadmap | 论坛、PWA、动态、会议、市场、外部 SDK 等 | 满足各自启动条件后再排期 |

这里的关键是：**基础建设有明确终点；模块拆分和性能优化交错推进，不先做一次全局大重构。**

**P0：10 个基础工作包**

| 编号 | 工作包 | 要交付什么 | 主要依赖 |
|---|---|---|---|
| F01 | 概念与责任地图 | 当前业务概念、模块职责、真实调用者、存储类别、已有证据与缺口 | 规划合入 main |
| F02 | 验证有效性与反馈效率 | 本地/CI/原生检查分工；等待、编译、执行、失败重跑的基线；高价值断言缺口 | F01 的相关场景和负责人 |
| F03 | 性能基线与消耗归因 | 启动、空闲、活跃、回到空闲的可重复测量；进程范围、资源来源和主要问题排序 | F01 的运行、存储和场景地图 |
| F04 | 权限、生命周期与接口契约 | 身份、隐私、个人/群同步、公告/成员权限、删除恢复、取消与提交权的规则 | F01 与实际行为调查 |
| F05 | 有用的模块边界 | 必要接口、明确责任、现有调用者迁移；错误、取消、持久化和资源边界 | 相关 F04 契约及 F02/F03 证据 |
| F06 | 事件与调度治理 | 复用有效事件、减少重复轮询、管理必要重试和定时工作、退出后停止任务 | 相关契约、测量和 F05 接口 |
| F07 | 通信与同步基础 | 整理连接、传输、同步、投递职责；验证多设备与群同步、恢复和权限 | 相关契约、测量和 F05 接口 |
| F08 | 存储与资源生命周期 | 增量 I/O、启动与历史加载、搜索、缓存/内存回收、保留、删除与标记增长 | 相关接口；涉及删除与同步范围时依赖 F07 的规则 |
| F09 | 回归保护与维护规则 | 给每个改动配正确性和性能回归、验证选择、维护文档与 AI 复用要求 | 随每个基础改动交付 |
| F10 | 基础集成验收 | 对整个约定范围做当前版本验收，处理跨模块问题和剩余风险 | 约定范围内的 F01—F09 |

F01 首先执行。它是调查和文档任务，**不会一上来就改产品代码**。

F02、F03、F04 拿到相关输入后可以并行。F05 只整理当前改动需要的边界；随后 F06、F07、F08 中依赖已稳定的部分可以并行。F09 从每个改动开始就跟进，不留到最后补测试。

**具体执行分四批**

1. **A 批：明确对象。** 完成 F01，知道哪些已实现、哪些部分实现、哪些未知，以及后续到哪里调查。
2. **B 批：取得依据。** 并行推进 F02/F03/F04，形成首批改造清单。每项必须说明影响、成本或风险、负责人、范围、验收和停止条件。
3. **C 批：小步改造。** 先接通必要模块接口，再完成对应优化，迁移真实调用者，并验证失败恢复。
4. **D 批：集成验收。** 在合并后的同一候选版本上完成 F10，再进入新功能阶段。

不提前指定“先换数据库”“先重写定时器”或“先替换 UI”。具体首项优化由调查结果决定。

**基础阶段必须做好什么，哪些留到后面**

| 基础必须完成 | 后续独立交付或条件性工作 |
|---|---|
| 解释资源消耗，治理约定的高影响问题，建立回归保护 | 完整监控面板、菜单栏图表、长期趋势和用户告警 |
| 现有 IM 的模块责任、接口、调用者迁移与生命周期 | 为假想业务建设通用框架、对外 SDK |
| 同步与成员权限、投递恢复、兼容和资源边界 | 新传输方式、论坛复制协议、浏览器网关 |
| 公告与成员权限分别建模，明确待处理与生效状态 | 新公告编辑、历史和确认界面 |
| 明确保留、删除、恢复和增长规则 | 新容量管理界面、提醒和未确认的自动清理政策 |
| 身份、接收权限、撤销与严重安全缺陷处理 | 新陌生人申请界面、信誉背书体系 |

已有实现如果满足要求，可以通过验证后保留，**每个工作包不等于必须重写一个模块**。

**基础验收覆盖 8 类场景**

- 有历史数据时启动、解锁，区分首次和再次启动。
- 窗口可见与隐藏时的稳定空闲。
- 单聊与群聊收发，区分本地接受、代管、送达和已读。
- 多设备与群历史追赶，包含重复、乱序、中断和权限变化。
- 历史、搜索和反复切换会话。

# Systematic Debugging

## Overview

Random fixes waste time and create new bugs. Quick patches mask underlying issues.

**Core principle:** ALWAYS find root cause before attempting fixes. Symptom fixes are failure.

**Violating the letter of this process is violating the spirit of debugging.**

## The Iron Law

```
NO FIXES WITHOUT ROOT CAUSE INVESTIGATION FIRST
```

fixtures do not establish that the full cohort fits its per-case, suite and job
budgets. Preserve executed and unrun counts when fail-fast or a watchdog truncates
that evidence.

Budget a mutation chunk for the baseline obligation, every selected mutant's
build and complete consumer suite, setup and report publication. Do not assume
mutants fail early or reuse an old selected-count constant as the inventory grows.
The planner must preserve the rotating sample's exact union while bounding each
worker's work; a shorter chunk changes scheduling, not assurance coverage.
A shared baseline may remove repeated execution only when workers validate the
same run, source, tools, configuration, complete inventory and trusted producer
attempt through the existing evidence owner. Preserve raw tool reports: an
external baseline is separate verified evidence, never an invented tool outcome.
Failed-only reruns may reuse the attested successful producer attempt from the
same run; missing or mismatched evidence must fail before mutant execution.
Keep compilation, individual-test, complete-suite and job limits distinct and
reserve time for process retirement and evidence publication. Invoked tools may
create independent process groups; retain the real tool's cancellation and build
retirement controls, not only successful-run evidence. A closed supervisor pipe
cannot replace the actual work owner's acknowledgment. See
[actual work ownership](ai-coding-reliability.md#r03-actual-work-owns-its-lifetime).

native/backend and release/security evidence stay mandatory. A missing automatic
consumer alone does not make an artifact optional: authoritative human reports
and manual diagnostic deliverables can still require it. Do not retry tests to
repair transport, or suppress the original failed attempt.

An artifact used as acceptance evidence has a stronger contract. Its consumer
must validate the actual tested head or merge source, workflow/run/attempt, platform and architecture,
relevant toolchain/features, expected inventory and content digests required by
the owning protocol. A matching filename, a successful download or a cache hit
is insufficient. Digests detect content changes; provenance establishes whether
those bytes belong to the intended candidate. Reject missing, stale, duplicate,
partial or incompatible inputs before merging evidence.

Keep these checks in the existing producer/consumer owner. Do not add a second
receipt format or evidence resolver. Exercise rejected-input cases when changing
that boundary, and preserve the documented rerun procedure for attempt-bound
artifacts. GitHub's download action reports a digest mismatch as a warning;
the evidence consumer must explicitly reject it. See [artifact validation](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/tutorials/store-and-share-data#validating-artifacts)

        if: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.full == 'true' && (runner.os == 'Linux') }}
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -e -o pipefail
          ulimit -c 262144
          node scripts/ci/linux-crash-diagnostics.mjs setup
          node scripts/ci/linux-crash-diagnostics.mjs selftest

      # Tauri reads frontendDist, so build the frontend before any Cargo step.
      - name: Build frontend
        if: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.full == 'true' }}
        working-directory: frontend
        run: npm run build

      - name: Check built JavaScript for macOS 12 WKWebView
        if: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.full == 'true' }}
        working-directory: frontend
        run: npm run check:build-syntax

      # Keep native lint, production builds and complete tests on every OS.
      - name: Clippy
        if: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.full == 'true' }}
        working-directory: src-tauri
        run: cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings

      - name: Build workspace
        if: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.full == 'true' }}
        working-directory: src-tauri
        run: cargo build --workspace --locked

      - name: Workspace doctests (Linux)
        if: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.full == 'true' }}
        run: cargo test --workspace --doc --locked

      - name: Produce sealed Linux workspace archive
        id: archive
        if: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.full == 'true' }}
        run: bash scripts/ci/linux-workspace.sh produce "$RUNNER_TEMP/linux-workspace-archive" --github-output
      - name: Preserve Linux binary archive
        if: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.full == 'true' }}
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        with:
          name: linux-workspace-binaries-${{ github.sha }}-${{ github.run_id }}-${{ github.run_attempt }}
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/linux-workspace-archive/workspace.tar.zst
          compression-level: 0
          retention-days: 1
          if-no-files-found: error
      - name: Preserve Linux archive metadata
        if: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.full == 'true' }}
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        with:
          name: linux-workspace-metadata-${{ github.sha }}-${{ github.run_id }}-${{ github.run_attempt }}
          path: |
            ${{ runner.temp }}/linux-workspace-archive/manifest.json
            ${{ runner.temp }}/linux-workspace-archive/inventory-*.json
            ${{ runner.temp }}/linux-workspace-archive/feature-resolution.json
          retention-days: 14
          if-no-files-found: error

      - name: Collect Linux native crash evidence and retire its storage
        if: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.full == 'true' && (always() && runner.os == 'Linux') }}
        run: node scripts/ci/linux-crash-diagnostics.mjs collect

      - name: Preserve Linux native crash diagnostics
        if: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.full == 'true' && (always() && runner.os == 'Linux') }}

# Repository Guidelines

## Roadmap and task execution

- Read the [development roadmap](docs/development-roadmap.md) before selecting
  planned work. It owns the thirty-source consolidation, foundation scope,
  priorities, task dependencies, phase acceptance, current claims and deferred
  features; this file owns the execution rules. Existing guides retain authority
  over product/security/resource contracts.
- The planning change must merge through the existing PR/review/current-head
  checks before product execution. Start the execution cycle from that accepted
  `main` revision, beginning with F01, then select tasks with accepted relevant
  inputs. A planning merge or an existing test file is not implementation or
  acceptance evidence. Do not bypass gates or resume an unmerged planning
  snapshot as though it were the accepted baseline.
- Deliver the finite current-IM foundations and their integrated acceptance
  before post-foundation features. Forum, PWA, marketplace, external SDK and other
  roadmap-only directions require a recorded activation decision; do not build
  their speculative infrastructure during foundation work. Verified urgent
  security, data-loss or hard-freeze findings override ordinary order.
- Before a claim, recheck the live tracker, existing branches/PRs and ownership.
  Register one task owner, source/parent SHA, outcome, exact owned paths, accepted
  inputs, shared-interface/integration owner, evidence and next action. Reuse
  existing work without silently reassigning it. Keep one authoritative live
  claim record and update state/evidence before releasing the claim.
- Admit parallel mutations only with stable accepted inputs/interfaces,
  independent path and policy ownership, a clear integration order and available
  review/validation capacity. Do not start work expected to need reimplementation
  when an upstream change merges. Separate files do not prove independence;
  serialize uncertain shared contracts or limit preparation to read-only work.
  Stop and reassess dependents when their accepted interface changes.
- For coordinated parallel tasks, declare an integration branch, create children
  from its accepted tip/parent, and merge reviewed, validated compatible results
  back in dependency order before integrated acceptance and the main PR gates.
  Preserve the [worktree lifecycle](#worktree-lifecycle); never sweep unrelated
  changes or bypass preservation/cleanup rules.
- Treat module extraction as a bounded change with a real existing consumer,
  explicit policy/lifecycle/errors and recovery evidence. Measure selected
  performance paths before and after; deliver regression protection and maintained
  decisions with each slice. Retain working boundaries when no justified change
  is needed. Unknown facts become bounded investigations, not assumed defects,
  numerical targets, migrations or commitments to future features.

## Reliability before implementation

- For background work, synchronization, storage, caching or UI-state changes, read
  [performance requirements](docs/performance-requirements.md). Identify the work
  trigger, resource budget, accumulation/reclamation policy and applicable
  performance regression before editing; record measured limits and remaining
  gaps. Apply its [startup, idle and active-business checklist](docs/performance-requirements.md#apply-to-every-feature)
  to every affected phase, including return to idle after use. Extend its general
  rules when a confirmed defect reveals a new pattern.

- Before implementing, refactoring, fixing or reviewing code, read the
  [AI coding reliability guide](docs/ai-coding-reliability.md), select the rules
  triggered by the changed boundaries, and inspect the owning code and callers.
  For concurrency/lifecycle changes, trace lock order, wait dependencies, actual
  work ownership, cancellation and commit authority before editing.
- Validate the applicable failure and recovery paths, not only the happy path.
  Record concrete evidence and remaining limits; a timeout, successful build or
  passing subset is not proof that UI freezes or all deadlocks are impossible.
- When a confirmed defect exposes a reusable failure pattern, update that guide's
  existing rule or add a distinct rule with its owner and regression evidence.
  Maintain the owning contract and test selectors; keep incident logs out of the guide.

## Project Structure & Module Organization

- Four-crate Rust workspace. `crates/mesh-talk-core/` is the UI-free protocol core (lib
  `mesh_talk_core` + the `mesh-talk-node` CLI bin in `src/bin/`): feature modules `node/`,
  `identity/`, `transport/`, `discovery/`, `eventlog/`, `ratchet/`, `channel/`, `dm.rs`,
  `file/`, `postoffice/`, `storage/`. `src-tauri/` is the Tauri desktop app: entry
  `src/main.rs` → `lib.rs`, IPC glue in `commands.rs` (auth) + `chat_commands/` (messaging)
  - `events.rs`, plus `state.rs`, `tray.rs`, `services/` (auth only).
- `crates/mesh-talk-integrations/` owns scoped local messaging grants, private IPC,
  and the dedicated bot host/admin CLI; `crates/mesh-talk-mcp/` adapts its four
  send/context/status tools to the official MCP SDK. Neither owns mesh crypto.
- Integration/e2e suites live in `crates/mesh-talk-core/tests/` (`two_node_cli`,
  `persistent_history`, `post_office_offline`, `decoder_smoke`); keep unit tests inline via
  `mod tests` (e.g. `node/node_tests.rs`).
- React client sits in `frontend/src`; Vite tooling in `frontend/package.json`.
- Operational scripts in `scripts/` (`setup-hooks.sh`, `check-health.sh`); architecture in
  `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`; conventions in `specifications/`. The
  [documentation map](docs/README.md) routes readers to maintained guides; the
  [documentation guidelines](docs/DOCUMENTATION_GUIDELINES.md) define ownership
  across the README, guides, and project site.

## Build, Test, and Development Commands

- `make dev` primes Rust + Node deps and installs git hooks.
- `make build` / `make frontend-build` — release build / Vite production build.
- During feature development, preview changed-boundary validation with `make test-plan`
  and run it with `make test-changed`. Unmapped changes require an explicit owner
  and reason; inspect escalation notes for browser/native or consumer checks.
  Use `make verify-plan` / `make verify-changed` at task completion to compose the
  same affected tests with applicable formatting, lint/types and builds. The
  test-only commands do not include static checks; neither mode replaces required
  PR/review, browser/native or release gates. `make validation-report` separates
  queue and execution costs; `make validation-audit` compares a clean affected
  plan with same-source broader failure evidence before narrowing any gate.
  Read selected capability references and inspect pending browser/native requirements.
  Execution prints a structured feedback report; follow the
  [validation protocol](docs/testing-feedback-loop.md#validation-stages-and-agent-responsibilities)
  for completed work, remaining evidence and additive semantic selections.
- During feature development, run affected tests only: `make test-focused
TEST_PACKAGE=mesh-talk-core TEST_FILTER=node::account_sync` selects Rust unit
  tests; add `TEST_TARGET=bridge_cross_lan` to select one integration target.
  `cd frontend && npm test -- src/features/chat/settingsDialogSession.test.ts`
  selects a frontend unit file. `make test` runs the full workspace suite
  (`cargo test --workspace`) for pre-PR and CI gates;
  `make e2e` runs the `#[ignore]`d multi-process backend rigs; `cd frontend && npm run e2e`
  runs the Playwright UI suite. Test builds use cheap KDF params (the `fast-test-kdf`
  feature), and `.cargo/config.toml` caps test/compile parallelism.
- UI / node spot checks: `make tauri-dev`, `make frontend-dev`,
  `cargo run -p mesh-talk-core --bin mesh-talk-node -- --keystore /tmp/a.keystore
--password pw --name alice` (add `--post-office` for relay mode).

## Coding Style & Naming Conventions

- Rust: `cargo fmt` (4-space, `snake_case` modules, `UpperCamelCase` types) +
  **`cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`** (must match CI — `--all-targets` covers
  tests/benches).
- Frontend: `npm run format` (Prettier) + `npm run lint` (ESLint flat config).
- Write documentation and reusable prompts in English unless a specific exception is needed.
- Reference `specifications/development_conventions.md` for naming nuances.

## Domain Language

- `CONTEXT.md` is the canonical domain glossary. `docs/domain-design.md` indexes
  the modeling references and defines DDD vocabulary and naming translations.
- Distinguish local users, accounts and devices; desktop, transport and ratchet
  sessions; discovery, presence, custody, recipient delivery and read state.
- Use explicit identity/lifetime names in new code. Preserve public, wire and
  stored identifiers unless a separately validated compatibility change is intended.
- Update the glossary and affected owning guides when a domain meaning changes;
  link to definitions instead of maintaining duplicate glossaries.

## Architecture & Components

- Before adding business logic, consult [module ownership and reuse](docs/module-boundaries.md),
  inspect the owning module and its callers, and extend its existing implementation.
  Parallel tasks should name their owned paths and shared-interface dependencies;
  coordinate changes to shared interfaces through one integration owner. Keep
  feature-specific helpers local and share rules when their meaning and lifecycle
  are the same. The guide owns the detailed assignment and handoff contract.
- Stack: Rust 2024 on Tokio; Tauri 2 + React shell. No vendor-operated server.
- The `Node` (`node/node.rs`) wires identity + signed UDP **multicast** discovery
  (group `224.0.0.167`, port 47474) + Noise-encrypted TCP transport (`transport/`,
  low-level socket in `transport/net.rs`) + the content-addressed event log + DM/channel/
  file crypto. Messages are events synced as a bounded append-only log, account-addressed
  across a user's devices; optional offline custody via equal eligible post offices.
  Routed discovery and opt-in post-office federation connect reachable sites without
  joining their IP subnets. Wire formats are versioned bincode.
- See **`docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`** before changing crypto, sync, or transport;
  **`docs/network-design-reference.md`** owns the communication invariants,
  module contracts, resource budgets and topology acceptance boundaries.

## Maintaining standards as requirements change

- Before changing tests, fixtures, dependencies or workflows in ways that affect
  CI cost or reliability, read [CI maintenance](docs/ci-maintenance.md). Reuse
  existing owners, measure the affected cost, and preserve acceptance evidence;
  keep required-check policy in its existing owner.
- Before implementation, identify the existing decision owner, authoritative rule,
  observable acceptance criteria, affected consumers and required boundary evidence.
  Extend the owning implementation and `validation.json`; new business capabilities
  should link their guide and invariants. Explain an unchanged contract in the PR.
- Run `make standards-check` after adding/moving source or changing contracts. It
  checks structural ownership and maintained references, including new files; it
  does not prove assertion quality, semantic completeness or candidate readiness.
  Hooks inspect the working tree, so partially staged commits still need a clean
  committed-candidate check in CI. Frontend dependencies must be installed.
- When CI exposes a local omission or flaky fixture, fix the owning selector, task
  or fixture and add a focused regression. Review timing and selection evidence
  before changing policy. Follow the maintained
  [requirement maintenance loop](docs/testing-feedback-loop.md#maintaining-standards-across-requirements).

## Testing Guidelines

- Integration coverage in `crates/mesh-talk-core/tests/` and `node/node_tests.rs`; embed
  unit tests near the code. Networking/crypto changes ship a loopback integration assertion.
- Backend multi-process E2E via `make e2e` (CI: `e2e-backend.yml`); Playwright UI E2E via
  `cd frontend && npm run e2e` (CI: `e2e-ui.yml`).
- Do not run full suites or E2E automatically during ordinary feature work. Run
  the affected unit or integration tests as changes are made; run E2E and the
  comprehensive health gate on explicit request, for optional full local preparation,
  or in CI.
- See `docs/testing-feedback-loop.md` for selection examples and escalation triggers.
- Document executed validation commands in every PR; ensure `make test` passes
  locally or through its matching CI workspace suite before merge.

## Commit & Pull Request Guidelines

- Before changing product versions or release automation, read [the version lifecycle](docs/updates.md#version-ownership-and-lifecycle).
  Root `Cargo.toml` `[workspace.package].version` is authoritative. Use
  `node scripts/release/version.mjs check|sync|prepare VERSION` (the `VERSION` argument belongs
  to `prepare` only); do not hand-edit generated npm/Cargo lock metadata or introduce another
  version constant. Root private npm metadata is a checked release-tooling projection;
  frontend private metadata is versionless and Tauri inherits Cargo. Never broadly replace
  matching dependency, fixture, history, wire or schema versions. Keep source builds `BASE-dev`,
  Nightlies `BASE-nightly.RUN.ATTEMPT`, official tagged builds `BASE`, and standard SemVer ordering.
- Version/changelog preparation and next-development-target changes use reviewed PRs. Ordinary main
  pushes must not create automatic release proposals or commit-derived product notes. Stable publication
  remains explicit through the existing verified tagged-release workflow; no direct main push,
  public empty release, mutable published tag or gate bypass. Nightly publication requires trusted
  `main` and a target above the latest Stable. Future changes must extend the existing version
  owner, its tests, standards/CI enforcement and capability contracts together; the owning guide
  documents permissions, bot-PR checks, dispatch and recovery requirements. Manual Stable draft
  preparation uses the reviewed exact-version CHANGELOG section and requires exact-source checks
  before creating its immutable tag/draft. The fixed release-history
  migration floor is historical provenance; never advance it during ordinary version bumps.

- Conventional commits (`feat:`, `fix:`, `refactor:`); scopes like `feat(node):` align with
  `specifications/git_standards.md`. Squash WIP; link issues. When asked to merge,
  default to squash merge unless the user explicitly requests another strategy;
  follow the [merge policy](specifications/git_standards.md#pull-request-merge-strategy)
  and current-head required checks.
- Create PRs through `./scripts/create-pr.sh -- <gh pr create options>`.
  The default checks the clean committed candidate, comparison base, argument safety,
  whitespace, cheap affected static checks, ownership blockers, structural standards,
  repository hygiene and applicable verified frontend patch coverage before publication.
  Use `make pr-check` for the same cheap static phase; missing current coverage
  evidence reports its explicit generation command and never starts suites implicitly.
  CI runs after publication; full-scope candidates retain cross-platform execution.
  Only the proven [documentation scope](docs/ci-maintenance.md#documentation-only-pr-scope)
  may omit unrelated product tests. All required checks must pass on the current PR head before merging. Creating a PR does not certify test acceptance.
- To run comprehensive checks locally before publication, use
  `./scripts/create-pr.sh --full-preflight <selectors/specs> -- <gh pr create options>`.
  This invokes `prepare-pr.sh` (platform preflight plus full health). For an existing
  PR, `./scripts/prepare-pr.sh <selectors/specs>` provides the same optional local gate.
  Use Playwright specs relevant to changed frontend behavior and repeated
  `--core-filter` / `--host-filter` / `--integration-filter` / `--mcp-filter` selectors
  for changed Rust crates. Preflight runs selected tests in Linux Docker and through
  SSH to `windows10`; Windows workspaces, caches and temporary data stay on drive D.
  Owning scenario rules add visual specs and require real native evidence for
  lifecycle/discovery changes. Missing environments or empty Rust selections fail
  full preflight. Include `e2e/ui-visual-regression.spec.ts` for theme/layout changes.
  See `docs/testing-feedback-loop.md` for configuration, coverage and plan preview.
  Fetch `origin/main` first if the comparison base is stale.
- Record focused validation and outstanding checks in the PR. Use
  `./scripts/check-health.sh` when comprehensive local evidence is needed; protected
  CI remains required before merge regardless of local results.

## Security & Adjustments

- `./scripts/check-health.sh` chains fmt, Clippy `--all-targets`, ESLint, tests, typos,
  cargo-deny, cargo-machete, gitleaks, shellcheck, audits, and both builds.
- Triage vulnerabilities immediately or document mitigation in the PR.
- If plans shift, update the relevant committed design or architecture docs. Keep
  `docs/superpowers/` and the root `plans/` directory local and untracked.

## Repository Hygiene

### Worktree lifecycle

- Create a worktree only when isolation is needed. Before creating one, inspect
  `git worktree list --porcelain` and record the task-owned path, branch and any
  dedicated build directory in ignored `tmp/` task notes. Treat pre-existing
  worktrees and unrelated changes as user-owned; never sweep them automatically.
- The coordinating session owns cleanup of every worktree it creates or delegates,
  including `.worktrees/` and `.claude/worktrees/agent-*`. Delegate completion does
  not transfer that responsibility. Before ending the task, stop task-owned
  processes and remove its worktrees, disposable branches and dedicated Cargo
  target directories, subject to the preservation rules below. Never delete a
  shared target directory or a directory whose ownership is uncertain.
- Before removal, preserve the work through either a verified merge into the
  intended integration branch under the existing PR/merge gates, or a local
  archive. For an archive, commit only task-owned outstanding changes (including
  intended untracked files), run the required commit checks, and create a unique
  `archive/<worktree-name>-<timestamp>` tag at the final branch tip. Verify the tag
  resolves to that tip and the worktree is clean before deleting anything. Never
  overwrite an existing archive tag, include secrets/ignored build output, or
  discard unrelated edits to make cleanup succeed. Cleanup does not authorize
  merging, pushing, bypassing review or running `entire clean`.
- Run removal from a surviving checkout with `git worktree remove <path>`, then
  `git branch -d <branch>` for a merged branch. Use `git branch -D <branch>` only
  for a task-owned archived branch after verifying its archive tag. Never use
  forced worktree removal, hard reset or bulk directory deletion to bypass a
  dirty worktree. Detached worktrees require the same preservation of their final
  commit before removal; there is no branch to delete.
- A pending PR, unresolved conflict, user decision, active concurrent session or
  failed preservation/cleanup step is an explicit retention exception. Preserve
  the required branch for an open PR; remove its clean worktree if no active work
  needs it. Recheck `git worktree list --porcelain` and task-owned branches/build
  paths before the final reply. Report cleanup performed and name every retained
  path/branch, its reason and the next action; never silently leave task worktrees.

- Keep implementation plans, research, investigation notes and scratch scripts
  under ignored `tmp/`; remove them when the work is complete.
- Merge durable decisions into the maintained owning guide. Do not commit
  completed-work reports, score histories, duplicate runbooks or archive copies.
- `docs/evals/` owns reusable suites/inventories, prompts and its README only.
  Generated evidence belongs in ignored output or PR/CI artifacts.
- Run `node scripts/check-repository-hygiene.mjs` before committing. The shared
  index check also runs in pre-commit, CI and health, rejecting ignored files
  even when force-added. See `docs/DOCUMENTATION_GUIDELINES.md` for ownership.

</INSTRUCTIONS>
