# Implementation status and acceptance boundaries

This stable path is the current status index, not a chronological TODO list or a
claim that every topology/platform combination has been verified. Feature and
protocol details belong to the linked owning guides; Git history records completed
work.

## Current capability areas

| Area                       | Implemented behavior                                                                                                                                  | Reference / boundary                                                                                                                                                                    |
| -------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Direct conversations       | Signed discovery, identity-pinned Noise/TCP, encrypted account-addressed DMs, replies, reactions, mentions, search and retained history.              | [Architecture](../docs/ARCHITECTURE.md); discovery and TCP reachability remain separate.                                                                                                |
| Groups                     | Signed membership controls, sender-key encryption, bounded fanout and authorized member recovery with per-member sharing.                             | [Group flows and scenarios](../docs/network-design-reference.md#d-group-creation-distribution-and-member-recovery); a removed/nonmember device cannot acquire authority from discovery. |
| Relay networking           | Equal trusted post offices, shared public enrollment, opaque custody/federation, direct-first attempts, soft preference and alternatives.             | [Network baseline](../docs/network-design-reference.md); an alternate needs a surviving onward route.                                                                                   |
| Network controls           | Per-device master/send/receive/directory preferences, physical-LAN-only discovery and direct LAN/Tailscale relay selection.                           | [Privacy controls](../docs/privacy-controls.md); visibility does not grant conversation authority or create a firewall.                                                                 |
| Files and folders          | Encrypted chunks, exact-offer consent, durable decisions, restart recovery, integrity checks and recipient completion.                                | [File flow](../docs/network-design-reference.md#e-files-folders-consent-and-completion); card arrival is not byte completion.                                                           |
| Linked devices             | Code-authorized enrollment, certified sibling synchronization and device-local category preferences.                                                  | [Pairing and replay](../docs/network-design-reference.md#g-linking-and-ongoing-account-synchronization); full replay needs its own live authenticated route.                            |
| Calls                      | Optional device-addressed live Noise signaling and separate WebRTC media.                                                                             | No post-office signaling fallback or TURN service; native WebView and physical capture acceptance remain separate.                                                                      |
| Desktop presentation       | Shared person/relay classification, account/device profile details, themes, avatars, stickers, virtualized navigation and optional pack installation. | [Visual system](../frontend/DESIGN.md) · [Customization packs](../docs/CUSTOMIZATION_PACKS.md).                                                                                         |
| Local privacy and recovery | Privacy presets, lock controls, hidden contacts, local retention, recall and encrypted manual backup/restore.                                         | [Privacy](../docs/privacy-controls.md) · [Backup/recovery](../docs/backup-recovery.md); restore creates a new device and cannot revoke an old one.                                      |

## Deliberate design boundaries

- **Pairing authorization:** a one-time 128-bit code binds the linker and joiner
  device keys. Durable enrollment invalidates old sessions; interrupted adoption
  has a restricted code-authenticated retry. There is no separate SAS ceremony.
- **Relay metadata:** production relays store opaque outer events, not readable
  original authors, conversation IDs or channel controls. Connection identities,
  pseudonymous mailboxes, size buckets and timing remain observable. See
  [the exact privacy boundary](../docs/post-office-metadata-privacy.md).
- **Bounded custody:** relay copies have capacity limits and a 30-day maximum age;
  this is not guaranteed minimum retention or permanent storage.
- **Connections:** the client Node has bounded sequential session reuse, not one
  multiplexed socket per relay or an eight-socket ceiling for the whole machine.
- **Reachability and trust:** Tailscale does not merge LANs; explicit relay trust
  and client directory consent are independent of routing.
- **Membership presentation:** removed group members' past reactions no longer
  render under the current-membership visibility rule.
- **Linux dependency constraint:** the maintained
  [GLib compatibility workflow](../.github/workflows/glib-0.20-watch.yml) tracks the
  GTK/Tauri dependency gate. Consult the lockfile and security configuration before
  changing versions; do not treat this note as a vulnerability waiver.

## Foundation qualification status

The [current-IM foundation inventory](../docs/module-boundaries.md#current-im-foundation-inventory)
binds the capability areas above to source owners, actual callers, store categories,
representative assertion bodies and remaining unknowns at source
`5fe57c380b4b047ced19337b1233013d6d0ffcd7`. Its implemented/partial/scoped-missing/unknown
labels describe static inspection scope, not new passing tests or accepted runtime
measurements. The [roadmap](../docs/development-roadmap.md#task-claims-branches-and-integration)
remains the sole foundation claim tracker and acceptance order.

Current indexed participant storage, direct-account desktop enqueue and group
account-operation submission paths must be distinguished from retained standalone
log/device-send compatibility callers and explicit physical-channel enqueue adapters. Experimental Bluetooth and historical mobile-PWA work are not production
foundation acceptance. The bounded F01 inputs have local static-review acceptance;
F02 verification, F03 measurements and F04 contract qualification remain outstanding
before construction. F01 does not certify F10 or authorize later features.

## Evidence and future decisions

The [implementation/evidence tracker](../docs/network-design-reference.md#implementation-and-evidence-tracker)
records named logical and physical checks. Three independent physical LANs, a
separate ordinary client host on the mini's LAN, native macOS WebView media and
physical camera/microphone quality remain distinct acceptance cases.

New protocol capabilities such as true multiplexing, automatic federation trust,
mailbox-backed calling, TURN or stronger replicated-storage guarantees require
an explicit design and new evidence. They are not implied by the implemented
capabilities above.

### Parallel admission

## First execution handoff

After this planning change merges, start F01 from that main revision. F01 is an
reconciliation, and mark a missing policy as unknown instead of asserting a
local default. A policy observation cannot authorize archive or attachment
release; those owners recheck current membership and disclosure policy.

Group creation retains its existing public creation and invitation producer.
Its owner-scoped desktop adapter checks the expected account and exact runtime
session before resolving invitees and rechecks at the creation commit. Both
desktop creation adapters take account IDs, not device IDs. The existing
`channels/account_invitation.rs` owner authenticates the selected account and
compatible format over Noise, trying its known routes. Creation reuses that
resolver and the existing account-authority grants, including one pending grant
per invited account and an immediately accepted creator-account owner grant.
The existing atomic new-channel event-store boundary publishes genesis, account
authority and initial history policy together; interrupted creation cannot expose
a device-only genesis while losing its account grants.
It does not invent an existing group lifetime or operation reference before genesis.

Typed desktop operation commands capture the exact local session owner and
expected account. Durable submission and cancellation recheck that authority at
the core admission callback; lifecycle reads retain the matching runtime guard.
The guarded ID factory binds an opaque ID to the full origin device and a random
nonce without accepting work. Deduplication still belongs to the account and ID;
a sibling resolves the original reference before resuming a foreign-origin ID.
Submission rechecks the existing entry under the final journal write lock after
transport preflight: an authenticated result may arrive during preflight. A
matching retry returns that retained status; a mismatched group or digest still
rejects the ID, and lookup admission never replaces an adopted result.
Logical operation IDs remain separate from committed public event IDs. Bounded
list and status projections contain lifecycle metadata only. The frontend IPC
adapter preserves pending outcomes for the existing action and outgoing-intent
owners; acceptance alone does not finish a dialog or mark a message as sent.

Simple owner controls prepare their exact signed public effect from the same
locked canonical membership projection used to revalidate the pinned source.
Their original logical operation, request digest and full executor identity bind
the existing delivery WAL; durable public effects and sidecars precede the
immutable completion result. A canonical no-op still requires a durable parent
view and never invents a public event ID. Affected source access and inventory
publish through their existing signed owners before public fanout can wait on a
slow member.
Ordinary and legacy operation-document publishers own their per-Node unit
ordering gate. Each group pass takes it before capturing the journal projection
and retains it through signed store merge, with no caller-held journal, document,
membership or delivery guard. The unit contains no durable payload, so recovering
its poison does not recover or bypass a poisoned journal or store.
The document store retains at most 128 runtime-only operation-publication
qualifications containing exact metadata, a projection fingerprint and a fixed
five-minute repair deadline. Publishers compare fresh projections and current
verified-own-head evidence before body access. These contain no document bodies
or authority; explicit consumers retain durable integrity checks. No gate spans
network work; invitation preparation precedes its admitted blocking local commit.

Authenticated body-free sibling invalidations remain active independently of
optional content categories. Mandatory control requests and results reuse that
bounded wake and account-document channel; content transfer still applies its
own category, sharing and read-entitlement checks. The existing two mandatory
workers reserve one slot for GroupControl and one for group inventory/device
names. Each lane retains its own full-peer-identity cursor, partial page, refresh
and retry state. A held directory response cannot delay an explicit operation
request or result; control traffic cannot consume the directory's reserved slot.
Combined progress is up to date only when both lanes have settled, and an error
or required upgrade in either lane remains visible. The shared TCP budget and
authentication, category and authority checks remain unchanged. The
[network contract](network-design-reference.md#g-linking-and-ongoing-account-synchronization)
owns the distinction between an accepted account's private copy and public
physical membership.

The other two existing synchronization slots are partitioned between optional
private documents and history/favorites. A held history response cannot delay an
authorized custody confirmation, profile or preference document. History and
favorites preserve their own continuations and coalesced refreshes; their errors
do not replace document progress. Optional document category and entitlement
checks still apply. Together with control and directory work, these remain four
workers in the same shared session pool, not additional network capacity.

### Account profiles and private trust

`identity/account.rs` and `identity/account_keystore.rs` own immutable creation
metadata persisted with the account key. Pairing and recovery preserve it without
inferring missing dates. `node/account_profile_data.rs` owns signed bounded
ordinary profile data and current-profile persistence; `node/account_profile_io.rs`
owns admitted edits, authenticated reception and legacy compatibility.
`storage/profile/profile_receive.rs` owns account-scoped exact receive evidence
and retry scheduling; `node/profile_receive_work.rs` is its compatibility facade.
The storage owner records exact, account-qualified superseded-source retirement
inside the authorized compaction transaction, independently of bounded discovery.
Neither processing nor retirement evidence grants custody. Retry scheduling runs on the profile's encrypted SQL connection. Discovery advances
through at most 128 committed event headers; each retry pass selects 16 fixed
metadata rows before loading one signed body at a time. Unknown devices and
disabled sibling-profile synchronization remain pending. Current-profile writes
finish before processed evidence is committed, so a crash or storage failure
retries idempotently. No historical profile-ID set is rebuilt in memory.
Send preparation enters host authority before acquiring the delivery journal.
Desktop biography saves reply after durable local acceptance while admitted fanout
continues independently. The ordinary nickname and bio edit share the publication
mutex, preventing a stale bio save from undoing a rename.
Profile-store guards end before delivery preparation acquires channel, routing or
event-log state. Group inventory first snapshots channel facts, releases the channel
book, then resolves profile names and routing classifications. Neither side may
retain one of these guards while waiting for the other. Deterministic lock-boundary
regressions cover background publication, biography/avatar edits and inventory
projection; keep them in both affected validation selections.
`src-tauri/src/account_profile.rs` exposes reads and bio edits, with no caller-supplied
names, timestamps or public proofs. `src-tauri/src/trust.rs` owns private observation
history and manual verification. Frontend `store/accountProfiles.ts` shares
session-bound profile reads and live invalidations across the header and dialogs.
The [profile and verification guide](peer-trust.md) owns meanings and evidence limits.

## Google Drive recovery transport

`src-tauri/src/google_drive/` owns remembered password-encrypted local OAuth
refresh grants, ephemeral operation connections, exact-session admission, bounded
Drive HTTP transfers and temporary encrypted file lifetimes. Its `remembered.rs`
keeps Google credentials native and separate from recovery archives.
`src-tauri/src/recovery.rs` remains the owner of consistent snapshot/runtime restart,
archive verification and transactional profile restore. Its `recovery/setup.rs`
owns the reusable local recovery key, one-time acknowledgement and selected
destination, using the existing password-encrypted local-user storage and exact
session/lock authority. `core/recovery/` owns format
and cryptography. `ui/lib/api/googleDrive.ts` adapts IPC, and
`ui/features/recovery/` provides shared connection/progress presentation for the
existing export/restore dialogs. See [backup and recovery](backup-recovery.md#google-drive-security-and-boundaries).

## Bounded history for channel invitations

`channel/history.rs` owns the four fixed history policy presets. The existing
channel lifecycle in `node/channels.rs` owns invitations; `node/join_history.rs`
owns frozen encrypted copies, owner-policy validation and post-acceptance row-key
release. It reuses the delivery journal, channel crypto primitives, causal
membership projection and received-history store. Desktop IPC delegates authority
to core; the member dialog presents the policy without independently deciding
history eligibility. The [channel guide](help/topics/channels.md#history-for-new-members)
owns user-visible limits and availability.

Native message presentation is queued onto the UI thread before acquiring the
exact desktop-session guard. The queued callback revalidates its session and runtime
ticket before emitting private events or notifications. A worker must not hold that
guard while synchronously querying window focus: the UI thread may itself be waiting
for the same session. `events.rs` owns this dispatch boundary and its lock-order and
stale-session regressions; `runtime_bootstrap.rs` uses it for DM, group and file callbacks.

### Account document projections

`node/account_documents/` owns private typed metadata and blobs, not group
authority or public identity. The existing account worker and session carry
manifest pages and bounded chunks; there is no second network daemon. Native
`account_documents.rs` checks exact local owner, runtime account and version
before mutations or plaintext release. Frontend linked coordinators project
accepted records into the owning draft, reception, pack and avatar stores; they
never own another network synchronization loop. Pack validation remains in
`pack.ts`; pack storage is namespaced by local owner and cryptographic account.
Pack storage's sparse numeric pending index selects pending records before
cloning archived/image payloads. Its version-three catalog sidecar contains only
IDs, labels and appearance metadata; startup and compact summaries do not hydrate
the complete library. Upgrade backfill and every subsequent
row/index update share their transaction; a failed commit cannot acknowledge an
edit. Public and legacy namespaces preserve their existing records. Migration
may scan old rows once; quiet pending reads must not enumerate the full library.
Receipt projections drain available pages in bounded batches and yield between
batches; owner retirement cancels queued continuation without claiming mutation
completion. Full payload reads are scoped point lookups; view owners retain only required
payloads, and the selected theme has its own readiness owner. Sequential native
sticker-source preparation uses transient reads and compact registration receipts,
not a renderer-wide image cache. The storage owner retains only active-account
and public database connections, retiring old scope/session handles after their
admitted operations settle. Unchanged linked versions stay outside read-write
admission; atomic mutations retain fresh scope/version checks. Local edit
revisions trigger publication after edit ownership is released; selected-theme
changes and remote projection do not restart it. See
[pack loading](CUSTOMIZATION_PACKS.md#runtime-loading).
`settings/shared.rs` owns the allowlist mapping of portable settings onto existing
per-key account preferences. Device paths, system permissions, autostart and
local-agent grants stay outside the replicated allowlist.
`account_documents/controls.rs` owns authenticated private DM control publication,
original-action ordering and sibling projections. `reactions.rs` and `recall.rs`
publish accepted actions through it; generic native document mutations cannot
create control records. Explicit kept-source preparation validates legacy caches.
`account_sync/archive.rs` filters known recalled private bodies/cards and invalidates cached
exports when the control revision changes. Group authority and local deletion
remain with their existing owners.

`channel_custody.rs` owns locally observed exact-event possession and retractions;
its indexed child keeps those exact positive and negative observations in the
leased profile database, with selected-event reads and 32-row keyset migration
pages. It shares the history-source publisher and legacy-writer barrier rather
than retaining the custody journal in memory. Auxiliary source identities 16–18
use a separate registry without rewriting the installed transcript-source schema.
`account_documents/custody.rs` owns their account-private versioned publication
and sibling projection. It reuses certified account sessions and document digests,
without adding a group transport or claiming recipient delivery. Channel authority
determines eligible external member principals. The footer distinguishes missing
status from a known zero count; its status coordinator clears stale projections
only for the messages and runtime lifetime it requested.
The document store keeps a separate bounded custody-key quota and an owned-file
scan budget consistent with legal document counts. `media_store.rs` prunes the
enumerated unreferenced regular files in one pass, preserving live files and
synchronizing the parent directory before successful return.

`account_documents/public_profile.rs` relays original signed contact profiles under
Profile consent; `account_profile_io.rs` retains signature, revision and avatar
projection authority. Per-source document heads preserve each contact's original
profile. Constructor work initializes only the optional reconciliation receipts;
the existing account-sync worker repairs at most sixteen publication heads and
sixteen projection heads per turn. Exact account/device-scoped completion receipts
compare accepted profile change revisions or signed document revision/hash before
loading avatars. Missing or failed receipts remain retryable after restart; an
unchanged warm open does not replay contact document payloads. Canonical profile
admission and its interrupted avatar projection keep their existing owners.
`account_documents/group_activity.rs` owns History-gated source-signed control
observations tied to the selected inventory snapshot. It cannot install membership
or keys. Both reuse the existing document worker and certified sibling sessions.

`account_documents/inventory.rs` owns source-certified descriptive group snapshots,
bounded automatic publication and account-private reference projection. It reuses
the document version/digest owner and private account worker. The group directory
is mandatory account topology; optional history, profile, appearance and contact
data retain their existing policies. A source reads real local group state and
never republishes a borrowed reference as authority. The native channel adapter
may project reference member facts for display under runtime admission; group
authorization, keys and mutations remain exclusively with the existing channel
owners. The frontend distinguishes this read-only reference from a backup archive
and removes its explanation when real validated group state arrives.

`node/account_documents/device_hostname.rs` owns bounded private per-device hostname
publication and certified-roster projection. The desktop runtime bootstrap reads
OS hostnames; admitted sync IPC releases them only for the expected current account.
`PersonalDevices` renders them without changing identity, account nicknames or
presence semantics. Hostnames reuse encrypted account-document persistence and the
existing certified sibling transport; public discovery and profiles never carry
them. See [private account synchronization](network-design-reference.md#g-linking-and-ongoing-account-synchronization).

### Parallel admission

Start parallel mutations only when all relevant inputs and shared interfaces are
accepted, path and policy ownership are independent, a review/integration owner
is available and no known upstream change is expected to invalidate the result.
Separate files alone do not establish independence. If a dependency remains
unstable, wait or do nonmutating preparation instead of building something that
will need reimplementation after merge. Stop/reassess if an accepted interface
changes. Incidental textual conflicts can occur; expected semantic rework is a
reason not to dispatch.

Use a declared integration branch when coordinating related parallel tasks.
Create each child from its accepted tip/parent, validate and review it, then merge
compatible results back in dependency order. Update dependent branches against
the integrated interface before final qualification. The integration branch
still needs existing current-head PR/review/CI gates before main. Do not treat
this workflow as permission to merge unreviewed children or bypass any gate.

Keep task notes/plans/profiles in ignored `tmp/` or validation artifacts. Preserve
and clean task-owned worktrees, disposable branches and dedicated build paths
under the repository lifecycle rules. An active task/PR is an explicit retention
reason; unrelated worktrees remain user-owned.

## First execution handoff

After this planning change merges, start F01 from that main revision. F01 is an
reconciliation, and mark a missing policy as unknown instead of asserting a
local default. A policy observation cannot authorize archive or attachment
release; those owners recheck current membership and disclosure policy.

Group creation retains its existing public creation and invitation producer.
Its owner-scoped desktop adapter checks the expected account and exact runtime
session before resolving invitees and rechecks at the creation commit. Both
desktop creation adapters take account IDs, not device IDs. The existing
`channels/account_invitation.rs` owner authenticates the selected account and
compatible format over Noise, trying its known routes. Creation reuses that
resolver and the existing account-authority grants, including one pending grant
per invited account and an immediately accepted creator-account owner grant.
The existing atomic new-channel event-store boundary publishes genesis, account
authority and initial history policy together; interrupted creation cannot expose
a device-only genesis while losing its account grants.
It does not invent an existing group lifetime or operation reference before genesis.

Typed desktop operation commands capture the exact local session owner and
expected account. Durable submission and cancellation recheck that authority at
the core a…531 tokens truncated…head evidence before body access. These contain no document bodies
or authority; explicit consumers retain durable integrity checks. No gate spans
network work; invitation preparation precedes its admitted blocking local commit.

Authenticated body-free sibling invalidations remain active independently of
optional content categories. Mandatory control requests and results reuse that
bounded wake and account-document channel; content transfer still applies its
own category, sharing and read-entitlement checks. The existing two mandatory
workers reserve one slot for GroupControl and one for group inventory/device
names. Each lane retains its own full-peer-identity cursor, partial page, refresh
and retry state. A held directory response cannot delay an explicit operation
request or result; control traffic cannot consume the directory's reserved slot.
Combined progress is up to date only when both lanes have settled, and an error
or required upgrade in either lane remains visible. The shared TCP budget and
authentication, category and authority checks remain unchanged. The
[network contract](network-design-reference.md#g-linking-and-ongoing-account-synchronization)
owns the distinction between an accepted account's private copy and public
physical membership.

The other two existing synchronization slots are partitioned between optional
private documents and history/favorites. A held history response cannot delay an
authorized custody confirmation, profile or preference document. History and
favorites preserve their own continuations and coalesced refreshes; their errors
do not replace document progress. Optional document category and entitlement
checks still apply. Together with control and directory work, these remain four
workers in the same shared session pool, not additional network capacity.

### Account profiles and private trust

`identity/account.rs` and `identity/account_keystore.rs` own immutable creation
metadata persisted with the account key. Pairing and recovery preserve it without
inferring missing dates. `node/account_profile_data.rs` owns signed bounded
ordinary profile data and current-profile persistence; `node/account_profile_io.rs`
owns admitted edits, authenticated reception and legacy compatibility.
`storage/profile/profile_receive.rs` owns account-scoped exact receive evidence
and retry scheduling; `node/profile_receive_work.rs` is its compatibility facade.
The storage owner records exact, account-qualified superseded-source retirement
inside the authorized compaction transaction, independently of bounded discovery.
Neither processing nor retirement evidence grants custody. Retry scheduling runs on the profile's encrypted SQL connection. Discovery advances
through at most 128 committed event headers; each retry pass selects 16 fixed
metadata rows before loading one signed body at a time. Unknown devices and
disabled sibling-profile synchronization remain pending. Current-profile writes
finish before processed evidence is committed, so a crash or storage failure
retries idempotently. No historical profile-ID set is rebuilt in memory.
Send preparation enters host authority before acquiring the delivery journal.
Desktop biography saves reply after durable local acceptance while admitted fanout
continues independently. The ordinary nickname and bio edit share the publication
mutex, preventing a stale bio save from undoing a rename.
Profile-store guards end before delivery preparation acquires channel, routing or
event-log state. Group inventory first snapshots channel facts, releases the channel
book, then resolves profile names and routing classifications. Neither side may
retain one of these guards while waiting for the other. Deterministic lock-boundary
regressions cover background publication, biography/avatar edits and inventory
projection; keep them in both affected validation selections.
`src-tauri/src/account_profile.rs` exposes reads and bio edits, with no caller-supplied
names, timestamps or public proofs. `src-tauri/src/trust.rs` owns private observation
history and manual verification. Frontend `store/accountProfiles.ts` shares
session-bound profile reads and live invalidations across the header and dialogs.
The [profile and verification guide](peer-trust.md) owns meanings and evidence limits.

## Google Drive recovery transport

`src-tauri/src/google_drive/` owns remembered password-encrypted local OAuth
refresh grants, ephemeral operation connections, exact-session admission, bounded
Drive HTTP transfers and temporary encrypted file lifetimes. Its `remembered.rs`
keeps Google credentials native and separate from recovery archives.
`src-tauri/src/recovery.rs` remains the owner of consistent snapshot/runtime restart,
archive verification and transactional profile restore. Its `recovery/setup.rs`
owns the reusable local recovery key, one-time acknowledgement and selected
destination, using the existing password-encrypted local-user storage and exact
session/lock authority. `core/recovery/` owns format
and cryptography. `ui/lib/api/googleDrive.ts` adapts IPC, and
`ui/features/recovery/` provides shared connection/progress presentation for the
existing export/restore dialogs. See [backup and recovery](backup-recovery.md#google-drive-security-and-boundaries).

## Bounded history for channel invitations

`channel/history.rs` owns the four fixed history policy presets. The existing
channel lifecycle in `node/channels.rs` owns invitations; `node/join_history.rs`
owns frozen encrypted copies, owner-policy validation and post-acceptance row-key
release. It reuses the delivery journal, channel crypto primitives, causal
membership projection and received-history store. Desktop IPC delegates authority
to core; the member dialog presents the policy without independently deciding
history eligibility. The [channel guide](help/topics/channels.md#history-for-new-members)
owns user-visible limits and availability.

Native message presentation is queued onto the UI thread before acquiring the
exact desktop-session guard. The queued callback revalidates its session and runtime
ticket before emitting private events or notifications. A worker must not hold that
guard while synchronously querying window focus: the UI thread may itself be waiting
for the same session. `events.rs` owns this dispatch boundary and its lock-order and
stale-session regressions; `runtime_bootstrap.rs` uses it for DM, group and file callbacks.

### Account document projections

`node/account_documents/` owns private typed metadata and blobs, not group
authority or public identity. The existing account worker and session carry
manifest pages and bounded chunks; there is no second network daemon. Native
`account_documents.rs` checks exact local owner, runtime account and version
before mutations or plaintext release. Frontend linked coordinators project
accepted records into the owning draft, reception, pack and avatar stores; they
never own another network synchronization loop. Pack validation remains in
`pack.ts`; pack storage is namespaced by local owner and cryptographic account.
Pack storage's sparse numeric pending index selects pending records before
cloning archived/image payloads. Its version-three catalog sidecar contains only
IDs, labels and appearance metadata; startup and compact summaries do not hydrate
the complete library. Upgrade backfill and every subsequent
row/index update share their transaction; a failed commit cannot acknowledge an
edit. Public and legacy namespaces preserve their existing records. Migration
may scan old rows once; quiet pending reads must not enumerate the full library.
Receipt projections drain available pages in bounded batches and yield between
batches; owner retirement cancels queued continuation without claiming mutation
completion. Full payload reads are scoped point lookups; view owners retain only required
payloads, and the selected theme has its own readiness owner. Sequential native
sticker-source preparation uses transient reads and compact registration receipts,
not a renderer-wide image cache. The storage owner retains only active-account
and public database connections, retiring old scope/session handles after their
admitted operations settle. Unchanged linked versions stay outside read-write
admission; atomic mutations retain fresh scope/version checks. Local edit
revisions trigger publication after edit ownership is released; selected-theme
changes and remote projection do not restart it. See
[pack loading](CUSTOMIZATION_PACKS.md#runtime-loading).
`settings/shared.rs` owns the allowlist mapping of portable settings onto existing
per-key account preferences. Device paths, system permissions, autostart and
local-agent grants stay outside the replicated allowlist.
`account_documents/controls.rs` owns authenticated private DM control publication,
original-action ordering and sibling projections. `reactions.rs` and `recall.rs`
publish accepted actions through it; generic native document mutations cannot
create control records. Explicit kept-source preparation validates legacy caches.
`account_sync/archive.rs` filters known recalled private bodies/cards and invalidates cached
exports when the control revision changes. Group authority and local deletion
remain with their existing owners.

`channel_custody.rs` owns locally observed exact-event possession and retractions;
its indexed child keeps those exact positive and negative observations in the
leased profile database, with selected-event reads and 32-row keyset migration
pages. It shares the history-source publisher and legacy-writer barrier rather
than retaining the custody journal in memory. Auxiliary source identities 16–18
use a separate registry without rewriting the installed transcript-source schema.
`account_documents/custody.rs` owns their account-private versioned publication
and sibling projection. It reuses certified account sessions and document digests,
without adding a group transport or claiming recipient delivery. Channel authority
determines eligible external member principals. The footer distinguishes missing
status from a known zero count; its status coordinator clears stale projections
only for the messages and runtime lifetime it requested.
The document store keeps a separate bounded custody-key quota and an owned-file
scan budget consistent with legal document counts. `media_store.rs` prunes the
enumerated unreferenced regular files in one pass, preserving live files and
synchronizing the parent directory before successful return.

`account_documents/public_profile.rs` relays original signed contact profiles under
Profile consent; `account_profile_io.rs` retains signature, revision and avatar
projection authority. Per-source document heads preserve each contact's original
profile. Constructor work initializes only the optional reconciliation receipts;
the existing account-sync worker repairs at most sixteen publication heads and
sixteen projection heads per turn. Exact account/device-scoped completion receipts
compare accepted profile change revisions or signed document revision/hash before
loading avatars. Missing or failed receipts remain retryable after restart; an
unchanged warm open does not replay contact document payloads. Canonical profile
admission and its interrupted avatar projection keep their existing owners.
`account_documents/group_activity.rs` owns History-gated source-signed control
observations tied to the selected inventory snapshot. It cannot install membership
or keys. Both reuse the existing document worker and certified sibling sessions.

`account_documents/inventory.rs` owns source-certified descriptive group snapshots,
bounded automatic publication and account-private reference projection. It reuses
the document version/digest owner and private account worker. The group directory
is mandatory account topology; optional history, profile, appearance and contact
data retain their existing policies. A source reads real local group state and
never republishes a borrowed reference as authority. The native channel adapter
may project reference member facts for display under runtime admission; group
authorization, keys and mutations remain exclusively with the existing channel
owners. The frontend distinguishes this read-only reference from a backup archive
and removes its explanation when real validated group state arrives.

`node/account_documents/device_hostname.rs` owns bounded private per-device hostname
publication and certified-roster projection. The desktop runtime bootstrap reads
OS hostnames; admitted sync IPC releases them only for the expected current account.
`PersonalDevices` renders them without changing identity, account nicknames or
presence semantics. Hostnames reuse encrypted account-document persistence and the
existing certified sibling transport; public discovery and profiles never carry
them. See [private account synchronization](network-design-reference.md#g-linking-and-ongoing-account-synchronization).

# Performance requirements

Read this before changing background work, synchronization, storage, caches or UI
state. Mesh Talk should cost little while waiting, load data when needed and stay
bounded as history grows. This guide owns cross-cutting performance requirements;
[module ownership](module-boundaries.md), [network budgets](network-design-reference.md#8-resource-budgets-compatibility-and-performance)
and [reliability rules](ai-coding-reliability.md) own their implementation contracts.

## Budgets and measurement

These are initial project targets, **not industry standards or claims that the
current application meets them**. Establish a production-build baseline on each
supported platform. Reference fixture: 4 logical CPUs, 8 GiB RAM, SSD, 100 contacts,
20 groups and 100,000 stored messages; no pending transfers, calls or animations.
Separate cold start, warm start, catch-up, visible idle and hidden idle. Measure a
quiet five-minute window after warmup; record build, runtime, profile and workload.
Warm startup restarts the process with OS caches retained; cold startup records
its uncached/first-launch conditions. Usable means an actionable list or
conversation, not a blank shell; report human authorization waits separately.
The empty-shell comparison keeps the same backend, runtime, process membership
and window settings, with user payloads absent.

| Resource                | Initial target for the reference fixture                                                                                                                                                            |
| ----------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Idle CPU                | Visible desktop: ≤1% of one logical CPU; hidden desktop: ≤0.25%; headless node: ≤0.5%, averaged over the window.                                                                                    |
| Retained memory         | Headless node: ≤64 MiB private commit. Desktop: ≤64 MiB workload delta above the same-build empty shell; establish a reviewed whole-family ceiling from that baseline.                              |
| Memory growth           | Repeated navigation/media cycles reach a bounded plateau. Tenfold stored history must not require tenfold startup reads or retained UI payloads.                                                    |
| Idle writes             | Zero business-data commits for unchanged inputs. Target ≤5 MiB/hour OS-observed attributable storage writes per application family after warmup; measure the full hour before claiming this target. |
| Background wakeups      | No application maintenance timer without pending work, a real deadline or a documented recovery purpose. Noncritical recovery defaults to ≥5 minutes and coalesces activation.                      |
| Startup and interaction | First usable shell ≤1 s warm / ≤3 s cold; ordinary interaction must not run blocking I/O, crypto or an unbounded traversal on the UI thread. Report hydration/catch-up separately.                  |

CPU means `100 × process CPU seconds / wall seconds`, summed over the full app
family; divide by logical CPU count only when reporting whole-machine percent.
Report Rust host **and** renderer/GPU/helpers. Distinguish private commit, private
resident memory, shared pages and live JS heap; on Linux use PSS for shared-page
attribution. Logical I/O includes IPC/network activity and is not physical disk
I/O; OS disk events also do not measure physical NAND write amplification. CPU alone does not establish battery/power efficiency: inspect wakeups, GPU,
network and actual energy where supported. Keep metrics collected in different
windows separate. Store measurements in PR/CI artifacts, not this guide.

An existing target miss requires recorded baseline and an owned follow-up; it is
not permission to worsen the path or silently raise its budget. A target change
requires comparable evidence and review. Migrations, catch-up and active media have
separate bounded work budgets and progress evidence, not an unlimited exception.

## Apply to every feature

Before implementation, identify the owning producer, its meaningful trigger,
bounded work unit, retained resources and stop condition. Review all three phases,
including costs introduced in another process or on another device:

| Phase           | Required design and evidence                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| --------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Startup         | Load indexed summaries and the active conversation's bounded page first. Defer inactive history, attachment bytes and optional features until demanded. Avoid decrypting all history, rebuilding unchanged indexes or republishing unchanged state at each login. Measure time to usable UI, peak memory, bytes read and writes separately from catch-up; migrations need resumable bounded progress.                    |
| Idle            | With unchanged inputs, settle business producers and avoid business-data writes. Use scoped events and exact next deadlines; coalesce noncritical repair into the existing serial queue, normally at least five minutes apart. A heartbeat, read, empty reply or offline device must not restart historical work. Verify visible and hidden states, including renderer/helpers and remote work triggered by this client. |
| Active business | Bound each query, decrypt, decode, transfer and rendering turn by items and bytes. Drain real available work promptly with backpressure and cancellation; user interaction and reception must remain responsive. Measure latency, peak CPU/memory and I/O for send/receive, catch-up, search, media and navigation as applicable, then prove resources settle when work finishes.                                        |

workload. Distinguish actionable progress from blocked work, record its outcome
and retain a bounded retry deadline. Successful reads, metadata comparisons and
already-held custody are not new user data. Serializing unnecessary work or
lengthening a timer alone does not establish that its cost is justified.

For every affected phase, the PR must state the trigger and stop condition,
resource bound, selected regression and measured result or explicit evidence gap.

snapshot. Existing misses remain explicit follow-ups with an owning module and
reproduction; never describe a passing correctness test as performance acceptance.
